117-hr-3992.one_liner: Stop employers from treating job applicants differently based on their age
provisions: Employers cannot stop someone from applying for a job because of their age.
Employers cannot put job applicants into separate groups based on their age.
Employers cannot label or rank job applicants differently because of their age.

117-hr-4032.one_liner: Have a federal agency teach small phone companies about open network technology
provisions: The National Telecommunications and Information Administration must reach out to small phone and internet companies to tell them about Open RAN networks.
Open RAN networks are wireless systems that use shared, open technology standards instead of equipment that only works with one company's products.
The agency must offer technical help to small companies that want to learn more about or use this type of network.

117-hr-4028.one_liner: Require a government report on U.S. technology supply chain risks and trusted vendors
provisions: Tells the National Telecommunications and Information Administration to write a report on where U.S. tech companies get their equipment and software
The report must list which technologies are most important for the U.S. economy
The report must measure how much U.S. internet and phone companies depend on technology from companies that are not considered trusted
The report must identify what the federal government needs to do and spend to support trusted tech companies
After the report, the agency must create a plan to help trusted tech vendors compete and reduce reliance on untrusted ones

117-hr-4.one_liner: Require states with voting violations to get federal approval before changing voting rules
provisions: States with 15 or more voting rights violations in the past 25 years must get approval from the Justice Department before changing any voting rule — and that requirement lasts 10 years.
States with 10 or more violations in the past 25 years, where at least one was committed by the state itself, must also get federal approval before changing voting rules.
States that run their own elections and had 3 or more violations in the past 25 years must get federal approval before changing voting rules.
Cities and counties with 3 or more voting rights violations in the past 25 years must get federal approval before changing their local voting rules, for 10 years.
States and local areas must tell the public when they change how voting works.
The Justice Department can require states to hand over documents or answer questions about their voting rules.
When courts hear cases about voting rules, judges must consider whether a state has a history of treating voters differently based on race.

117-hr-4067.one_liner: Give legal backing to an FCC advisory council on communications network safety
provisions: Creates a law that officially sets up a council to advise the FCC on how to keep phone and internet networks safe and working
The council gives recommendations on how to improve the security and reliability of communications networks across the country
Before this bill, the council existed without a law behind it — this bill makes it official

117-hr-4055.one_liner: Require the federal government to run a public cybersecurity education campaign
provisions: A federal office called the NTIA must create a campaign to teach Americans about staying safer online.
The campaign covers best practices — steps people can take every day to lower the chance of getting hacked or having their data stolen.
The NTIA must both build the campaign and run it so that it reaches real people.
The campaign teaches cybersecurity literacy — knowing how online threats work and what to do about them, not just knowing they exist.

117-hr-4045.one_liner: Create a federal task force to study and report on 6G wireless technology
provisions: Sets up a new group called the 6G Task Force inside the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which is the government agency that oversees phone and internet networks.
The task force will look at where 6G wireless technology stands today and what standards are being developed for it.
It will also look at possible uses for 6G technology once it is built.
The task force will include people from phone and internet companies, universities and public interest groups, and federal, state, local, and tribal governments.
The task force will produce a report with its findings.

117-hr-4089.one_liner: Require car rental companies to report suspicious behavior to police
provisions: The Department of Homeland Security must create a list of warning signs for car rental employees to watch for when customers rent or buy vehicles.
Car rental companies and dealers would use these guidelines to decide when to call law enforcement about a customer.
The guidelines would be shared with rental companies and dealers across the country.

117-hr-4111.one_liner: Push for better rules to help poorer countries review their debt contracts
provisions: Tells the U.S. Treasury to have its representative at the International Monetary Fund push for global standards on how countries write debt contracts with private lenders.
Calls for the IMF to offer help to lower-middle-income countries so they can better understand the legal and money terms in their debt deals.
The goal is to give those countries the tools to review and compare loan contracts before signing them.

117-hr-4300.one_liner: Give free national park passes to veterans, active military, and Gold Star Families
provisions: Active military members, veterans, and Gold Star Families get a free America the Beautiful pass, which normally costs $80 per year.
The free pass covers entry fees and standard fees at all federal parks and recreation areas across the country.
Gold Star Families are families of U.S. service members who died while serving.

117-hr-4250.one_liner: Expand State Department rewards for tips about war crimes suspects
provisions: The State Department pays rewards for tips that lead to the arrest, trial, or transfer of a foreign national.
That person must be accused of war crimes, crimes against humanity, or genocide.
Before this bill, the crime had to match the definition used by the specific international court handling the case.
This bill also counts crimes defined under U.S. law or the laws of the country where the crime happened.

117-hr-4233.one_liner: Give veterans using education benefits access to VA counseling
provisions: Veterans who use VA or military education benefits can get counseling through the VA.
This includes counseling at Vet Centers, which are VA community offices that offer mental health support.
Active-duty service members using these education benefits are also covered.
The VA is required to offer this counseling — not just allowed to.

117-hr-4256.one_liner: Raise the cap on bank investments in small business funds from 5% to 15%
provisions: This bill raises the amount banks can put into small business investment funds from 5% of their capital to 15%.
A federal banking regulator must approve the investment before a bank can move forward.
Banks can also invest in a company whose only purpose is to put money into these small business funds.

117-hr-4352.one_liner: Let the federal government take land into trust for all federally recognized tribes
provisions: The federal government can place land into federal trust for all 574 federally recognized tribes.
Land held in federal trust is protected from state taxes and some state laws.
Before this bill, a 2009 Supreme Court ruling blocked this for tribes recognized after 1934.
This bill overrules that court decision and extends the rule to all tribes.
The changes apply as if they were always part of the original 1934 law.

117-hr-4489.one_liner: Put Forest Service lawsuit and settlement money in interest accounts to fund repairs
provisions: When the federal government collects money from lawsuits or settlements tied to Forest Service activities, that money goes into an account that earns interest.
The interest earned in those accounts pays for cleanup or repair work on national forests.
The money is only invested when it is not needed for immediate use.

117-hr-446.one_liner: Require the FTC to track and share information about scams targeting older adults
provisions: The Federal Trade Commission must publish a report on scams that target older adults.
The report must include recommendations for how to stop those scams.
The FTC must update its website with current information about scams targeting older adults.
The website must list contact information for law enforcement and adult protective services.
The FTC must work with news outlets and law enforcement to spread that information.

117-hr-4369.one_liner: Create federally funded university centers to research faster drug manufacturing
provisions: The FDA picks colleges or universities to become official Centers of Excellence in continuous drug manufacturing.
Each center gets federal grant money to run its research program.
Each center studies new ways to make drugs using continuous manufacturing.
Each center shares what it learns with the FDA.
Continuous manufacturing makes drugs faster than the batch method most factories use today.

117-hr-447.one_liner: Fund and expand job training apprenticeships across the country
provisions: Creates an official office inside the Department of Labor to oversee and run apprenticeship programs nationwide.
Sets quality rules for apprenticeships, including what training must be provided and what agreements employers and workers must sign.
Gives money to groups that want to start or grow apprenticeship programs, including programs for teens and young adults.
Gives money to help more businesses offer apprenticeships to workers.
Sets up state offices to manage local apprenticeship programs and help workers and employers get started.
Links apprenticeship programs with high schools, colleges, and adult education to help workers connect their training with formal schooling.
Works to bring more people from underrepresented groups into apprenticeship programs.

117-hr-4481.one_liner: Require agents who help small businesses get SBA loans to register and pay a fee
provisions: Creates a registration system run by the Small Business Administration for agents who help small businesses apply for government-backed loans.
Agents who connect small businesses with SBA 7(a) loans must sign up in this system each year.
Agents must pay a yearly registration fee to stay in the system.
The SBA can collect data on these agents through the registration system.
The 7(a) loan program gives loans to small businesses that cannot get regular bank loans on normal terms.

117-hr-4555.one_liner: Run a public education campaign to improve oral health knowledge
provisions: The Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA), a federal health agency, must run a public education campaign about oral health.
The campaign must focus on children, pregnant women, and parents.
The campaign must also reach older adults, people with disabilities, and racial and ethnic minorities.

117-hr-4515.one_liner: Help small business owners build cybersecurity plans through trained local advisors
provisions: The Small Business Administration must create a program to certify workers at small business development centers in cybersecurity planning.
Depending on the size of the center, at least 5% or 10% of each center's workers must complete this certification.
Once certified, these workers help small business owners make plans to protect their businesses from cyber threats.
Small business development centers are local offices — there are about 1,000 across the country — that already provide free or low-cost business advice.

117-hr-4611.one_liner: Make software vendors report security weaknesses to the Department of Homeland Security
provisions: Companies selling technology products or services to the Department of Homeland Security must provide a full list of all software components.
Each vendor must certify that their components have no known security weaknesses.
If a vendor finds a security weakness, they must notify DHS about it.
Vendors must also submit a plan to fix any weaknesses they find.
DHS must issue rules covering both new contracts and contracts already in place.

117-hr-4531.one_liner: Require the SBA to report annually on loan agents who help small businesses borrow money
provisions: Requires the Small Business Administration to publish a yearly report on agents who help small businesses apply for government-backed loans.
The report must include how many agents are working with loan applicants and what types of services they provide.
The report must count how many fraudulent loans were made where the borrower used one of these agents.
The report must show how much money in referral fees these agents were paid in total.

117-hr-4502.one_liner: Fund the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education for 2022
provisions: Pays for the Department of Labor for the year starting October 2021, covering job training, workplace safety, and worker pay enforcement.
Pays for the Department of Health and Human Services, including the CDC, the National Institutes of Health, and Medicare and Medicaid programs.
Pays for the Department of Education, covering student financial aid, special education, school improvement, and college programs.
Funds the Social Security Administration, which sends monthly payments to about 70 million retired, disabled, and low-income Americans.
Sets rules for how all of this money can and cannot be spent.

117-hr-485.one_liner: Renew and expand federal child abuse prevention programs through 2027
provisions: Keeps federal child abuse prevention and treatment programs funded through September 2027
Creates national rules for how states track and report child deaths and serious injuries caused by abuse
Builds an online system so states can share child abuse records with each other across state lines
Adds steps for child protective services to follow when a family is dealing with drug or alcohol problems
Calls for a review of racial bias in how child protective services handles cases
Orders a study on unregulated custody transfers — when a parent hands a child to a stranger outside the legal system — and how to stop them

117-hr-4616.one_liner: Set replacement interest rates for contracts still tied to the retired LIBOR benchmark
provisions: LIBOR was an interest rate that banks used to set prices on loans and other money contracts. It stopped being used in 2023.
Many contracts — including some home loans and business deals — were tied to LIBOR and had no backup rate written in.
For those contracts, the Federal Reserve picks a replacement rate to use instead of LIBOR.
The switch to the new rate happens automatically — no one has to go to court or sign new paperwork.
People and companies that switch to the new rate cannot be taken to court just for making that switch.
The switch does not count as selling or trading property, so no extra taxes are owed because of it.

117-hr-4660.one_liner: Rename a federal building and courthouse in Wheeling, West Virginia
provisions: Changes the official name of the federal building and courthouse at 1125 Chapline Street in Wheeling, West Virginia.
The building will be called the Frederick P. Stamp, Jr. Federal Building and United States Courthouse.
The building serves as both a federal office building and a U.S. courthouse.

117-hr-4679.one_liner: Name a federal building in Washington DC after Norman Yoshio Mineta
provisions: The federal building at 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE in Washington, DC will be officially called the Norman Yoshio Mineta Federal Building.
Norman Mineta served as U.S. Secretary of Transportation from 2001 to 2006 — the cabinet department whose main office is at that address.
He also served more than 20 years as a U.S. Representative from California, representing the San José area.
Mineta served in the U.S. Army as a first lieutenant after being held in a Japanese American internment camp during World War II.
The name change is official but does not change how the building is used or how it is funded.

117-hr-4686.one_liner: Freeze the assets and block the US entry of Cambodian officials who hurt democracy
provisions: Freezes the US bank accounts and property of senior Cambodian government, military, or security officials who took actions to undermine elections or violated human rights
Blocks those same officials from entering the United States
Covers companies owned or controlled by those officials
Does not apply to goods imported from Cambodia — trade continues as normal
The President can cancel sanctions for a specific person if doing so is in the US national interest
The President can pause all sanctions if Cambodia takes real steps to stop actions against democracy or human rights

117-hr-4981.one_liner: Give a government opioid commission more time to finish its report
provisions: A government commission studying how synthetic opioids enter the U.S. now has 390 days to finish its report, instead of the original 270 days.
That adds about 4 extra months to the deadline.
The commission's job is to study the problem and suggest ways to stop synthetic opioids like fentanyl from coming into the country.

117-hr-4881.one_liner: Put land already owned by the Pascua Yaqui Tribe into federal trust and allow gaming
provisions: The federal government will hold land in Pima County, Arizona in trust for the Pascua Yaqui Tribe of Arizona.
The land is already owned by the Tribe — this bill changes its legal status to federal trust, which gives it added protections.
Once in trust, the land becomes part of the Pascua Yaqui Reservation.
The Tribe can run casino gaming on this land.

117-hr-5.one_liner: Ban discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity in housing, jobs, and public places
provisions: Federal law would ban discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation, and gender identity in hiring, housing, schools, lending, and most businesses.
Stores, restaurants, gyms, and other businesses could not turn away customers based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
People could not be denied access to restrooms, locker rooms, or dressing rooms that match their gender identity.
The Department of Justice could step into federal court cases to support people who face discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
The law would apply to more types of businesses than current civil rights law, including places that offer entertainment, transportation, or recreational activities.

117-hr-4996.one_liner: Add new rules for shipping companies operating in U.S. waters
provisions: Stops shipping companies from punishing customers who use a different carrier or file a complaint against them
Requires the Federal Maritime Commission to post a public list of shipping companies that lied on paperwork or were fined
Forces shipping companies to meet basic service standards set by the government
Stops shipping companies from charging unfair fees when cargo sits waiting at ports
Requires shipping companies to report to the government each quarter on how much cargo they moved in and out of U.S. ports
Gives the Federal Maritime Commission the power to investigate and fine shipping companies for unfair charges

117-hr-51.one_liner: Make Washington D.C. the 51st state of the United States
provisions: Washington D.C. would become the 51st state, called Washington, Douglass Commonwealth.
DC residents would gain two U.S. Senators and one member of the House of Representatives.
The White House, the Capitol, and the Supreme Court stay under federal control.
Those buildings and nearby federal land are not part of the new state.
A new commission would help manage the switch from DC government to state government.
Current DC laws stay in effect until the new state is ready to take over.

117-hr-5323.one_liner: Send $1 billion to Israel to restock its Iron Dome missile defense system
provisions: Sends $1 billion to Israel's government to buy more Iron Dome interceptor missiles and equipment
The Iron Dome is a system that shoots down short-range rockets fired at Israel
The money comes from the U.S. Department of Defense budget

117-hr-5293.one_liner: Extend several VA programs that were set to expire
provisions: Makes the VA dental insurance plan for veterans and some of their family members permanent — it no longer needs to be renewed
Extends through September 2022 a program that pays for travel costs when veterans go to a Vet Center for care
Lets the VA accept donations of land or buildings from state or local governments through December 16, 2026

117-hr-5119.one_liner: Give tribal governments more time to spend COVID relief money
provisions: The Coronavirus Relief Fund gave tribal governments money to cover costs from the COVID-19 pandemic.
The old deadline to spend that money was December 31, 2021; this bill moves the deadline to December 30, 2022.
Tribal governments can use the money for costs like public health services, emergency response, and other needs tied to the pandemic.
This bill applies only to tribal governments — not to states or cities.

117-hr-5221.one_liner: Require more federal health agencies to meet with urban Native American groups
provisions: Right now, only the Indian Health Service must meet with groups that represent Native Americans living in cities.
This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to make sure IHS and other HHS offices meet with those groups.
These meetings must cover health care rules under the Indian Health Care Improvement Act and other federal health laws.

117-hr-5290.one_liner: Keep the government's livestock price reporting program running through 2022
provisions: Keeps a USDA program running that requires meat companies to report the prices they pay for cattle, hogs, and other livestock
The program was set to expire and this bill lets it continue through the year ending September 2022

117-hr-550.one_liner: Fund states to upgrade vaccine record systems and set new data standards
provisions: The Department of Health and Human Services must create a plan to improve the databases that track who has gotten which vaccines.
HHS must set rules for what technology and data formats these tracking systems must use.
HHS gives money to state and local health departments to upgrade their vaccine record systems.
Health departments that receive the money must use the data formats HHS requires.
HHS must send a report to Congress on what it has done.

117-hr-5487.one_liner: Fund programs to collect data and spread awareness about stillbirths
provisions: Lets the Department of Health and Human Services give money to states and organizations to track and collect data on stillbirths.
Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to create guidelines for health departments on how to collect stillbirth data.
Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to create educational materials about stillbirths and make them free to the public.
Creates a training program for doctors who do after-birth examinations on stillborn babies.
Requires the Surgeon General to publish a report with guidelines about stillbirths and what raises the risk of one.

117-hr-5551.one_liner: Keep CDC programs running that study and prevent birth defects in children
provisions: Keeps the CDC's National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities funded through the year starting October 2025.
The center runs programs for babies born with birth defects, children with developmental disabilities, and people with blood disorders.
Keeps a CDC program running that studies how folic acid helps prevent birth defects and spreads information about it.

117-hr-546.one_liner: Stop the Justice Department from reading messages between prisoners and their lawyers
provisions: The Justice Department cannot read private electronic messages between a person in prison and their lawyer.
This covers emails and other digital messages that are protected by attorney-client privilege.
Attorney-client privilege means a person has the right to speak privately with their lawyer without the government listening.

117-hr-5434.one_liner: Keep federal road, transit, and safety funding running through October 2021
provisions: Keeps road, bus, and safety program funding at 2021 levels through October 31, 2021
Raises the spending cap for large freight and highway projects from $600 million to $700 million
Extends research into technology that stops drunk drivers from starting their cars through 2022
Keeps loan programs running for fixing up railroads near train stations through October 31, 2021
Extends funding for the Appalachian Regional Commission, a federal agency that helps rural communities in 13 states, through 2022
Guarantees federal workers get paid as soon as possible if the government runs out of approved spending authority and they are sent home or made to work without pay
Keeps two trust funds for boating safety and cleaning up underground gas tank leaks running through November 1, 2021

117-hr-5561.one_liner: Keep funding hearing screening and early care programs for newborns and young children
provisions: Keeps money flowing to federal programs that test newborns' hearing in hospitals
Funds services that help families get early care when a baby is found to be deaf or hard of hearing
Extends this funding through the year starting October 2025
Supports three federal agencies — HRSA, CDC, and NIDCD — in running these programs

117-hr-5574.one_liner: Require TSA to make airport signs and materials easier to understand for all travelers
provisions: The TSA must create a plan to make materials at major airports easier to read and understand.
The plan must cover people who speak languages other than English.
The plan must also cover people who are blind, have low vision, or are deaf or hard of hearing.

117-hr-5608.one_liner: Create a USDA program to study and manage a disease killing deer, elk, and moose
provisions: Creates a program inside the USDA to research and manage Chronic Wasting Disease, which is a deadly brain disease spreading through deer, elk, and moose herds across the country.
The USDA works with state and tribal wildlife agencies, universities, and research centers to study how the disease spreads, how animals resist it, and how to detect it.
The USDA works with state and tribal agencies to build and carry out plans to control the disease in their local animal populations.
The USDA creates materials to teach the public about the disease and how to help stop it from spreading.
The USDA asks the public for ideas on how to improve the rules for certifying that deer herds are free of the disease.

117-hr-5609.one_liner: Create a public database of contracts between cattle buyers and ranchers
provisions: The USDA must build and keep a public list of every type of contract that large meat-buying companies offer to cattle ranchers.
The list must include any bonus or penalty payment schedules tied to those contracts.
The USDA must publish updates to the list every week or every month, depending on the type of contract.
Meat-buying companies that refuse to share accurate contract information with the USDA can be fined or penalized.
The government must give grants to universities and research stations to teach ranchers how to use the contract and market information.

117-hr-567.one_liner: Give legal backing to a U.S. counterterrorism program in Africa that has run since 2005
provisions: Turns the Trans-Sahara Counterterrorism Partnership Program into an official program backed by law — it has operated since 2005 without one
The State Department runs the program, working with the Defense Department and USAID
The program works with countries in North and West Africa on fighting terrorism — including training their militaries, securing borders, and pushing back on terrorist messaging online and in media
The State Department must write a 5-year plan covering what the program will do in both the Sahel and Maghreb regions of Africa
The State Department must tell Congress before spending money on the program
The State Department must send Congress a yearly report on what the program did

117-hr-5720.one_liner: Require federal judges to report stock trades and post their financial disclosures online
provisions: Federal judges must file a report within 45 days of buying, selling, or trading stocks, bonds, or other investments worth more than $1,000.
The U.S. Courts office must build a public website where people can search, sort, and download these financial reports.
Reports must be posted online within 90 days of when they are due.
If a judge's personal safety could be at risk from sharing certain information, that information can be kept private.

117-hr-654.one_liner: Let some anti-drug community groups skip a funding match requirement
provisions: Groups that get federal money to reduce drug use among kids normally have to raise matching funds from their community.
This bill lets the program skip that matching requirement for groups that cannot raise those funds because of COVID-19.
The program must confirm a group truly cannot raise the money before waiving the requirement.

117-hr-8.one_liner: Require background checks for all private gun transfers between individuals
provisions: Right now, background checks are only required when buying a gun from a licensed store. This bill adds the same requirement to private transfers between individuals.
To transfer a gun privately, the person giving the gun must first bring it to a licensed gun dealer, who runs a background check on the person receiving it.
Some transfers are exempt — for example, a gun given as a gift between spouses.

117-hr-5763.one_liner: Keep federal road, transit, rail, and safety programs funded through December 2021
provisions: Keeps federal funding for road, transit, rail, and highway safety programs at their 2021 levels through December 3, 2021.
Lets the Highway Trust Fund, Sport Fish and Boating Trust Fund, and Leaking Underground Storage Tank Trust Fund keep spending money through December 4, 2021.

117-hr-6.one_liner: Give green cards to non-citizens who came to the US as children
provisions: Non-citizens who entered the US as children and have lived here since January 1, 2021 can apply for a 10-year green card.
To qualify, they must pass a background check and be in school or have completed a school program.
Children of certain visa holders — such as people on work visas — can also qualify.
People with TPS (a program that pauses deportation during foreign crises) or DED (a program that delays deportation for certain groups) can apply for a full permanent green card within 3 years.
After 10 years, people who got a green card under this bill can make it permanent by finishing school, joining the military, or holding a job.
Information from these applications cannot be used to find or deport people.
States can offer in-state college tuition to undocumented students without having to offer that same discount to all U.S. citizens.

117-hr-983.one_liner: Make it a federal crime to steal veterans' benefits
provisions: Creates a new federal crime for running a scam to steal someone's veterans' benefits.
Anyone caught doing this can go to prison for up to five years, pay a fine, or both.
The law covers both completing the scam and trying to do it.

117-hr-941.one_liner: Renew federal funding for bone marrow and cord blood transplant programs through 2026
provisions: Keeps a federal program running that helps patients find donors for bone marrow and umbilical cord blood transplants.
The program is funded through the end of the government's budget year in 2026.
Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to review research on treatments using adult stem cells and tissue from births.
Requires a government watchdog office to write a report on how many workers are trained in regenerative medicine.

117-hr-803.one_liner: Set aside lands in Colorado as protected wilderness areas
provisions: Turns certain federal lands in Colorado into protected wilderness areas, which means no roads, buildings, or motorized vehicles are allowed there
Adds some of those lands to the existing West Elk Wilderness area
Keeps allowing competitive running races that are already permitted in the Redcloud Peak and Handies Peak areas
Lets the Colorado Army National Guard continue flying training missions over the new wilderness areas
Creates two new wilderness areas — Pisgah East and Pisgah West — once any current uses that are not allowed in wilderness stop
Secures federal water rights for some of the new wilderness areas
Requires the Defense Department to study how expanding wilderness areas across the Western U.S. affects military flight training

117-hr-842.one_liner: Expand union and worker protections under federal labor law
provisions: More workers — including some contractors and people previously counted as supervisors — would get the same union protections as other employees.
Workers can join strikes started by workers at a different company, and their union cannot be sued for supporting that strike.
Union contracts can require all workers covered by the contract to pay union fees, even in states that currently have laws blocking this.
Employers cannot fire or penalize workers for going on strike, or permanently replace them with other workers.
Employers cannot require workers to attend meetings designed to talk them out of joining a union.
Employers cannot make workers sign papers giving up their right to join a class-action lawsuit.
Companies that break these rules can face fines and court orders from the National Labor Relations Board.

117-hr-826.one_liner: Require reports to Congress on reuniting Korean Americans with family in North Korea
provisions: The State Department must report to Congress on talks with South Korea about reuniting Korean Americans with family in North Korea.
A special government official focused on North Korean human rights must also report to Congress.
That official's reports cover conversations held with Korean Americans who have family in North Korea.
Both sets of reports must happen more than once — not just a single time.

117-hres-134.one_liner: Condemn the 2021 military takeover in Burma and call for release of detained leaders
provisions: Says the U.S. opposes the military takeover that happened in Burma on February 1, 2021
Calls on Burma's military to free everyone who was arrested during the takeover
Calls on Burma's military to restore phone and internet access that was shut down
Calls on Burma's military to give power back to the elected civilian government

117-hres-1.one_liner: Let the Speaker swear in all newly elected members of Congress
provisions: The Speaker of the House gives the oath of office to all newly elected members of Congress.
Every newly elected member must take the oath before they can vote or do any official work.
This happens at the start of every new Congress, usually in early January.
This is a standard step to open a new Congress, not a change in law.

117-hres-147.one_liner: Set the rules for debating two bills in the House
provisions: Sets the time limit and debate rules for a bill that would protect certain lands in Colorado as wilderness
Sets the time limit and debate rules for a bill that would ban discrimination based on sex, gender identity, and sexual orientation
This is a procedural step — it does not pass either bill, it just controls how the House will discuss them

117-hres-130.one_liner: Formally condemn China and Hong Kong for breaking rights promised to Hong Kong people
provisions: When Britain gave Hong Kong to China in 1997, China promised Hong Kong could keep its own laws and freedoms until at least 2047.
Starting in 2020, China and Hong Kong passed national security laws that limit what people in Hong Kong can say, protest, and do.
Under these laws, people can be arrested for things that were allowed before 2020.
Congress says these laws break the promises China made to Hong Kong's people and to the world.
This resolution is a formal statement — it does not create new US laws or change any rules.

117-hres-101.one_liner: Set the federal government's spending and budget plan through 2030
provisions: Sets a budget for the federal government for the year starting October 2020.
Outlines spending and revenue targets for each year from 2022 through 2030.
Includes instructions for lawmakers to pass separate bills that could add to the national deficit.

117-hres-188.one_liner: Set the rules for debating three bills on workers and gun checks
provisions: Sets the time and debate rules for voting on a bill that changes how unions and workers can organize
Sets the rules for voting on a bill that requires a background check for every gun sale, including private sales
Sets the rules for voting on a bill that closes a gap that lets gun sales go through before a background check is finished

117-hres-179.one_liner: Set debate rules for two bills on voting access and police reform
provisions: This bill sets the rules for how the House will debate H.R. 1.
H.R. 1 covers changing voting rules, limiting campaign money, and adding ethics rules for government workers.
This bill also sets the rules for how the House will debate H.R. 1280.
H.R. 1280 covers holding police accountable in court and collecting data on officer misconduct.
Passing this bill does not make either H.R. 1 or H.R. 1280 law — it only decides how each bill gets debated.

117-hres-198.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress will vote on a budget bill
provisions: Sets the time limit and debate rules for the House to vote on a budget bill that came back from the Senate
Decides how long members of Congress can speak before the vote happens
Controls what changes or additions can be made to the bill before the final vote

117-hres-21.one_liner: Call on the Vice President to declare the President unable to serve using the 25th Amendment
provisions: Calls on Vice President Mike Pence to use Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, a part of the Constitution that lets the Vice President and Cabinet declare the President unable to do his job.
Calls on Pence to gather the heads of the Cabinet departments to vote on whether the President can carry out his duties.
If that group agrees, Pence would take over and act as President.
Requires Pence to send written notice to the top leader of the Senate and the Speaker of the House that he is taking over as Acting President.

117-hres-166.one_liner: Set the rules for how the House debates and votes on H.R. 1319
provisions: This bill sets the rules for how the House of Representatives will debate H.R. 1319.
It controls how long lawmakers can speak and whether they can offer changes to the bill during debate.
It is a procedural step — it does not create or change any policy on its own.

117-hres-243.one_liner: Remove Representative Eric Swalwell from the House Intelligence Committee
provisions: Removes Representative Eric Swalwell from the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.
The House Intelligence Committee oversees U.S. spy agencies and gets access to classified national security information.
This is a House-only resolution — it does not go to the Senate or need the President's signature to take effect.

117-hres-303.one_liner: Set the rules for debating equal pay and workplace violence bills
provisions: Sets the time limits and voting rules for debating a bill that would change how workers can sue over unequal pay based on sex
Sets the time limits and voting rules for debating a bill that would require health care employers to make plans to stop workplace violence

117-hres-275.one_liner: Condemn the 2021 Atlanta shootings and violence against Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders
provisions: The House says the March 16, 2021 shootings in Atlanta, Georgia were wrong and should not have happened.
Eight people were killed in those shootings.
The House says it will keep working against hate and violence toward Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders.
This resolution does not create any new laws or change any existing rules.

117-hres-233.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress debates five separate bills
provisions: Decides how long Congress can debate a bill to renew protections for victims of domestic violence
Decides how long Congress can debate a bill on letting certain non-citizens stay in the country legally
Decides how long Congress can debate a bill on visas for farm workers
Decides how long Congress can debate a bill on stopping automatic cuts to government spending
Decides how long Congress can debate a proposal to remove the deadline for adding an equal rights amendment to the Constitution

117-hres-317.one_liner: Condemn China's treatment of Uyghurs and call on the President to act
provisions: States that China's government is responsible for ongoing abuses against Uyghurs and other minority groups
Calls these abuses genocide and crimes against humanity
Calls on the President to take steps to stop these actions

117-hres-380.one_liner: Set the rules for debating two bills on debt collection and pregnancy workplace rights
provisions: Sets the time limits and debate rules for the House to vote on a bill about debt collection
Sets the time limits and debate rules for the House to vote on a bill about workplace rights for pregnant workers
This is a procedural step — it does not change any laws on its own

117-hres-331.one_liner: Formally censure a House member for public statements about a court trial
provisions: Censures Representative Maxine Waters, which is an official formal rebuke by the House of Representatives
The censure is tied to statements Waters made about the trial of Derek Chauvin, a former police officer
A censure does not remove a member from office but puts an official mark of disapproval on record

117-hres-403.one_liner: Let the House vote on rare disease drug rules and condemn the Atlanta shootings
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House will debate and vote on two separate bills
One bill changes how long a drug company can be the only seller of a drug made for rare diseases
The other bill is a formal statement from the House condemning the March 16, 2021 shootings in Atlanta that killed 8 people
The condemnation statement says the House stands against hate and violence targeting Asian American and Pacific Islander people

117-hres-330.one_liner: Set the House debate rules for three bills on D.C. statehood and immigration
provisions: Sets the terms for how the full House will debate a bill that would make Washington D.C. the 51st state
Sets the terms for how the full House will debate a bill about legal rights for people held at border checkpoints or inside immigration detention centers
Sets the terms for how the full House will debate a bill that would move the power to ban groups of non-citizens from entering the country from the president to Congress
This bill does not change any law itself — it only controls how and when the House can vote on these three other bills

117-hres-38.one_liner: Allow the House to vote on asking the VP to take over as acting President
provisions: This resolution sets the debate rules for H. Res. 21 in the House.
H. Res. 21 would ask Vice President Pence to use Section 4 of the 25th Amendment.
Under Section 4, the VP can temporarily act as President if the Cabinet says the President cannot serve.
The President keeps the title and can contest the declaration.
The resolution also lets the House fine any member who does not wear a mask on the floor.
The mask rule was announced on January 4, 2021 during a public health emergency.

117-hres-479.one_liner: Set debate rules for a House vote on making Juneteenth a federal holiday
provisions: This resolution sets the rules for how the House of Representatives will debate S. 475.
S. 475 is a bill that would make Juneteenth National Independence Day a legal federal holiday.
The resolution controls how long members can speak on the bill and what changes can be offered during debate.

117-hres-41.one_liner: Set the debate rules for a House vote on impeaching President Trump
provisions: Gives the House a set amount of time to debate whether to impeach President Trump
Controls how much time each side gets to speak during the debate
Limits what changes can be made to the resolution before the House votes on it

117-hres-409.one_liner: Set the rules for debating two bills in the House
provisions: Set time limits and voting rules for debating a bill to create a commission to investigate the January 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol
Set time limits and voting rules for debating a bill to send emergency money to cover government costs through September 30, 2021
Decided which changes to those bills could be voted on during debate

117-hres-473.one_liner: Let the House vote on repealing the Iraq war law and new company rules
provisions: Lets the House vote on repealing the 2002 law that gave the president approval to send troops to Iraq.
Limits debate time on the Iraq war law vote to one hour, split equally between supporters and opponents.
Lets the House vote on requiring public companies to disclose more information and creating a new government committee on sustainable finance.
This bill only sets the rules for how those two votes happen — it does not repeal the Iraq war law or create the committee itself.

117-hres-414.one_liner: Update mask rules in the House to match CDC guidance for vaccinated members
provisions: Tells the House doctor's office to update its mask rules for the House floor and committee rooms
The new rules would apply to members and staff who are vaccinated against COVID-19
The update must match CDC guidance from May 13, 2021, which said vaccinated people can go without masks in most indoor settings

117-hres-508.one_liner: Set the House debate rules for voting on the roads and transit funding bill
provisions: This bill sets the rules for how the House of Representatives debates and votes on H.R. 3684, the highways and transit funding bill.
It controls things like how long members can speak and what changes can be offered during the debate.
It does not itself spend money or change any laws — it only controls the process for considering H.R. 3684.

117-hres-503.one_liner: Create a House committee to investigate the January 6th attack on the Capitol
provisions: Creates a 13-member House committee to look into the January 6th, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol.
The committee can hold hearings, collect evidence, and issue subpoenas — legal orders to get documents and testimony from people.
Other House committees must hand over any related records within 14 days.
The committee must suggest ways to prevent future attacks, domestic terrorism, and politically motivated violence.
The committee will write a report with findings and steps to improve security at the Capitol and other government buildings.

117-hres-504.one_liner: Set rules for debating four separate bills in the House
provisions: Sets the time limit and debate rules for four different bills before the full House votes on them
One bill changes how inspectors general — government watchdogs — can be fired or removed
One bill replaces a statue of a judge who ruled against Black Americans with one of the first Black Supreme Court Justice, Thurgood Marshall
One bill provides money for highways, road safety, and public transportation
One bill creates a committee to investigate the January 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol

117-hres-535.one_liner: Set House debate rules for three bills on chemicals, the FTC, and Afghan visas
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House will debate and vote on three separate bills.
One bill would require the EPA to label certain man-made chemicals called PFAS as hazardous waste, making companies legally responsible for cleaning them up.
Another bill would confirm that the FTC can go to court to stop companies from breaking consumer protection laws.
A third bill would speed up the visa application process for Afghans who helped the U.S. military or government.
This bill itself does not change any laws — it only sets the debate rules so Congress can vote on the three bills above.

117-hres-486.one_liner: Set the House debate rules for voting on six pending bills
provisions: Allows the House to vote on a bill that changes how workers prove age discrimination against the federal government in court.
Allows the House to vote on a bill that would lower the cost of birth control for veterans who get it through VA hospitals.
Allows the House to vote on a bill that would require banks to track and report loan data for small businesses owned by LGBTQ people.
Allows the House to vote on canceling an EPA rule that set air pollution limits for oil and gas operations.
Allows the House to vote on canceling a banking rule that determined when a national bank counts as the official lender on a loan.
Sets aside money to pay for the work of a House committee focused on economic differences between groups of Americans.

117-hres-555.one_liner: Set the rules for debating the Labor, Health, and Education spending bill
provisions: Set a time limit and debate rules for the House to vote on a spending bill for the Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education departments
The bill covered government spending for the year ending September 30, 2022
Decided which changes to the spending bill could be offered during the debate

117-hres-554.one_liner: Urge the Speaker to seat five Republicans on the January 6th committee
provisions: Condemns the Speaker of the House for refusing to seat five Republican members on the committee set up to investigate the January 6th attack on the Capitol.
The five members named are Jim Banks of Indiana, Jim Jordan of Ohio, Rodney Davis of Illinois, Kelly Armstrong of North Dakota, and Troy Nehls of Texas.
Calls on the Speaker to appoint all five of them to the committee.

117-hres-567.one_liner: Set the rules for debating three government spending bills in Congress
provisions: Decided how the House of Representatives would debate and vote on three separate spending bills
The first bill covered money for Congress itself for the year ending September 30, 2022
The second bill covered money for the State Department and programs in other countries for the same year
The third bill covered money for the Commerce Department, Justice Department, and science programs for the same year
Set time limits and rules for how long Congress could debate each bill before voting

117-hres-601.one_liner: Set the House floor rules for voting on three separate bills
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House will debate and vote on a bill that changes which states must get federal approval before changing their voting laws
Sets the rules for how the House will debate and vote on a $1.2 trillion infrastructure bill covering roads, bridges, and public transit
Sets the rules for how the House will debate and vote on a budget plan covering 2022 through 2031

117-hres-667.one_liner: Set the rules for debating three bills in the House
provisions: Sets the time limits and debate rules for a vote on a bill about abortion access
Sets the time limits and debate rules for a vote on the 2022 military budget and troop levels
Sets the time limits and debate rules for a vote on a short-term government funding bill to keep the government running through September 30, 2022

117-hres-688.one_liner: Allow the House to vote on a bill about physical activity guidelines for Americans
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House will debate and vote on a separate bill called S. 1301.
The bill being voted on would have the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services publish physical activity guidelines for Americans.
This bill itself does not create any guidelines — it only sets up the process for considering the guidelines bill.

117-hres-716.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress debates four bills on workers and families
provisions: Sets the time and rules for debate on a bill about preventing family violence
Sets the time and rules for debate on a bill about breastfeeding breaks at work
Sets the time and rules for debate on a bill about age discrimination in hiring
Sets the time and rules for debate on a bill about physical activity guidelines from the government

117-hres-730.one_liner: Find Steve Bannon in contempt of Congress for refusing to comply with a committee subpoena
provisions: Finds that Steve Bannon refused to follow a subpoena — a legal order to appear and provide documents.
That subpoena came from the House committee investigating the January 6th attack on the U.S. Capitol.
Tells the Speaker of the House to send this finding to federal prosecutors in Washington, D.C.
Federal prosecutors can then decide whether to bring criminal charges against Bannon.
Tells the Speaker to take any other steps needed to enforce the subpoena.

117-hres-727.one_liner: Set the rules for the House to debate the January 6th contempt report
provisions: Set the rules for how long the House could debate the January 6th Committee report and the contempt vote against Steve Bannon
Let the House vote on whether Steve Bannon should be held in contempt for ignoring a congressional subpoena
A subpoena is an official order requiring someone to hand over documents or appear before Congress
This resolution only set the terms for the debate — it did not make any final decision on the contempt question itself

117-hres-72.one_liner: Remove Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene from two House committees
provisions: Takes Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene off the House Committee on the Budget
Takes Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene off the House Committee on Education and Labor
Only the full House votes on this — it does not go to the Senate or the President

117-hres-789.one_liner: Formally censure a House member for posting a video showing violence against colleagues
provisions: The House formally censures Representative Paul Gosar.
The censure is a response to a video Gosar posted on social media that showed images of violence toward Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and President Biden.
A censure is an official statement of disapproval by the House — it does not remove a member from office or change their pay.
The censured member is required to stand in the well of the House while the resolution is read aloud.

117-hres-760.one_liner: Express U.S. support for Cuban citizens peacefully protesting for freedom
provisions: Congress states it stands with Cuban people who are protesting peacefully.
Congress condemns Cuba's government for arresting peaceful protesters and journalists.
Congress calls on Cuba to stop detaining people who protest peacefully.
Congress calls on Cuba to free all political prisoners.
Congress calls on the U.S. government to take steps to support Cuban people's right to protest.

117-hres-795.one_liner: Set the rules for the House to vote on formally rebuking Representative Paul Gosar
provisions: This bill sets the debate time limits and procedures the House will follow before voting on H. Res. 789.
H. Res. 789 is a censure of Representative Paul Gosar, a House member from Arizona — censure is a formal rebuke recorded in the congressional record.
A censure is an official condemnation by the full House, but it does not remove the member from office or take away their right to vote on legislation.
The bill has no effect outside of Congress — it only controls how this one internal vote will be run.

117-hres-774.one_liner: Set the rules for how the House debates a budget bill
provisions: This resolution controls how the House will debate H.R. 5376, a budget bill Congress is handling through a process called reconciliation.
It sets time limits for debate and controls what changes to the bill members can offer during the floor vote.
This resolution only covers the debate rules for H.R. 5376 in the House — it does not pass the bill or affect how the Senate votes on it.

117-hres-8.one_liner: Set the rules for how the House of Representatives will operate in 2021
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House of Representatives will run during the 117th Congress, which covers 2021 to 2023.
Makes the Office of Diversity and Inclusion a permanent part of the House.
Keeps rules in place requiring the House to protect employees from harassment and discrimination, and adds protections for people who report wrongdoing.
For COVID-19 relief bills, the Budget Committee chair can skip the normal rules for calculating how much a law will cost.
For bills related to climate change, the Budget Committee chair can skip the normal rules for calculating how much a law will cost.
Requires the House Clerk to keep a public list showing which members support bills already passed by the Senate.
Lets investigators demand documents or testimony in a probe into political interference at federal health agencies during the COVID-19 response.

117-hres-85.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress debates an apprenticeship bill and a budget plan
provisions: Sets the time limit and debate rules for a vote on a bill that expands apprenticeship programs across the country
Sets the time limit and debate rules for a vote on the federal budget plan covering 2021 through 2030
Does not change any laws itself — only controls how the House of Representatives runs its debate on these two items

117-hres-838.one_liner: Set the rules for debating three separate bills in the House
provisions: Decides how much time members of Congress get to debate three different bills
One bill would limit presidential power and add rules about elections
One bill would name a memorial in Orlando, Florida after the Pulse nightclub shooting
One bill would address mental health support for doctors and nurses

117-hres-829.one_liner: Set the rules for debating a bill to keep the government funded through 2022
provisions: Set the time limit and debate rules for the House to vote on a bill that kept the government running through September 2022
Controlled which changes to the bill could be voted on during debate

117-hres-803.one_liner: Set the rules for how the House debates the Build Back Better spending bill
provisions: Sets the terms for how the House can debate and vote on H.R. 5376, known as the Build Back Better Act.
Requires a technical fix to the bill to be treated as already approved before debate begins.
This is a procedural step — it does not create or change any policy on its own.

117-hres-837.one_liner: Call on China to release tennis player Peng Shuai and stop hiding her case
provisions: Says the House believes the International Olympic Committee did not protect Peng Shuai's right to speak freely
Calls on China to allow an outside investigation into Peng Shuai's claims that a top Chinese official sexually assaulted her
Calls on China to stop blocking news reports and online discussions about Peng Shuai's case
Calls on China to let Peng Shuai leave the country if she wants to
Calls on China not to punish Peng Shuai's family members who are still in China

117-s-1502.one_liner: Protect what police officers tell peer counselors and set national program standards
provisions: When a law enforcement officer talks to a peer support specialist, those conversations generally cannot be shared with others.
A peer support specialist is a fellow officer trained to provide counseling — the privacy rule covers their side of the conversation too.
The Department of Justice must create best practices and professional standards for how these counseling programs should run.

117-hres-91.one_liner: Set the rules for a House vote on removing a Member from committees
provisions: The House will follow a set of rules when it votes on H. Res. 72
H. Res. 72 is a resolution to remove a specific House Member from certain committees
The rules control how the vote on that resolution will be run on the House floor

117-s-108.one_liner: Let the Seminole Tribe of Florida sell, lease, or transfer land it owns outright
provisions: The Seminole Tribe of Florida can lease, sell, or transfer land it owns directly.
This only applies to land the federal government does not manage on behalf of the tribe.
The tribe can make these property deals without needing extra approval from the federal government.

117-s-1095.one_liner: Cut off GI Bill survivor benefits at colleges that charge out-of-state tuition to veterans' families
provisions: If a public college charges veterans' surviving family members more than in-state tuition rates, the VA stops approving that school for GI Bill survivor benefits.
This applies to family members using the Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance program, which covers children and spouses of veterans who died or were disabled in service.
Schools that want to keep accepting these students' GI Bill benefits must charge them the same tuition rate as in-state students.

117-s-1064.one_liner: Sanction people in Nicaragua blocking elections and report on corruption and human rights abuses
provisions: Adds Nicaragua to a list of countries whose citizens can have their U.S. visas blocked if they interfere with elections or take part in serious corruption.
Requires the U.S. to push international banks and financial groups to add oversight to any loans or aid they give to Nicaragua.
Requires the State Department and Treasury to make a plan to use sanctions — such as freezing money and blocking travel — to pressure Nicaragua toward free and fair elections.
Requires the president to impose targeted sanctions on people found to be blocking free and fair elections in Nicaragua.
Requires a report on corruption by Nicaragua's President Daniel Ortega, his family members, and top government officials.
Requires a report on Russian activity in Nicaragua and on human rights abuses against rural farming communities and native groups.
Requires a plan to support independent news and media in Nicaragua and remove obstacles to people getting outside information.

117-s-189.one_liner: Raise pay for disabled veterans whenever Social Security gets a raise
provisions: When Social Security payments go up to keep pace with rising prices, veterans' disability payments go up by the same percentage
The raise also applies to extra payments veterans get for supporting a spouse or children
The raise includes a clothing allowance paid to veterans with certain service-related disabilities
Surviving spouses and children of veterans who died from service-related causes get the same raise too

117-s-164.one_liner: Require the FDA to teach doctors about biosimilar drugs
provisions: The FDA must create or improve training programs that teach doctors about biological drugs and their lower-cost versions called biosimilars.
Biosimilars are drugs that work the same as a brand-name biological drug but are made by a different company.
The FDA can build a website where doctors and health workers can find information about these drugs.

117-s-1828.one_liner: Pay government workers who suffer brain injuries from hostile acts while on assignment
provisions: Lets CIA officers, diplomats, and other government workers receive payments if they suffer a brain injury while on assignment.
The worker's family members can also receive payments if they are harmed the same way.
The injury must be linked to war, insurgency, hostile acts, terrorism, or another situation designated by the agency.
The injury cannot be the result of the worker's own wrongdoing.
Workers who were injured before this bill passed can still receive payments.
Each agency must send a classified report to Congress listing how many payments were made and how much each one was.
This bill was created after U.S. government workers began reporting a condition called Havana Syndrome starting in 2016.

117-s-1910.one_liner: Approve VA hospital construction and repair projects for 2021
provisions: The Department of Veterans Affairs gets the go-ahead to build or repair specific medical facilities for veterans.
Each project has a set dollar limit so costs cannot go above a fixed amount.
The projects are scheduled for the year starting in October 2020.
Congress sets the spending cap on each project one by one.

117-s-1511.one_liner: Expand death and disability benefits for police, firefighters, and first responders
provisions: Adds traffic-control firefighters and police cadets in training to the program that pays money to public safety workers killed or badly hurt on the job.
Covers officers who respond to emergencies outside their normal work area.
Raises the up-front payment families get while waiting for a final decision on a death claim, and adjusts that amount each year to keep up with rising prices.
Raises the payout on any claim that has been waiting more than 365 days for a final answer.
Adds brain and memory disorders — like dementia — as injuries that qualify for disability payments.
Changes education payments for surviving spouses and children from optional to required.
Lets 9/11 first responders or their surviving family members file death or disability claims in certain situations.
Gives the Department of Justice the power to demand documents from outside groups, like government agencies, to speed up claims processing.

117-s-325.one_liner: Give a federal commission on Native children two more years to finish its report
provisions: A federal commission studying programs for Native children now has 5 years to finish its report, instead of 3 years.
The commission looks at programs run by federal, state, local, and tribal governments that serve Native children.
The final report goes to the President and Congress and includes plans for federal policies on Native children.

117-s-796.one_liner: Require the VA to run a care program for pregnant and postpartum veterans
provisions: The VA must run a program that connects pregnant and postpartum veterans with doctors and care providers outside the VA system.
Doctors and care providers outside the VA get training on the specific health needs of veterans who are pregnant or recently gave birth.
The training includes mental and behavioral health issues that can come from military service.
A government watchdog office must write a report on how many veterans die or get seriously hurt during or after pregnancy.
That report must look at whether Black, Hispanic, and other veterans of different racial and ethnic backgrounds have worse health outcomes.

117-s-475.one_liner: Make June 19 a federal public holiday called Juneteenth National Independence Day
provisions: June 19 becomes a federal public holiday, called Juneteenth National Independence Day.
Federal workers get a paid day off on June 19 each year.
Juneteenth joins the 10 other federal holidays, such as July 4th and Labor Day.
Private employers are not required by this bill to give workers the day off, but many follow federal holiday schedules.

117-s-578.one_liner: Require sesame to be listed as an allergen on food labels
provisions: Makes sesame an official food allergen that must appear on food labels, joining peanuts, milk, eggs, wheat, soy, fish, shellfish, and tree nuts.
Food companies must add sesame to their labels starting January 1, 2023.
Requires the Department of Health and Human Services to report on food allergy research and data collection.
About 1.6 million Americans have sesame allergies — this law gives them the same label warnings already required for the other eight major allergens.

117-s-272.one_liner: Require federal agencies to post their budget requests online for the public
provisions: Each federal agency must put its budget request documents on its own website and on a single searchable government site like USAspending.gov.
The documents must be posted within two weeks of being sent to Congress.
People must be able to download individual reports, all reports at once, or just the results of a search.
The Office of Management and Budget must keep a public webpage listing which agencies submitted budget documents, when they were sent to Congress, and when they were posted online.

118-hr-1797.one_liner: Require safety rules for rechargeable batteries used in electric bikes and scooters
provisions: The Consumer Product Safety Commission must create new safety rules for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries.
The rules apply to batteries used in electric bikes, electric scooters, and similar small electric vehicles.
Single-use batteries are not covered — only rechargeable ones fall under these rules.
The rules must lower the risk of fires caused by these batteries.
The safety rules apply to products sold to regular consumers, not to commercial or industrial equipment.

117-s-957.one_liner: Require VA hospitals to have drop boxes for unused prescription drugs
provisions: Every VA medical facility that has an on-site pharmacy must have a physical drop box where anyone can leave unused prescription drugs
Every VA location that has a dedicated law enforcement space must also have one of these drop boxes
Any person — not just veterans — can use these drop boxes to safely get rid of controlled substance medications

117-s-848.one_liner: Change how federal teaching grants get turned into loans when teachers miss service requirements
provisions: Teachers whose federal teaching grants were turned into loans can ask the Department of Education to review that decision.
The Department of Education can review and reverse a grant being changed to a loan.
Teachers whose required teaching service was disrupted by COVID-19 can get extra flexibility to meet their teaching terms.
The bill updates the process the government uses to check whether teachers have met their required years of service.

118-hr-1767.one_liner: Keep veterans' education benefits when schools are closed by fraud or a VA inspection
provisions: If a VA inspection causes a school to shut down a program, veterans enrolled in that program keep their benefits.
If the Department of Education finds a school harmed student loan borrowers, veterans in that program keep their benefits.
To offer VA-funded programs, schools must agree to repay the VA if they close or cut a program due to fraud.

118-hr-192.one_liner: Stop non-citizens from voting in Washington DC local elections
provisions: Non-citizens cannot vote in any DC election, including local races for mayor, city council, or school board.
DC passed a law in 2022 letting non-citizens vote in local elections if they live in the city and meet certain rules — this bill cancels that law.
Federal law already blocks non-citizens from voting in national elections like presidential or congressional races — this bill extends that block to DC local elections too.

118-hr-2964.one_liner: Require disposable wipes to carry a 'Do Not Flush' label on packaging
provisions: Companies that make or sell disposable wipes must put a 'Do Not Flush' label and symbol on the packaging.
This includes baby wipes, cleaning wipes, and personal care wipes.
The label and symbol must follow specific industry guidelines for how they look.
The Federal Trade Commission — a government agency that enforces consumer rules — will create the rules for how this works.
The FTC can take action against companies that do not follow the labeling rules.

118-hr-3019.one_liner: Create a system to inspect and oversee federal prisons
provisions: The DOJ Inspector General must inspect all federal prisons, with higher-risk prisons checked more often.
Inspections can happen with or without advance notice.
A new official called an Ombudsman is created inside DOJ to receive complaints about federal prisons.
The Ombudsman can look into problems, ask questions, and suggest fixes — or choose not to act on a complaint.
Federal prisons cannot punish anyone for filing a complaint or triggering an inspection.
The Ombudsman must work with prisons to let people inside, their families, and the public know this role exists.

118-hr-3354.one_liner: Name a Virginia post office after former Secretary of State Madeleine Albright
provisions: Renames the post office at 220 North Hatcher Avenue in Purcellville, Virginia as the 'Secretary of State Madeleine Albright Post Office Building'.
Madeleine Albright served as U.S. Secretary of State from 1997 to 2001 and was the first woman to hold that office.
Only the name of the building changes — all mail services, hours, and operations at that post office stay the same.
The new name takes effect when the bill is signed into law.

118-hr-3195.one_liner: Reopen federal land in Minnesota's Superior National Forest to mining
provisions: A 2020 federal order blocked mining on about 225,000 acres of forest land in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties, Minnesota — this bill cancels that order.
Mining companies can apply to operate mines in the Superior National Forest, and the government must finish all required reviews within 18 months of getting a plan.
Mineral leases and permits that were taken back under the 2020 ban are restored to the companies that held them.
Once restored, those leases and permits cannot be challenged in court.

118-hr-2925.one_liner: Let mining companies build roads and structures on public land before finding minerals
provisions: Mining companies can build roads, buildings, and other structures on public land even before they find any minerals there.
Right now, companies must show they found minerals before they can do major construction on public land — this bill removes that requirement.
This applies to land owned by the federal government, which makes up about 28% of all land in the United States.

118-hr-3950.one_liner: Require ticket sellers to show the full price before you pick a seat
provisions: Ticket sellers must show the total price — including all fees — before you choose a ticket, not at the end of checkout.
The full price must also appear in any ad or price listing, not just at the checkout page.
Sellers must list each fee separately, such as service fees, processing fees, delivery fees, and taxes.
If a seller does not actually have the ticket yet, they must tell you that before you pick it.
The Federal Trade Commission enforces these rules.

118-hr-354.one_liner: Let active and retired police officers carry concealed guns in more places across state lines
provisions: Active and retired police officers can carry a hidden gun in school zones, which was not allowed before
Active and retired police officers can carry a hidden gun in national parks
Active and retired police officers can carry a hidden gun in businesses and other places open to the public
Active and retired police officers can carry a hidden gun in certain federal buildings open to the public
States can let retired officers go through gun qualification tests less often than current rules require

118-hr-3738.one_liner: Create a new VA office to run economic and education programs for veterans
provisions: Creates a new office inside the Department of Veterans Affairs to run economic programs for veterans, their families, and survivors.
The new office takes over job training, employment programs, and the program that helps service members move into civilian jobs.
The new office takes over education programs that help veterans pay for school.
The new office takes over the VA's home loan programs and the database that tracks small businesses owned by veterans.
Before programs move to the new office, the VA must confirm the move will not disrupt services to veterans.
Sets a cap on how many full-time workers the new office can hire in 2024 and 2025.
Sets a matching cap for the Veterans Benefits Administration.

118-hr-3397.one_liner: Block a Bureau of Land Management conservation rule from taking effect
provisions: Requires the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to pull back its proposed conservation rule.
Stops BLM from finishing, putting in place, or enforcing that rule.
Blocks BLM from making final or putting in place any future rule that is substantially similar to its proposed conservation rule.

118-hr-3602.one_liner: Add prison time for tipping off criminals about border agents or destroying border equipment
provisions: Anyone who tells criminals where border agents are, to help with an immigration, customs, or drug crime, can get up to 10 years in prison.
Destroying or damaging a device used to watch the border or a border crossing can get someone up to 10 years in prison.
Using a gun while helping someone with a felony record enter the country illegally adds extra prison time on top of the original sentence.

118-hr-4016.one_liner: Speed up repayment to veterans whose benefits were stolen by their caretakers
provisions: When a person in charge of a veteran's money misuses those funds, the VA must pay the veteran back faster.
The VA cannot hold up repayment just because it hasn't finished deciding whether it made a mistake in choosing that caretaker.
The VA does not have to investigate its own role in every single case of stolen benefits before sending repayment.

118-hr-4581.one_liner: Add stillbirth prevention research to a federal health funding program
provisions: A federal program that gives money to states for mother and child health services will now also cover research on preventing stillbirths.
States can use the grant money to run programs that work to reduce the number of stillbirths.

118-hr-4143.one_liner: Expand a federal team's power to investigate collapses of bridges, towers, and other structures
provisions: A federal team at NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) can only investigate when buildings collapse or almost collapse.
People must have died or been at risk of dying.
This bill lets the team also investigate other structures, like bridges or towers.
The team finds out what likely caused the structure to fail.
The team also looks at how people were evacuated and whether emergency responses worked.
The team recommends changes to engineering rules and standards based on what it finds.

118-hr-4310.one_liner: Ban consumer products that contain 10% or more sodium nitrite
provisions: Makes it illegal to sell any consumer product that contains 10% or more sodium nitrite.
Sodium nitrite is a chemical that can be deadly in large amounts — a small quantity can kill a person.
A 10% concentration means 1 out of every 10 parts of the product is sodium nitrite.
Products with lower concentrations of sodium nitrite, like some cured meats, are not affected by this rule.

118-hr-4510.one_liner: Reauthorize and expand the federal office that manages wireless signals and internet policy
provisions: Keeps the NTIA — the federal office that manages wireless signals and internet policy — funded through 2025.
Raises the head of NTIA to a higher rank within the Department of Commerce.
Gives the NTIA official authority over spectrum — the frequencies that carry Wi-Fi, phone calls, and TV signals.
Requires the NTIA to run a public campaign to help Americans learn how to stay safe online.
Requires the NTIA to report on whether foreign companies in the U.S. telecom supply chain pose security risks.
Requires the NTIA to create a plan to get more Americans connected to the internet.
Requires the NTIA to review whether foreign ownership of U.S. telecom companies creates national security risks.

118-hr-4824.one_liner: Expand a Department of Energy program for carbon storage research, testing, and commercialization
provisions: The Department of Energy's carbon storage program now includes storing carbon in plants and soil, and storing it underground in rock formations and water-filled rock layers.
