The program covers research, testing, real-world demonstrations, and bringing carbon storage to commercial use — not just lab work.
DOE must submit a long-term, strategic, and prioritized plan once a year that identifies the biggest obstacles to using these carbon storage methods at a large scale.
The first long-term strategic plan must be submitted within two years of this bill becoming law.

118-hr-4755.one_liner: Fund federal research into tools that keep personal data private
provisions: The National Science Foundation must fund research on tools that make personal data harder to trace back to specific people.
The foundation must include this type of privacy research in its computer security grant program.
A network of 24 federal agencies must work together to speed up the creation and use of these privacy tools.
The National Institute of Standards and Technology must work with businesses and the public to create voluntary rules for using these tools when collecting and sharing data.

118-hr-4691.one_liner: Require Congress to approve or block Iran sanctions changes before they take effect
provisions: The President must send Congress a written notice before lifting, pausing, or changing any Iran sanctions.
After getting that notice, Congress has 30 days to vote on whether to allow the action.
If Congress is in summer recess between July 10 and September 7, the review window extends to 60 days.
The President cannot take the action until Congress approves it with a vote.
If Congress votes to block the action, the President cannot move forward with it.

118-hr-4763.one_liner: Set rules for which government agency oversees different types of digital money
provisions: Creates a set of rules deciding whether digital assets like crypto tokens are watched over by the CFTC (a trading watchdog) or the SEC (the stock market regulator)
If a digital asset runs on a blockchain that no single person or company controls, the CFTC oversees it — the same agency that watches over gold and oil trading
A blockchain counts as not controlled by one party if no person or company owns 20% or more of the digital asset or its voting power
If a digital asset runs on a blockchain where one person or company is still in charge, the SEC oversees it — the same agency that watches over stocks
Some digital assets can skip SEC rules if they cap how much they sell each year and limit sales to experienced investors who meet certain financial thresholds
Stablecoins — digital tokens tied to a fixed dollar value — are not regulated by either agency, except when it comes to stopping fraud

118-hr-4639.one_liner: Stop law enforcement from buying your private data without a court order
provisions: Right now, police and spy agencies can buy your personal data from data brokers without a warrant. This bill makes that illegal.
Data brokers are companies that collect and sell information about people — like where you go, what you buy, and who you talk to.
Under this bill, the government must get a judge's approval before getting your personal records from any outside company.
Government agencies cannot share data they bought with police or intelligence agencies to get around this rule.
Any data the government got this way cannot be used against you in court.
This bill also covers a new type of company — middlemen that move or store your data between tech services — and gives them the same rules as other tech providers.

118-hr-4877.one_liner: Start a five-year government research program on abandoned oil and gas wells
provisions: The Department of Energy must start a research program on abandoned oil and gas wells — wells that were drilled but no longer in use.
The program works to find where abandoned wells are located, including ones that were never officially recorded.
It studies how to plug, clean up, and repurpose those wells.
It looks for ways to reduce harm to the environment from abandoned wells.
The program runs for five years and then ends.

118-hr-5403.one_liner: Stop the Federal Reserve from creating or issuing a digital dollar
provisions: Stops Federal Reserve banks from opening accounts for individual Americans
Stops the Federal Reserve from creating a digital version of the U.S. dollar
Stops the Federal Reserve from using a digital dollar to control interest rates or the money supply

118-hr-529.one_liner: Extend the ocean zone where U.S. customs officers can board and check ships
provisions: The zone where U.S. customs rules apply at sea expands from 12 nautical miles to 24 nautical miles from the U.S. coast.
U.S. customs officers can board and search ships anywhere in this 24-nautical-mile zone.
Ships found carrying undeclared or illegal goods within 24 nautical miles of shore can be stopped and inspected.
The 24-nautical-mile boundary matches a limit the U.S. set under international law in 1999.
The old boundary — 4 leagues, which equals 12 nautical miles — is replaced by the new 24-nautical-mile line.

118-hr-5863.one_liner: Remove federal income taxes on payments received for wildfire and certain disaster losses
provisions: Money you get for wildfire disaster losses from fires declared after 2014 is not taxed as income.
People who lost money in the East Palestine, Ohio train derailment on February 3, 2023, don't pay taxes on relief payments.
The bill extends a rule that lets disaster victims deduct personal losses from their federal taxes.

118-hr-4866.one_liner: Create new programs to improve wildfire tracking and coordination across agencies
provisions: NOAA sets up a new program to help federal, state, and local groups share information about wildfires and how they spread.
The program funds research and tools to detect wildfires earlier and better understand how weather affects fire behavior.
NOAA can hire private companies to collect data from planes and satellites to help predict and monitor wildfires.
NOAA can test drones to gather weather data in areas where wildfires occur.
A new group made up of different federal agencies is created to help state and local governments manage wildfires without doing the same work twice.
A separate advisory group is created to give guidance to the coordinating group and other agencies on wildfire management.

118-hr-6093.one_liner: Extend NOAA weather forecasting programs and add new weather data tools
provisions: Keeps NOAA weather research programs funded through 2028
Requires NOAA to improve radar accuracy and expand weather forecasting in areas that currently get less coverage
Requires NOAA to buy weather data from private companies and test whether that data works with government systems
Requires upgrades to weather warning systems so they reach more people, including in rural areas, using newer technology like cloud-based services
Adds a program to improve flood forecasts along coastlines
Adds programs to improve weather forecasts for farmers and water managers in western and central states, plus a network to track soil moisture

118-hr-615.one_liner: Stop federal agencies from banning lead ammunition and fishing tackle on federal land
provisions: Stops federal agencies from banning lead bullets or lead fishing tackle on federal land open to hunting or fishing.
This applies to land run by the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture.
Agencies can still ban lead if field data from that specific area shows it is causing a drop in local wildlife.
The state where that land is located must also approve the ban before it can take effect.
Some lead rules that were already in place before this bill stay in effect.

118-hr-6046.one_liner: Label Ansarallah a terrorist group and freeze the money and visas of its members
provisions: The State Department must officially label Ansarallah, also known as the Houthis, as a foreign terrorist organization.
The President must freeze any money or property that Ansarallah holds in the United States.
Members, helpers, and partners of Ansarallah are banned from getting U.S. visas and have their U.S. money frozen.
Groups or businesses that Ansarallah owns or controls face the same money freeze and visa ban.

118-hr-6090.one_liner: Require the Education Department to use a set definition of antisemitism in discrimination reviews
provisions: The Education Department's civil rights office must consider the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) definition of antisemitism when looking into discrimination complaints.
The IHRA definition describes antisemitism as a certain perception of Jews, which may be expressed as hatred toward Jews.
This rule applies to schools and other programs that get federal money.
Right now, the civil rights office considers this definition as a guide, but this bill writes that requirement into law.

118-hr-5947.one_liner: Cancel a deal that moved $6 billion in Iranian funds and block future ones
provisions: Cancels the waiver that let about $6 billion in Iranian money move from bank accounts in South Korea to bank accounts in Qatar.
Those funds had been frozen, and the move was tied to the release of five American citizens held in Iran.
Ends the Treasury Department licenses that made those fund transfers possible.
Stops the President from using waiver power to free up certain Iranian accounts in the future.

118-hr-6323.one_liner: Change when the President can lift limits on foreign banks that helped Iran move money
provisions: Right now, the President can lift limits on foreign banks that helped Iran move money, but only when needed for national security.
This bill adds a second reason the President can lift those limits: if Iran stops supporting terrorism in other countries.
Congress gets the power to pass a vote blocking the President from using the national security reason to lift those limits.

118-hr-6543.one_liner: Require hotels and short-term rentals to show all fees in the listed price
provisions: Hotels, motels, inns, and short-term rentals must include all required fees in the price they show when advertising or listing a room.
When you browse for a place to stay, the price you see must already include fees like resort fees or cleaning fees — not add them at checkout.
This rule does not apply to travel booked through a company, government, or school travel program.
The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general can take action against businesses that break this rule.

118-hr-6285.one_liner: Reopen federal land in Alaska for oil and gas drilling
provisions: Brings back oil and gas leases in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (ANWR) in Alaska that were canceled by the Biden administration.
The Department of the Interior must accept bids on canceled leases within 30 days and reissue them.
A second round of lease sales must happen by December 22, 2024.
Cancels two federal rules and two executive orders that paused or limited drilling in the area.
Limits the ability of the President and the Department of the Interior to cancel future drilling leases in this area.
Limits the ability of courts to block lease approvals under this program.

118-hr-6571.one_liner: Create a federal program to track and fix weak spots in U.S. supply chains
provisions: A group inside the Department of Commerce tracks where important U.S. goods come from and flags weak spots that could cause shortages.
The government picks which industries, goods, and supply chains need the most attention and monitoring.
A team of federal agencies works together to respond when a supply chain problem hits.
The program works with other countries to find ways to reduce the risk of shortages.
Businesses can choose to follow new guidelines the government creates to lower their supply chain risk.
The program must report regularly on what it finds and how well it is working.

118-hr-6192.one_liner: Give the government more ways to cancel energy rules for home appliances
provisions: Appliance energy standards no longer need to be reviewed or updated on a 6-year schedule
The government can cancel an energy rule if it raises costs for consumers
The government can cancel an energy rule if it does not save a meaningful amount of energy or water
The government can cancel an energy rule if it makes a product — like a gas stove — unavailable to some buyers
New energy rules must be both technically possible and cost-justified before taking effect

118-hr-6960.one_liner: Keep federal funding for children's emergency medical programs through 2029
provisions: A federal program that helps states pay for emergency medical care for children will keep running.
The program gives money to state governments and medical schools to treat children who are badly hurt or very sick.
Federal funding for this program is approved through September 2029.

118-hr-6983.one_liner: Name a post office in Lakeland, Georgia after Nell Patten Roquemore
provisions: Gives the official name 'Nell Patten Roquemore Post Office' to the post office at 15 South Valdosta Road in Lakeland, Georgia.
The name is set by Congress, making it an official federal designation.
The name change applies only to that one building — no other post offices are affected.

118-hr-7423.one_liner: Name a post office in Rayville, Louisiana after Luke Letlow
provisions: The post office at 103 Benedette Street in Rayville, Louisiana will be officially named the Luke Letlow Post Office Building.
Luke Letlow was elected to represent Louisiana's 5th district in Congress but died in December 2020 before taking office.
The name change is honorary and does not change how the post office runs or the services it offers.
Only the one building at 103 Benedette Street in Rayville is affected by this bill.

118-hr-7109.one_liner: Add a citizenship question to the census and exclude non-citizens from House seat counts
provisions: The census form would ask every person in every household whether they are a U.S. citizen, a U.S. national, a non-citizen living here legally, or a non-citizen living here without legal status.
The government would publish the count of people in each of those four groups for every state.
Non-citizens would not be counted when the President sends Congress the population totals used to divide up House seats.
Right now, all people — citizens and non-citizens — are counted when deciding how many House seats each state gets.

118-hr-7219.one_liner: Make federal agencies post the data and methods behind their rules
provisions: The Office of Management and Budget must update its rules for how federal agencies use data when writing or updating regulations.
Federal agencies must use the best available data and science when writing any rule or guidance.
Any agency that writes a rule must post online the data sources, models, and methods it used so the public can see them.
These posting rules apply to any information that has a clear or large effect on how a rule is written or explained to the public.

118-hr-6572.one_liner: Create a federal program to promote blockchain and digital ledger technology
provisions: The Department of Commerce must create a program to support blockchain and other digital ledger technologies.
Blockchain is a system that stores and shares verified digital records across many computers at once.
The program also covers digital tokens — transferable online records — and the process of creating them.
Commerce must form advisory groups to develop best practices for using blockchain and related technologies.
Commerce must send Congress a yearly report on the program.
The report must include recommendations for new laws to strengthen U.S. competitiveness in blockchain.

118-hr-7343.one_liner: Require federal detention of non-citizens who assault police or first responders
provisions: Non-citizens who are arrested for, charged with, or convicted of assaulting a police officer, firefighter, or other first responder must be taken into federal custody.
The Department of Homeland Security is required to detain these individuals — it does not have the option to skip detention.
This rule applies to non-citizens who already meet certain grounds for being denied entry into the United States.
Once detained, these individuals can be removed from the country.

118-hr-7581.one_liner: Require a federal report on attacks against police officers and their mental health resources
provisions: The Department of Justice must write a report on attacks that targeted police officers on purpose.
The report must look at whether these attacks can be added to existing crime tracking systems.
The report must also list what mental health support is available to police officers.

118-hr-7659.one_liner: Keep the Coast Guard funded and update its rules through 2026
provisions: Keeps the Coast Guard running at current staffing levels through the end of 2026.
Lets the Coast Guard respond to cyberattacks, crime by foreign groups, and threats from other countries.
Gives Coast Guard Academy teachers a faster path to getting hired.
Gives some Coast Guard Reserve members up to 12 days of parental leave when they have a new child.
Requires the Coast Guard to make evacuation plans for its bases in areas at high risk of a tsunami.
Requires a higher-level review before keeping an officer who has a sexual assault on their record.
Provides money to buy new ships and planes, update computer systems, and fix buildings.

118-hr-764.one_liner: Remove federal protections for gray wolves in the lower 48 states
provisions: Takes gray wolves off the federal protected species list in the lower 48 states.
A 2020 rule took wolves off the protected species list.
A federal court struck that rule down in 2022 — this bill puts it back.
One separate subspecies, the Mexican wolf found in the Southwest, stays on the protected list.
Courts cannot challenge or block this rule change.

118-hr-7530.one_liner: Remove DC's power to lower criminal sentences and tighten youth offender rules
provisions: Takes away DC's power to change any criminal sentences that are in place when this bill becomes law.
Lowers the age for youth offender status from 24 to 18 — meaning 18-to-24-year-olds no longer qualify for lighter sentences.
Removes the ability for DC judges to give a sentence below the lowest sentence required by law for youth offenders.
Removes the option for DC judges to give probation instead of jail time to youth offenders.
Requires DC's Attorney General to post monthly crime data about youth offenders on a public website.

118-hr-7525.one_liner: Help local special districts qualify to receive federal grant money
provisions: The budget office called OMB has 180 days to put out rules on how federal agencies decide if a special district can get grants.
A special district is a local government body created by state law to do one specific job, like running a water system or fire department.
It has its own budget and is separate from other local governments in the area.
All federal agencies must follow those rules within one year of when they come out.

118-hr-8070.one_liner: Fund the military and set pay and rules for U.S. armed forces in 2025
provisions: Raises base pay for lower-ranked enlisted troops (E-1 through E-4) by an average of 15%, on top of a 4.5% raise already set for 2025
Sets the number of active duty and reserve troops allowed to serve
Lets the military buy aircraft, ships, and missiles
Requires the military to build a new missile defense site on the East Coast by December 31, 2030
Requires the military to set up a quantum computing center at a military research lab
Lets the Marines test AI and machine learning software to improve how supplies and equipment are tracked and delivered

118-hr-8036.one_liner: Send money to the Pentagon and State Department to support U.S. allies in Asia and the Pacific
provisions: Sends extra money to the Department of Defense and the State Department to support U.S. allies in Asia and the Pacific in the year starting October 2023.
Pays to replace military equipment and supplies that the U.S. sent to Taiwan and countries that helped Taiwan.
Puts money into building more submarines faster.
Funds military needs in the Pacific that were not yet covered in the regular budget.
Lets the President send more military equipment to other countries or international groups.
Adds money to a program that helps other countries buy U.S. military equipment.
Gives money to an international group that makes low-interest loans to poorer countries.

118-hr-8035.one_liner: Send about $61 billion in emergency military and economic aid to Ukraine
provisions: The bill sends about $61 billion in emergency funding — labeled as outside the normal budget limits — to support Ukraine in its war with Russia.
The Department of Defense gets money to replace weapons and equipment already sent to Ukraine and to cover the cost of military training it provided.
The State Department and the U.S. foreign aid agency get money to send to Ukraine to help keep its government and economy running.
The President must send long-range missiles called Army Tactical Missile Systems to Ukraine.
Ukraine must sign an agreement to pay the U.S. back for the economic money it receives.
Other countries must chip in matching funds for some of the aid, so the U.S. is not the only one paying.
New rules require regular updates to Congress on how the money is being used and whether it is reaching its stated goals.

118-hr-8034.one_liner: Send military weapons and aid money to Israel during the conflict
provisions: Sends money to the U.S. military to cover the cost of operations in the Middle East
Buys new weapons to replace ones the U.S. already sent to Israel, including Iron Dome and David's Sling missile defense systems
Pays to send additional weapons and military equipment directly to Israel through a government arms program
Sends money to help refugees and people forced from their homes by the conflict
Adds money to protect U.S. embassies and government buildings in other countries
Gives the President more power to send military equipment to other countries without going through the normal approval steps
Stops any of this money from going to the U.N. Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA)

118-hr-8038.one_liner: Add sanctions and bans targeting fentanyl traffickers, Iran, and TikTok
provisions: Freezes the money and property of people outside the US who are linked to bringing fentanyl into the country.
Lets the US take Russian government money and send it to Ukraine to pay for war damage and rebuilding.
Bans TikTok and its parent company ByteDance from operating apps or websites in the US.
Stops companies that sell personal data from sharing Americans' private information with China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.
Freezes money and blocks travel for foreign people who help Iran sell oil to other countries.
Freezes money of foreign governments that give weapons or funding to Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad.
Stops US banks from doing business with Chinese banks that help Iran sell oil.

118-hr-8580.one_liner: Funds military construction and veterans services for the year starting October 2024
provisions: Sends money to the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, National Guard, and reserve units to build and repair military bases and facilities.
Pays for the NATO Security Investment Program, which funds shared military buildings and infrastructure with U.S. allies.
Funds health care, benefits, and burials for about 9 million veterans through the Department of Veterans Affairs.
Pays for building, fixing, and running housing for military families and service members who live on base.
Pays to close and clean up old military bases no longer in use.
Funds the Armed Forces Retirement Home, which provides housing and care for retired military veterans.
Also pays for national war memorials and a court that handles veterans legal appeals.

118-hr-8146.one_liner: Require a government report on how border policies affected police officers
provisions: Tells the Department of Justice to write a report on how border policies from 2021 to 2025 affected police officers at the federal, state, local, and tribal levels.
The report covers officers from all levels of government — not just federal border agents.

118-hr-8369.one_liner: Require the U.S. to deliver all weapons and military aid to Israel
provisions: Stops the government from blocking or pausing weapons deliveries to Israel.
Stops federal money from being used to pay any Pentagon or State Department worker who holds back military aid to Israel.
Requires the Pentagon and State Department to deliver all weapons and military equipment that were scheduled to go to Israel in 2024 and 2025.
Freezes some Pentagon and State Department office budgets until those offices confirm all held-back weapons have been delivered to Israel.
Requires the Pentagon and State Department to file regular reports to Congress on what weapons and military support have been sent to Israel.

118-hr-8289.one_liner: Keep FAA programs and airport funding running through May 17, 2024
provisions: Keeps FAA drone testing programs running until May 17, 2024, including programs that track where drones are flying.
Keeps the airport grants program going — it gives money to public airports for building projects and reducing noise near airports.
Keeps taxes on airline tickets and jet fuel in place so the FAA can keep collecting money to fund aviation programs.
Keeps a program running that lets smaller airports use remote-operated towers instead of having staff on-site.
Lets the Department of Homeland Security and the Justice Department keep taking action against drones that get too close to high-risk sites inside the United States.

118-hr-8282.one_liner: Cut US funding to the ICC and sanction people who help it investigate protected persons
provisions: Cuts all US government money going to the International Criminal Court (ICC) and blocks future payments.
Puts visa bans and property freezes on any foreign person who helps the ICC investigate, arrest, or prosecute a protected person.
Also bans the family members of sanctioned people from getting US visas.
Protected persons include US citizens, US companies, and anyone living in the US.
They also include citizens or legal residents of US-allied countries that have not joined the ICC.
The US signed but never ratified the ICC treaty, and formally withdrew its signature in 2002.

118-hres-1209.one_liner: Remove the current Speaker of the House from their position
provisions: Declares the Speaker of the House seat empty, which would require the House to vote for a new Speaker
Any member of the House can call this vote, and it passes with a simple majority of members present

118-hres-1173.one_liner: Set debate rules for seven bills covering mining, hunting, wildlife, and antisemitism
provisions: This resolution sets the terms for how the House will debate seven separate bills.
One bill would let hunters and anglers use lead bullets and lead fishing gear on federal lands and waters.
One bill would give mining companies more stable rights to use land near their mine sites for support operations.
One bill would bring back mining leases and permits in the Superior National Forest in Minnesota that were canceled.
One bill would remove the gray wolf from the federal list of protected endangered animals.
One bill would cancel a federal rule that required the Bureau of Land Management to protect and preserve federal land health.
One bill would lock in the permits and approvals already given to oil and gas companies to drill on Alaska's coastal plain.

One bill would require schools and colleges that get federal money to use a definition of antisemitism from a group called the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance when handling discrimination complaints.

118-hres-1160.one_liner: Set House voting rules for five foreign aid and sanctions bills
provisions: The House set the rules for debating and voting on five bills at once.
One bill provided emergency money for Israel through September 30, 2024.
A second bill provided emergency money for Ukraine through the same date.
A third bill provided emergency money for countries in the Indo-Pacific region.
A fourth bill let the President place sanctions on Russia and Iran.
The House voted to accept changes the Senate made to a combined foreign aid bill called H.R. 815.

118-hres-1112.one_liner: Formally oppose Biden administration immigration policies in Congress
provisions: This resolution is a formal statement from Congress that does not change any laws or spend any money.
It states that Congress disagrees with how the Biden administration handled immigration at the border.
It calls on the administration to use different immigration policies, including stricter border enforcement.

118-hres-1194.one_liner: Set rules for House floor votes on energy, census, crypto, and mining bills
provisions: Allows a House vote on energy appliance rules. That bill would stop the Energy Department from setting new standards unless proven to work and worth the cost.
Allows a House vote on adding a citizenship question to the U.S. Census. That bill would base House seat counts on citizens only, not all residents.
Allows a House vote to cancel an SEC rule on crypto. That rule required banks to list customers' crypto holdings as debts on their books.
Allows a House vote on a mining bill. That bill would give mining companies more secure rights to use land around their mines for support work.

118-hres-1210.one_liner: Condemn Biden Administration border policies and call on leaders to support law enforcement
provisions: Congress states that border policies during the Biden Administration put extra pressure on law enforcement officers
Congress says that law enforcement officers face dangers and stress because of conditions at the border
Congress calls on leaders at all levels of government to support and encourage law enforcement officers
Congress expresses sympathy for the stress that law enforcement officers deal with on the job

118-hres-1215.one_liner: Call on leaders to speak out against antisemitism and recognize Jewish American contributions
provisions: Calls on elected officials and faith leaders to speak out against antisemitism
Calls on government and civic leaders to take steps to protect Jewish American communities
Calls on the executive branch and civic leaders to tell the public about the history and contributions of Jewish Americans

118-hres-1213.one_liner: Express Congress's condemnation of calls to cut or eliminate police funding
provisions: Says Congress condemns any calls to cut or eliminate police funding
States that police officers need proper equipment, training, and resources to keep the public safe
Expresses condolences to the families of officers who died in the line of duty

118-hres-1243.one_liner: Schedule House votes on digital money rules and DC voting limits
provisions: Sets up a vote on rules for who oversees digital currencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum — two agencies would share that job: the CFTC and SEC
Sets up a vote to stop the Federal Reserve from creating a government-run digital dollar that people could use directly
Sets up a vote to block non-citizens from voting in Washington DC elections

118-hres-1227.one_liner: Schedule House votes on bills about law enforcement, DC crime, and Israel defense
provisions: The House can vote on a bill to send defense equipment to Israel
The House can vote on a bill to limit youth offender status in Washington, D.C. to people 18 and under
The House can vote on a bill to hold non-citizens in jail if they assault a police officer
The House can vote on bills requiring reports on how the southern border affects local, state, and federal police
The House can vote on a bill updating rules for off-duty and retired police officers carrying guns in public

118-s-546.one_liner: Expand a federal grant program to help police departments hire more officers
provisions: Lets police departments use federal COPS grant money to cover the cost of background checks, psychological tests, and other fees that job applicants have to pay
Creates new grants for police departments that team up with schools and colleges to run job fairs and recruiting events
Tells the Department of Justice to create a guide to help police departments that are short-staffed apply for these grants
Requires the Government Accountability Office to study how recruiting problems and officers leaving the job affect police departments at the federal, state, tribal, and local levels

118-hres-1287.one_liner: Set the House debate rules for the 2025 military spending bill
provisions: This resolution controls how the House of Representatives debates H.R. 8070, the 2025 defense spending bill.
It sets how much time members of Congress get to speak about the bill on the House floor.
It decides which changes to the bill members can propose during debate.
After debate ends, it allows the full House to hold a final vote on the defense bill.

118-hres-1269.one_liner: Allow the House to vote on veterans funding and ICC sanctions bills
provisions: Allows the House to vote on a bill that sets funding for military building projects and the Department of Veterans Affairs through September 30, 2025.
Allows the House to vote on a bill that would put restrictions on the International Criminal Court if it investigates, arrests, or takes to trial any American or person from a U.S. ally country.
Sets the rules for how long the House can debate each bill and how the votes will work.

118-s-138.one_liner: Set a U.S. position on Tibet's legal status and counter China's claims about Tibet
provisions: The U.S. defines Tibet to include not just the Tibet Autonomous Region, but also Tibetan areas in four other Chinese provinces: Qinghai, Sichuan, Gansu, and Yunnan.
A U.S. government office focused on Tibet gets a new job: push back on false information about Tibet's history spread by China's government.
The U.S. officially states that the conflict between Tibet and China is not resolved and that Tibet's legal status is still an open question under international law.

118-hres-1292.one_liner: Find Attorney General Merrick Garland in contempt of Congress for ignoring a subpoena
provisions: Says AG Merrick Garland broke the rules by not turning over what the House Judiciary Committee asked for in a subpoena.
The House votes to officially find him in contempt of Congress.
Tells the Speaker of the House to send the case to federal prosecutors in Washington, D.C.
Federal prosecutors would then decide whether to bring criminal charges against Garland.
Tells the Speaker to take any other steps needed to force Garland to follow the subpoena.

117-hr-1218.one_liner: Add pregnancy and birth outcome data to an FCC internet health map
provisions: The FCC runs an online map that shows where people have internet access and how that connects to health outcomes. This bill adds data about what happens to mothers during and after pregnancy to that map.
The FCC must work with the CDC to decide which pregnancy and birth outcomes to include on the map.
A government watchdog agency must study whether having internet access improves health outcomes for pregnant women and new mothers.

119-sjres-103.one_liner: Cancel a VA rule letting veterans get reproductive health care at VA facilities
provisions: The Department of Veterans Affairs made a rule letting veterans and some family members get reproductive health care at VA facilities.
The rule applied even in states where that care is restricted.
This resolution cancels that VA rule.
Once canceled, VA facilities in states that restrict reproductive care would no longer be required to provide it under that rule.

117-hconres-70.one_liner: Condemn threats against historically Black colleges and recognize Black History Month
provisions: Congress states that threats and violence against historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) are wrong
Congress says the federal government will work to protect HBCU students, teachers, and staff from violence
Congress recognizes Black History Month

119-sjres-107.one_liner: Cancel an IRS rule on when wind and solar projects qualify for tax credits
provisions: Cancels an IRS rule setting the standard for when a wind or solar project counts as started for tax credit purposes.
These credits are called the Clean Electricity Production Credit and the Clean Electricity Investment Credit.
They give tax breaks to companies that build new wind or solar power facilities.
Under the canceled rule, a project qualified for credits if it broke ground before a set deadline, even if not yet finished.
Without this rule, there is no IRS standard defining when a wind or solar project counts as having started construction.

119-sjres-116.one_liner: Pull US military forces out of any fighting with Iran not approved by Congress
provisions: Tells the President to stop using US military forces in any fighting with or inside Iran
Stops any US military action against Iran that Congress has not voted to approve
Applies to all US armed forces currently involved in hostilities connected to Iran

117-hr-1916.one_liner: Require private health insurance to cover treatment of birth defects and congenital conditions
provisions: Private health insurance plans must cover diagnosis and treatment of birth defects and conditions a person is born with.
Coverage must include surgeries, procedures, and items that improve, fix, or restore body parts — if a doctor says it is needed for normal function or appearance.
Insurance plans cannot set stricter limits or higher out-of-pocket costs for these services than they do for other medical or surgical care.

117-hr-2116.one_liner: Ban discrimination based on hair texture or style tied to race or national origin
provisions: Makes it illegal to treat someone differently because of their hair texture or style.
This applies when that style or texture is tied to their race or where their family is from.
The law covers jobs, housing, public places, and any program that gets federal money.
Anyone discriminated against under this law can take legal action to enforce their rights.

117-hr-2074.one_liner: Set up a federal program to help tribes own and manage buffalo on their lands
provisions: The federal government sets up a program inside the Department of the Interior.
The program helps Native American tribes own and manage buffalo on their own lands.
The government can give tribes money, contracts, and support for bringing buffalo back or managing them.
Before taking any action that affects buffalo or their habitat — including dealing with sick buffalo — the government must talk with tribes first.
The government will write a policy for how buffalo and their habitat are managed on tribal lands.
The government can move extra buffalo from federal land onto tribal land if a tribe agrees.

117-hr-1621.one_liner: Stop judges from using not-guilty charges to give longer prison sentences
provisions: Right now, a federal judge can give someone a longer prison sentence based on crimes a jury found them not guilty of.
This bill stops that practice.
Judges can still consider the crimes someone was found guilty of when deciding a sentence.
This applies to federal courts across the country.

117-hr-1836.one_liner: Let National Guard and Reserve members count more service time toward GI Bill education benefits
provisions: National Guard and Reserve members can now count paid training days, inactive duty training, and general duty service toward their GI Bill education benefits.
Before this bill, some types of service that came with pay did not count toward qualifying for education benefits.
This change lets more Guard and Reserve members qualify for the Post-9/11 GI Bill, which covers tuition, housing, and books at colleges and trade schools.

117-hr-2842.one_liner: Rename a post office in Petaluma, California after Lynn C. Woolsey
provisions: Gives the federal post office at 120 4th Street in Petaluma, California the official name 'Lynn C. Woolsey Post Office Building'
This is a federal action covering a U.S. Postal Service building, not a state or city decision
The bill does not change how the post office runs, who works there, or what services it offers
No money is spent and no other rules are changed by this bill

117-hr-2324.one_liner: Rename a post office in Tallahassee, Florida after D. Edwina Stephens
provisions: Changes the official name of the post office at 2800 South Adams Street in Tallahassee, Florida to the 'D. Edwina Stephens Post Office'

117-hr-3113.one_liner: Put public land maps online showing which roads, trails, and waters are open
provisions: Three federal agencies — the Department of the Interior, the Forest Service, and the Army Corps of Engineers — must agree on shared data standards so their maps work together.
These agencies must put digital maps online showing which roads and trails on public land are open or closed.
The maps must show what types of vehicles — like ATVs, trucks, or bikes — are allowed on each road or trail.
The maps must show the dates when roads and trails open and close each season.
The maps must show where hunting and shooting are allowed and where they are restricted.
The maps must show which parts of rivers or lakes are closed to boats or have limits on engine power.

117-hr-2954.one_liner: Change rules for workplace retirement savings accounts
provisions: Requires many employers to sign workers up for retirement savings plans automatically, instead of waiting for workers to sign up themselves
Raises the age at which retirees must start taking money out of their retirement accounts from 72 to 75
Lets older workers put more money into their retirement accounts each year to catch up on savings

117-hr-2501.one_liner: Require two federal agencies to update their agreement on handling radio frequency disputes
provisions: Tells the FCC and a Commerce Department office called NTIA to update the written agreement they share on how radio frequencies get managed
The update must improve how the two agencies settle conflicts when different users share or are close to the same radio frequencies
The update must make sure radio frequencies are used as efficiently as possible

117-hr-3359.one_liner: Give murder victims' families the right to request a review of unsolved cases
provisions: Family members of murder victims can ask federal investigators to review the case file if the murder happened more than 3 years ago
To qualify, investigators must have already followed all leads and have no named suspect
Immediate family members — like parents, spouses, and children — are the ones who can make this request

117-hr-3531.one_liner: Let a private foundation build a WWII home front women's memorial
provisions: A private group called the Women Who Worked on the Home Front Foundation gets permission to build a memorial on federal land in Washington, D.C.
The memorial honors women who worked jobs in the U.S. to support the war effort during World War II.
The private foundation must raise and pay for all costs to build the memorial — no federal money can be used.
The memorial must follow the rules set by the Commemorative Works Act, which covers how memorials are built on federal land.

117-hr-3539.one_liner: Rename a post office in Hagatna, Guam after Atanasio Taitano Perez
provisions: Names the post office at 223 West Chalan Santo Papa in Hagatna, Guam the 'Atanasio Taitano Perez Post Office'.
This is a ceremonial naming — it changes only the official name and nothing else about the post office.
The bill does not include any information about who Atanasio Taitano Perez was.

117-hr-3197.one_liner: Transfer federal land in Eunice, Louisiana to the city for free
provisions: The federal government gives specific parcels of land in Eunice, Louisiana to the city at no cost.
The land being transferred is part of the original townsite of Eunice.
Once the land is transferred, it is removed from the boundaries of Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve in Jefferson Parish, Louisiana.

117-hr-3485.one_liner: Block foreign nationals who violate LGBT and intersex rights abroad from getting U.S. visas
provisions: Blocks foreign nationals from getting U.S. visas if they violated people's rights based on sexual orientation, gender identity, or sex characteristics.
This covers violations against people who are LGBT or intersex — or who others think are, even if they are not.
The President must create a list of foreign nationals responsible for these violations and update it regularly.
People on that list can also face other U.S. penalties beyond being blocked from getting visas.
The State Department must assign a senior officer to track violence and discrimination against LGBT and intersex people in other countries.

117-hr-3743.one_liner: Raises the money the FDA and NIH must send to their research foundations each year
provisions: The FDA must send at least $1,250,000 to the Reagan-Udall Foundation each year — up from $500,000.
The NIH must send at least $1,250,000 to the Foundation for the NIH each year — also up from $500,000.
Both agencies can now send up to $5,000,000 a year to their foundations — up from $1,250,000.
Both foundations use this money to support scientific research that helps the FDA and NIH do their work.

117-hr-4445.one_liner: Let people take sexual assault and harassment cases to court instead of forced arbitration
provisions: If someone signs a contract that says they must use private arbitration for sexual assault or harassment claims, that part of the contract no longer counts.
People can still choose arbitration after an incident happens, but companies cannot force it ahead of time.
This applies to new claims filed after the law takes effect.
Courts — not private arbitrators — decide whether this law applies to a specific case.

117-hr-4380.one_liner: Name a garden in El Paso, Texas an official national memorial
provisions: Makes the Healing Garden at 6900 Delta Drive in El Paso, Texas an official national memorial
The garden is renamed the El Paso Community Healing Garden National Memorial

117-hr-3894.one_liner: Require Medicaid to update its guidance on health issues linked to poverty
provisions: Tells the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to update its rules for states on how to handle health problems tied to poverty, housing, and other life conditions
Covers both Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), which together serve over 90 million Americans
States must get updated guidance from the federal government on a regular basis to help them respond to these issues

117-hr-3617.one_liner: Remove marijuana from federal drug laws and wipe federal marijuana conviction records
provisions: Removes marijuana from the federal list of illegal substances, so no one can face federal charges for making, selling, or having marijuana.
Creates a process for people with federal marijuana convictions to have those records cleared.
Adds a federal tax on cannabis products made or brought into the US.
Creates a fund to support people and businesses in communities that faced heavy marijuana enforcement.
Lets cannabis businesses apply for small business loans and services from the federal government.
Stops the federal government from taking away benefits like housing or food assistance based on marijuana-related offenses.
Stops immigration officials from denying someone's immigration case because of a marijuana-related event.

117-hr-4738.one_liner: Create a public archive of personal stories from the COVID-19 pandemic
provisions: The Library of Congress will collect personal stories from people who lived through the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States.
The project will gather video and audio recordings of people sharing their experiences.
All collected stories and records will be made available to the public.

117-hr-4673.one_liner: Automatically sign up veterans for VA health care when the Defense Department confirms they qualify
provisions: Veterans who qualify for VA health care get signed up automatically — they do not have to apply on their own.
The VA uses data from the Defense Department to confirm which veterans qualify, then signs them up.
Each veteran gets online access to proof of their enrollment and a way to opt out if they choose.

117-hr-4476.one_liner: Create a new council inside DHS to give advice on protecting the U.S. economy
provisions: Creates a new group inside the Department of Homeland Security called the DHS Trade and Economic Security Council.
The council gives advice and suggestions to DHS leaders about protecting the country's economy.
The council looks for situations where the U.S. depends too heavily on one country or one company for important goods.
The council helps DHS decide what economic security problems to focus on first.

117-hr-5001.one_liner: Extend federal programs to protect endangered fish in two Colorado river systems
provisions: Gives the Department of the Interior more time — through the 2024 budget year — to build facilities that help endangered fish survive in the Upper Colorado and San Juan rivers.
Moves the deadline for a progress report on these fish recovery programs to 2022.

117-hr-4706.one_liner: Add the Blackwell School in Marfa, Texas to the National Park System
provisions: Makes the Blackwell School in Marfa, Texas a national historic site managed by the federal government
The school was used during a time when Black and white students were forced into separate schools, from 1885 to 1965
The site cannot be created until the federal government signs a written deal with the Marfa school district to hand over or jointly manage the property
The federal government can only get land for the site through donations or land trades — not by taking it
No private land can be added to the site without the owner's written agreement
The Department of the Interior must write a plan for how the site will be managed

117-hr-5577.one_liner: Rename a post office in Atlanta, Georgia after John R. Lewis
provisions: Gives the post office at 3900 Crown Road Southwest in Atlanta, Georgia the official name 'John R. Lewis Post Office Building'

117-hr-5343.one_liner: Require FEMA to report to Congress on how often case managers leave their jobs
provisions: FEMA must send Congress a report showing how often case managers quit or leave their jobs
The report must include the average and middle length of time case managers stay employed
FEMA must describe what steps it is taking or plans to take to reduce turnover among case managers

117-hr-55.one_liner: Make lynching a federal hate crime with prison time and fines
provisions: Lynching is now listed as a hate crime under federal law.
People found guilty can be sent to prison, fined, or both.
This applies to any attack where a group of people kills or seriously harms someone because of their race, religion, or other protected identity.

117-hr-5547.one_liner: Require economic development grant applicants to include child care plans
provisions: Groups applying for public works or economic development grants must add a section to their planning documents describing how they will expand access to child care, elder care, disability care, or early childhood education in their area.
This applies to grants given out under the Economic Development Administration program.
The new requirement is added to the planning document that grant applicants already have to submit — called a comprehensive economic development strategy.

117-hr-5314.one_liner: Add new rules limiting presidential power and blocking foreign money in elections
provisions: The President cannot pardon himself or herself.
If a sitting President or Vice President commits a federal crime, the clock on filing charges stops until they leave office.
Anyone running for President or Vice President must hand over their last 10 years of tax returns to the Federal Election Commission.
The Department of Justice must keep a written record of all calls and meetings between its staff and the White House.
If Congress issues a subpoena and someone ignores it, Congress gets new tools to force compliance in court.
Presidential emergency declarations get new time limits and rules that Congress can use to push back.
Political campaigns must report any contact with foreign governments, and foreign donations of money or private information about a candidate stay banned.

117-hr-5657.one_liner: Create a new registration process for medical marijuana research
provisions: Creates a new sign-up process so doctors and scientists can get permission from the DEA to study medical marijuana
Lets companies register with the DEA to grow and supply marijuana specifically for medical research
The Department of Health and Human Services must keep running its existing marijuana growing program through the National Institute on Drug Abuse
Lets researchers access the same types of marijuana sold in state-licensed dispensaries, not just government-grown research strains
The government-supplied marijuana stays available until private companies can provide enough on their own

117-hr-5616.one_liner: Require DHS to track and improve accreditation for its law enforcement training programs
provisions: DHS must report to Congress on whether each of its basic training programs is accredited.
If a DHS training program loses accreditation, that part of DHS must notify the department within 30 days.
DHS must research new tools and systems to let state, local, tribal, and territorial agencies access DHS training.
The focus is on departments in rural or hard-to-reach areas.
The goal is to help these agencies prepare for terrorism and other homeland security threats.

117-hr-5673.one_liner: Update rules for a federal loan program that helps communities prepare for disasters
provisions: The federal government runs a loan program that helps cities and towns reduce damage from natural disasters before they happen.
Cities and towns that get money from this program must follow the two most recent published versions of building safety codes and construction standards.
The bill makes small fixes to how this loan program works.

117-hr-5665.one_liner: Create a State Department office to track anti-Muslim acts in foreign countries
provisions: Creates an office inside the State Department to monitor anti-Muslim acts in other countries.
Creates a government position called the Special Envoy for Monitoring and Combating Islamophobia to lead the office.
Requires the State Department's yearly reports to Congress to cover anti-Muslim acts in foreign countries.
Those reports must include information about violence, harassment, and hate speech targeting Muslim people.
The reports must also cover what each country's government did in response to those acts.

117-hr-5641.one_liner: Raise the dollar limit that qualifies a disaster recovery project as small
provisions: Raises the cutoff for what counts as a small project to $1 million, letting more disaster recovery projects use a faster, simpler approval process.
Small projects get approved under a shorter set of steps, which means communities can start rebuilding sooner after a disaster.
The government must check and possibly update this $1 million cutoff every three years.

117-hr-5681.one_liner: Give Shadow Wolves tracking unit officers a higher ICE rank
provisions: Lets ICE upgrade Shadow Wolves officers to special agent rank after required training.
Shadow Wolves is a tracking unit that patrols land belonging to the Tohono O'odham Nation.
Officers in similar tracking units at other locations can also be upgraded to special agent rank after the same training.
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) must study and report on the best ways to expand the Shadow Wolves program.
The Government Accountability Office (GAO) must do a separate study on expanding the program.

117-hr-5689.one_liner: Expand disaster prevention funding and coverage for wildfires, tsunamis, and ice storms
provisions: Lets unused disaster prevention money be moved to other projects after 7 years or when a grant closes, whichever comes first.
Raises the share of national disaster prevention grants for public buildings and roads from 6% to 15%.
Lets private nonprofit buildings — like food banks or community centers — get money and help to prepare for disasters before they happen.
Adds wildfires, tsunamis, and ice storms to the list of disasters that prevention money can be used for.
Requires FEMA to set aside 10% of yearly disaster prevention funds to help buildings meet the latest published safety codes.
Creates a test program where states and cities give money directly to homeowners to make their homes more disaster-proof.

117-hr-5695.one_liner: Update internal government bookkeeping references in federal law
provisions: Changes page and chapter numbers inside the U.S. law books so they point to the right place after a 2016 reorganization
No new rules, spending, or rights are created or removed — only the location codes inside the legal text change

117-hr-5679.one_liner: Fix outdated cross-references in federal law across ten titles of U.S. Code
provisions: Updates internal bookkeeping in federal law so that references to old section numbers point to the correct, current section numbers
Does not change any policy, funding, or rules — only corrects where one law points to another
Affects sections across ten areas of federal law, including agriculture, education, and public lands
No dollar amounts, deadlines, or rules for people are changed

117-hr-5677.one_liner: Fix outdated cross-references in federal law without changing any rules
provisions: This bill corrects technical errors in federal law where internal references point to the wrong place.
It updates how laws in Title 2 (laws about Congress), Title 50 (laws about national security), and Title 52 (laws about elections) refer to each other.
No rights, benefits, or rules change as a result of this bill.
Only the internal numbering and references used by lawyers and courts are updated.

117-hr-6434.one_liner: Create a National Park Service network about Japanese American history in World War II
provisions: Tells the National Park Service to set up a network focused on Japanese American history during World War II
The network will look at existing studies about places where Japanese Americans were held during the war so it does not repeat work already done
The network will create and share materials like maps, guides, and online information about what Japanese Americans went through during World War II

117-hr-5705.one_liner: Update internal code references after crime law sections were moved to a new title
provisions: Congress moved crime and law enforcement laws to a new section of U.S. law called Title 34 in 2017.
Other laws that pointed to the old section numbers now have broken references.
This bill updates those old references so they point to the correct new location in Title 34.
No laws change — only the internal addresses used to find them.

117-hr-5982.one_liner: Update and reorganize existing space program laws into one place in the U.S. Code
provisions: Moves existing space program laws into a single section of federal law called Title 51
Does not change what the laws say — only reorganizes where they appear in the U.S. Code
Makes small technical fixes so the laws read clearly and consistently

117-hr-5706.one_liner: Require transportation companies to have policies against sexual assault and harassment
provisions: Passenger airlines, buses, trains, and rideshare companies like Uber and Lyft must create written policies on sexual assault and harassment, train their staff, and set up ways for people to report incidents.
People who physically or sexually assault transportation workers face civil fines.
The Department of Transportation must collect data on how many sexual assault and harassment reports each company receives and post that information online for the public to see.
People who experience sexual assault or harassment on transportation can report it to police in a way that keeps their name and personal details private.
The Department of Transportation must write and publish an official definition of what counts as sexual harassment in transportation.

117-hr-5961.one_liner: Update the federal rulebook for government advisory committees and financial disclosures
provisions: Rewrites the rules for federal advisory committees — groups of outside experts that give advice to the government — without changing what those rules actually say
Rewrites the rules for Offices of Inspector General, which are the government offices that look for waste and fraud, without changing what those rules say
Rewrites the financial disclosure rules for federal workers, including the President and Vice President, without changing what those rules say
Rewrites the rules about how much money federal workers can earn from outside jobs without changing what those rules say

117-hr-6865.one_liner: Fund the Coast Guard and update its safety and environmental rules through 2023
provisions: Sets the Coast Guard's budget for the years ending September 2022 and September 2023
Changes how the Coast Guard handles reports of sexual assault and sexual harassment among its members
Changes safety rules for ships and boats on the water
Changes rules for how ships and boats are built
Updates rules for navigation on U.S. waterways
Changes rules for dealing with aquatic invasive species — plants and animals that spread into waters where they don't belong and can damage local ecosystems
Changes rules for how oil spills are reported and cleaned up

117-hr-897.one_liner: Transfer 2,560 acres of California land to the Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians
provisions: Puts about 2,560 acres of land in California into federal trust for the Agua Caliente Band of Cahuilla Indians, a federally recognized tribe
Land held in trust becomes part of the tribe's reservation
No gambling is allowed on the land transferred through this bill

117-hr-963.one_liner: Stop companies from forcing workers and customers into private arbitration
provisions: Right now, many companies make workers and customers sign contracts that say any dispute must go to a private arbitrator instead of a court.
This bill makes those contract clauses unenforceable for disputes about jobs, shopping, competition, and civil rights.
Workers and consumers would be able to bring these disputes to court or join class-action lawsuits instead.
The change applies to new disputes after the bill becomes law.

117-hr-735.one_liner: Name a Cotati, California post office after Arturo L. Ibleto
provisions: The post office at 502 East Cotati Avenue in Cotati, California will officially be called the Arturo L. Ibleto Post Office Building.
Arturo Luis Ibleto was a person from the Cotati, California area whom Congress chose to honor with this public building designation.
No postal services, hours, staff, or operations at this location change — only the official name changes.
The U.S. Postal Service will update its records and building signs to use the new name.

117-hres-1017.one_liner: Set the House debate rules for cannabis and insulin cost bills
provisions: This is a procedural resolution — it sets the rules for how the House will debate two other bills, not a policy change itself.
The first bill (H.R. 3617) would remove cannabis from the federal list of illegal substances, making it no longer a federal crime to possess or use it.
H.R. 3617 would also let people with past federal cannabis convictions apply to clear their records.
H.R. 3617 would create a fund to send money to communities that faced heavy drug enforcement over the past decades.
The second bill (H.R. 6833) would cap how much people with health insurance have to pay out of pocket each month for insulin.

117-hres-849.one_liner: Set House debate rules for a bill creating a State Department anti-Islamophobia office
provisions: This is a procedural rule that sets the terms for how the House of Representatives can debate and vote on H.R. 5665.
It controls how much time members of Congress get to speak about the bill and what changes to the bill can be considered.
The underlying bill, H.R. 5665, would create a new office inside the State Department to track and respond to discrimination against Muslims around the world.
The procedural rule does not itself create the office — it only governs how the House handles the debate over whether to do so.

117-hres-831.one_liner: Call on the US to push NATO to create a center focused on democracy
provisions: Calls on the President to use the US vote at NATO to update NATO's core plan so it states support for shared democratic values among member countries
Calls on the President to use the US vote at NATO to create a Center for Democratic Resilience inside NATO's main office in Brussels
This center would work to strengthen democratic systems in NATO member countries, partner countries, and countries that want to join NATO
This is a resolution, meaning it expresses the opinion of Congress but does not create a law or spend money

117-hres-852.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress will vote on raising the debt limit
provisions: Sets the process Congress will follow to debate and vote on a bill that raises the federal debt limit
Limits how long Congress can debate the debt limit bill before taking a vote
Does not change the debt limit itself — only controls how the vote on changing it will work

117-hres-848.one_liner: Allow the House to vote on charging Mark Meadows with contempt of Congress
provisions: Lets the full House vote on a report from the committee that investigated the January 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol.
The report says Mark Meadows, who was White House Chief of Staff under President Trump, should be charged with contempt of Congress.
Contempt of Congress means the House believes a person refused to hand over documents or answer questions that Congress asked for.
This is a procedural step — it opens debate and a vote on the contempt report, but does not itself charge anyone.

117-hres-851.one_liner: Find Mark Meadows in contempt of Congress for ignoring a legal order
provisions: Congress sent Mark Meadows a legal order to appear and hand over documents — called a subpoena.
Meadows was White House Chief of Staff when the January 6th attack on the Capitol happened.
He refused to follow that order.
This resolution says Congress officially finds him in contempt — meaning he broke the law by refusing.
The Speaker of the House must send his case to federal prosecutors for possible criminal charges.
The Speaker must also take steps to force Meadows to follow the subpoena.

117-hres-860.one_liner: Schedule votes on two bills about veteran education and VA healthcare enrollment
provisions: Allows the House to vote on a bill that counts time spent in active duty training toward GI Bill education benefits
Allows the House to vote on a bill that would sign eligible veterans up for VA healthcare automatically instead of requiring them to apply
Sets the debate time and rules for how each of these two bills will be considered on the House floor

117-hres-912.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress would vote on postal service and spending bills
provisions: Set a time limit and voting rules for debating the postal service bill (H.R. 3076) on the House floor
Set a time limit and voting rules for debating a spending bill (H.R. 6617) that kept the government funded through September 30, 2022
Decided which changes to those bills could be proposed and voted on during debate

117-hres-868.one_liner: Set the rules for how the House votes on a NASA property leasing bill
provisions: The House can debate the Senate's version of the NASA leasing bill under a set time limit with no extra changes allowed.
Once the time limit is up, the House votes up or down on the Senate version of the bill.
The House can move to a final vote on the rule itself without additional debate once it is brought up.

117-hres-950.one_liner: Set the rules for debating a veterans toxic exposure health care bill
provisions: Sets the time limit and debate rules for Congress to vote on H.R. 3967, a bill about health care for veterans exposed to toxic substances
Controls which changes to the bill can be proposed during debate
Does not change any health care rules itself — only controls how the vote on the main bill will be run

117-hres-900.one_liner: Set the rules for debating three separate bills in the House
provisions: This is a procedural bill that sets the time limits and debate rules for three other bills before the House votes on them.
The first bill would place sanctions on foreign individuals who violate the rights of LGBTQI people.
The second bill would stop companies from forcing workers and customers to use private arbitration in sexual assault or sexual harassment cases.
The third bill would create a federal research program focused on engineering biology to keep the U.S. competitive globally.

117-s-1226.one_liner: Name a federal courthouse in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania after Judge Sylvia H. Rambo
provisions: The courthouse at 1501 North 6th Street in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania gets an official new name: the Sylvia H. Rambo United States Courthouse.
Sylvia H. Rambo was appointed as a federal judge in 1979 — one of the first women to serve as a federal judge in Pennsylvania — and served on the bench for over 30 years.
The courthouse serves the Middle District of Pennsylvania, which handles federal court cases for the central part of the state.
The name is official and permanent — it applies to all signs, records, and documents tied to that building going forward.

117-hres-956.one_liner: Call for a cease-fire in Ukraine and continued support against Russia
provisions: Calls for an immediate stop to fighting in Ukraine
Calls for all Russian military forces to leave Ukrainian territory
Supports keeping economic penalties on Russia in place
Calls on the U.S. and its allies to send more military equipment to Ukraine for defense

117-s-2126.one_liner: Name a federal building in Cheyenne, Wyoming after Louisa Swain
provisions: The federal building at 308 W. 21st Street in Cheyenne, Wyoming will be officially named the Louisa Swain Federal Office Building.
Louisa Swain was the first woman to vote in a U.S. election, casting her ballot in Laramie, Wyoming in 1870.
Wyoming gave women the right to vote in December 1869, more than 50 years before the 19th Amendment made it a right for women across the country in 1920.

117-hres-979.one_liner: Set the rules for debating two bills in the House
provisions: Sets the time limit and rules for how the House can debate a bill about arbitration agreements
Sets the time limit and rules for how the House can debate a bill about hair texture and style discrimination
Controls which changes lawmakers can propose during debate on each bill

117-hres-973.one_liner: Set the rules for the House to vote on four separate bills
provisions: Allowed the House to vote on a government spending bill to fund federal agencies through September 2022
Allowed the House to vote on a short-term spending extension to keep the government running
Allowed the House to vote on a ban on importing oil and energy from Russia
Allowed the House to vote on emergency COVID-19 relief spending for 2022
Set time limits and debate rules for each of those four votes

117-s-2629.one_liner: Set up a national system to track and count cybercrime reports
provisions: The Department of Justice must work with the National Academy of Sciences to create a system for sorting different types of cybercrime into categories.
The DOJ must add a cybercrime section to the national database that police departments use to report crimes.
The national crime survey that the government runs each year must start asking people questions about cybercrime.
A government watchdog must check whether people are actually reporting cybercrime and whether some groups report it less than others.

117-s-3294.one_liner: Place statues of Justices Sandra Day O'Connor and Ruth Bader Ginsburg in the Capitol
provisions: A government committee must get statues of Supreme Court Justices Sandra Day O'Connor and Ruth Bader Ginsburg.
The statues must be placed permanently inside the U.S. Capitol building or on its grounds.
Sandra Day O'Connor was the first woman on the Supreme Court, serving from 1981 to 2006.
Ruth Bader Ginsburg served on the Supreme Court from 1993 until her death in 2020.

117-s-321.one_liner: Award a Congressional Gold Medal to the women of the 6888th Central Postal Battalion
provisions: Gives a Congressional Gold Medal to the women who served in the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion during World War II
The 6888th was made up of Black women in the U.S. Army who sorted mail for American troops stationed in Europe
The medal will be kept at the Smithsonian Institution where people can see it and researchers can study it

117-s-2959.one_liner: Let school districts use 2022 data for a key federal school funding program
provisions: School districts that get federal money through the Impact Aid Program can use their data from 2022 instead of collecting new data for 2023.
The Impact Aid Program gives money to schools that lose property tax income because federal land nearby does not get taxed.
Schools that have more students living on military bases or Native American lands also get money through this program.
Districts can use either their 2022 student count numbers or their 2022 federal property values — whichever applies to how they qualify for the program.

117-s-400.one_liner: Name the Department of Transportation headquarters building after William T. Coleman Jr.
provisions: The Department of Transportation building at 1200 New Jersey Avenue in Washington, DC gets a new official name: the William T. Coleman, Jr., Federal Building.
William T. Coleman Jr. was the first Black person to serve as U.S. Secretary of Transportation, a role he held from 1975 to 1977 under President Gerald Ford.
This is a name-only change — no rules change, no money moves, and the building works exactly as before.

117-s-566.one_liner: Rename a Rhode Island post office after Specialist Matthew R. Turcotte
provisions: Changes the official name of the post office at 42 Main Street in Slatersville, Rhode Island to the 'Specialist Matthew R. Turcotte Post Office'

118-hjres-165.one_liner: Cancel a 2024 federal rule on sex discrimination in schools
provisions: Cancels a 2024 Department of Education rule about sex discrimination in schools that get federal money.
The canceled rule set new definitions for what counts as sex-based harassment.
The canceled rule also added new steps schools must follow when students file sex discrimination complaints.
Schools go back to the rules that were in place before April 29, 2024.
Title IX, the 1972 law that bans sex discrimination in federally funded schools, stays in place.
This resolution only removes the 2024 update to how that law is enforced.

117-s-658.one_liner: Let the Department of Homeland Security partner with nonprofits to teach cybersecurity skills
provisions: The Department of Homeland Security can team up with a group of nonprofit organizations to build and run cybersecurity training programs.
The training is meant to help protect the country from online attacks.
The nonprofit group can create new training, update existing training, and teach it to people who need it.

117-s-583.one_liner: Require DHS to publish yearly reports on new government buying methods
provisions: DHS must post a yearly report on its website showing which new buying methods it used and whether they saved money, worked faster, or led to better results.
DHS must write guides and offer training to staff on new ways to buy goods and services from outside companies.
DHS must share what works across the agency and make that information available to other federal agencies.
A council of top government buyers from across federal agencies must meet to look at better ways to handle purchasing and contracts.
One of the goals DHS must track is whether more contracts are going to small businesses.

117-s-452.one_liner: Award a gold medal to hockey player Willie O'Ree for his role in growing the sport
provisions: Gives Willie O'Ree, or a family member if he is not available, a Congressional Gold Medal
The medal honors his work in hockey and his efforts to open the sport to more people

118-hr-1513.one_liner: Create a federal task force to study sixth-generation wireless technology
provisions: The FCC (the federal agency that oversees communications) must set up a group called the 6G Task Force.
The task force will include people from communications companies, public interest groups and universities, and federal, state, local, and tribal governments.
The task force will study the current state of 6G wireless technology and how standards for it are being set.
The task force will report on possible uses of 6G technology.

118-hr-1398.one_liner: Restart a Justice Department program to investigate Chinese government spying
provisions: Brings back a DOJ program that was shut down in 2022, now called the CCP Initiative.
The program looks into spying, hacking, and theft of U.S. trade secrets tied to the Chinese Communist Party.
It also watches for threats to U.S. power grids, water systems, and other key infrastructure.
DOJ must report to Congress once a year on what the program is doing and what problems it faces.
The program runs for six years and then automatically ends.

118-hr-1157.one_liner: Set up a fund to push back against Chinese government influence in the US and other countries
provisions: Creates a fund to pay for activities that push back against the Chinese government's efforts to gain power and control over other countries
Defines Chinese government influence as actions that help China gain control over other countries or hurt the security and independence of the US or its allies
Covers Chinese government efforts that threaten other countries' economies or governments

118-hr-1103.one_liner: Require yearly reviews of whether Hong Kong's US offices can stay open
provisions: Hong Kong has three offices in the US that get special protections, like not being taken to court and not paying property taxes.
The President must check at least once a year whether those offices should keep those protections.
If the President decides the offices no longer deserve those protections, the offices must close within 180 days.
If the President decides the offices can stay open, Congress can still vote to overrule that decision.
US government agencies can only work with these offices if they are still approved to operate under this law.

118-hr-1425.one_liner: Require Senate approval before the U.S. joins any WHO pandemic treaty
provisions: Any pandemic agreement made through the World Health Organization must be approved by the U.S. Senate before it takes effect.
The Senate must vote to approve it like a treaty — it cannot take effect by presidential action alone.
This applies to any agreement made through a WHO group formed in December 2021 to work on pandemic rules.

118-hr-2789.one_liner: Require studies on fighting drug smuggling and expanding services in nearby countries
provisions: The State Department must send Congress a plan to work with Mexican states and cities to stop fentanyl and opioid smuggling.
The State Department must study whether space-based phone and internet technology could help Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean.
The State Department must review how to help people in Caribbean countries get better access to banks and financial services.

118-hr-1631.one_liner: Let private groups keep copyright on technical standards written into law
