provisions: Private organizations that write technical standards keep their copyright even when those standards become part of a law or government rule.
To keep copyright protection, the organization must post the standard for free on a public website so anyone can read it.
If someone argues that a standard has lost its copyright, that person must prove it — the burden is on them, not the organization.

118-hr-5179.one_liner: Keep labeling rules for goods made in the West Bank and Gaza
provisions: Goods made in the West Bank or Gaza must carry labels showing where they were made
This labeling rule already exists, but this bill writes it into law so it is harder to remove
The State Department and U.S. Customs cannot spend any money to change or end this labeling rule

118-hr-3724.one_liner: Change the rules colleges must follow to keep their accreditation
provisions: Colleges that have accreditation can receive federal student aid — this bill changes the rules accrediting groups must follow to stay recognized by the government.
Accrediting groups cannot require colleges to take sides on political or social issues in order to keep their accreditation.
Accrediting groups cannot require colleges to treat people differently based on sex, race, or ethnicity.
Accrediting groups cannot stop a college from having a religious mission, requiring a statement of faith, or setting a code of conduct for students and employees.
Accrediting groups cannot add new rules beyond what Congress has specifically approved.

118-hr-1516.one_liner: Cut DHS funding to colleges with ties to Chinese government programs
provisions: Colleges that have contracts, deals, or received gifts from Chinese government-linked groups cannot get money from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
Confucius Institutes are cultural programs that get money from the Chinese government, directly or through other groups.
A college loses its DHS funding as long as it keeps that relationship.
A college can get its DHS funding back if it ends all ties with those groups.

118-hr-7213.one_liner: Keep funding autism research, education, and tracking programs through 2029
provisions: Keeps funding a CDC program that tracks how many people have autism and studies its causes through 2029.
Keeps funding programs run by the Department of Health and Human Services that help with autism education, early detection, and early treatment through 2029.
Keeps a federal committee running through 2029 that coordinates autism research and policy across government agencies.

118-hr-5339.one_liner: Require retirement plan managers to base investment choices only on financial risk and return
provisions: Managers of 401(k) and pension plans must choose investments based only on expected financial risk and return for workers.
Managers cannot use environmental, social, or other non-financial reasons when picking investments.
There is an exception: if two investment options look equal on financial grounds, a manager can use other factors to break the tie.
Workers who choose their own investments inside a retirement plan may still be offered options that use non-financial screens.

118-hr-7152.one_liner: Create a registry of Korean American families separated from relatives in North Korea
provisions: The State Department builds a list of Korean American families who want to reconnect with family members living in North Korea.
The registry stores information about these families to help arrange future in-person reunions.
When the U.S. government holds talks with North Korea, it must push for progress on family reunions.
The State Department sends regular reports to Congress on the registry and on whether North Korea is moving toward allowing reunions.

118-hr-5441.one_liner: Keep EPA programs running to protect and restore Long Island Sound through 2028
provisions: Keeps EPA programs running through 2028 that work to protect and restore Long Island Sound.
Long Island Sound is a body of water off the coasts of New York and Connecticut where rivers meet the ocean.
Includes a grant program that gives money to local groups working to conserve the area.
Long Island Sound supports fishing, swimming, and recreation for communities across New York and Connecticut.

118-hr-7637.one_liner: Stop the Energy Department from setting stricter rules on refrigerator energy use
provisions: Stops the Department of Energy from making or enforcing new energy rules for refrigerators, freezer-refrigerators, and freezers unless three conditions are met.
The new rule must be possible to build with current technology.
The new rule must not cost consumers more money overall.
The new rule must save a meaningful amount of energy.

118-hr-7700.one_liner: Restrict new dishwasher energy rules unless they are affordable, feasible, and save real energy
provisions: The Department of Energy can only set new energy rules for dishwashers if three tests are met.
The technology to meet the rule must already exist, and the rule must make economic sense.
The rule must not raise the total cost for buyers.
The rule must save a meaningful amount of energy.
The DOE also cannot enforce existing dishwasher energy rules that do not pass these three tests.

118-hr-7887.one_liner: Remove degree and experience requirements from most federal contractor job bids
provisions: Right now, the government can ask contractors to hire workers with specific degrees or years of experience.
This bill removes that requirement from most federal contract bids.
An agency can still add those requirements to a bid.
But the person in charge of the contract must write down why the job cannot be done without them.
The Office of Management and Budget must send guidance to all federal agencies within 60 days of this bill becoming law.
That guidance will explain how to follow the new rules.

118-hr-7909.one_liner: Make sex crimes and domestic violence grounds to deport or block non-citizens from entering
provisions: Non-citizens who admit to or are convicted of domestic violence, sex crimes, or planning a sex crime can be blocked from entering the US.
Current law lets the government deport non-citizens for domestic violence, stalking, and child abuse. This bill adds sex offenses — including crimes against children — to that list.
Non-citizens convicted of planning a sex offense can also be deported.
The bill expands what counts as domestic violence for deportation — it now includes physical or sexual abuse, or a pattern of controlling behavior, within close relationships like marriage or dating.

118-hr-8281.one_liner: Require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections
provisions: People must show a document proving U.S. citizenship — like a passport or birth certificate — when they sign up to vote in federal elections.
States cannot process a voter registration form for federal elections unless the person hands over that citizenship document.
States must set up a backup process for people who want to prove citizenship but do not have the standard documents.
States must check their voter rolls on an ongoing basis and remove anyone who is not a U.S. citizen.
Anyone can take an election official to court if that official signs up a voter who did not show citizenship proof.
Election officials who register someone without seeing citizenship proof can face criminal charges.
The federal agency that helps states run elections must send states instructions for following this law within 10 days.

118-hr-7980.one_liner: Block EV tax credits for cars with parts from companies tied to China or adversary nations
provisions: Cars with parts made or processed by companies tied to China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea lose the EV tax credit.
This applies to the new clean vehicle tax credit created in 2022, not older EV incentives.
Companies linked to terrorist groups are also covered by this rule.
Buyers of affected vehicles would no longer qualify for the credit, which is worth up to $7,500.

118-hr-8752.one_liner: Fund the Department of Homeland Security for the year starting October 2024
provisions: Gives money to the agencies that check people and goods entering the United States at the border.
Funds the agency that screens passengers and bags at airports across the country.
Gives money to FEMA, the agency that sends help after hurricanes, floods, and other disasters.
Funds the agency that enforces immigration laws inside the United States.
Gives money to the Coast Guard, which patrols U.S. waters and responds to emergencies at sea.
Funds the Secret Service, which protects the President and other government leaders.
Gives money to the agency that protects government computer systems from outside attacks.

118-hr-8314.one_liner: Fine nonprofits that take foreign money and then donate to political campaigns
provisions: If a nonprofit receives foreign money and then donates to a political campaign, it is fined.
The fine is 200% of the donation — meaning the group pays back double what it gave.
A nonprofit that does this more than twice loses its tax-exempt status.
Tax-exempt status means the group does not pay federal taxes — the bill removes that status after a third violation.

118-hr-8772.one_liner: Fund Congress and its support offices for the year starting October 2024
provisions: Gives money to pay for running the House of Representatives and offices that help lawmakers do their jobs
Pays for the Capitol Police, who protect Congress and the people and buildings around it
Funds the Congressional Budget Office, which figures out how much bills would cost before Congress votes on them
Funds the Library of Congress, which includes a research service that answers policy questions for lawmakers and a copyright office that protects creative work
Funds the Government Accountability Office, which checks whether the government is spending money the way it was supposed to
Sets rules for what the money in this bill can and cannot be used for
Does not include money for the Senate — the Senate sets its own budget separately

118-hr-8333.one_liner: Block federal funds from going to groups that use biotech from foreign adversary companies
provisions: Groups that get federal money cannot buy or use biotech equipment or services from companies linked to foreign adversaries like China.
The government must create a list of banned biotech companies; five specific companies are already named in the bill.
Any group that has a contract with a banned company also cannot receive federal funds.
The government can approve exceptions that last up to one year, with one possible extension of 180 days.
U.S. intelligence must write a report on the security risks of foreign companies collecting DNA and other body data through biotech tools.

118-hr-8771.one_liner: Fund the State Department and U.S. foreign programs for 2025
provisions: Gives the State Department money to run U.S. embassies and diplomatic offices around the world for the year starting October 2024.
Funds USAID, the government agency that sends development money and aid to other countries on behalf of the U.S.
Pays for the Peace Corps, which sends American volunteers to work in communities in other countries.
Funds the Export-Import Bank and other agencies that help U.S. companies sell goods and services to foreign buyers.
Pays for security programs that send military and economic help to other countries.
Funds commissions that track issues like religious freedom abroad and U.S. relations with China.

118-hr-8997.one_liner: Fund energy, water, and nuclear programs for the year starting October 2024
provisions: Gives money to the Army Corps of Engineers to build and maintain rivers, harbors, and flood control systems across the country
Funds the Bureau of Reclamation, which runs water supply and dam projects mostly in western states
Pays for Department of Energy programs covering nuclear power, renewable energy, electricity grid work, and fossil fuels
Funds cleanup of radioactive waste and old nuclear sites that are no longer in use
Pays to maintain the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, a government stockpile of oil held for national emergencies
Funds nuclear weapons and defense programs run by the National Nuclear Security Administration
Pays the budgets of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission

118-hr-8812.one_liner: Fund and update Army Corps of Engineers water and flood projects across the country
provisions: Approves new Army Corps of Engineers projects to improve rivers, ports, and harbors so ships can move through them more easily
Funds projects to reduce flood damage in communities near rivers and coasts
Pays for work to restore wetlands, fish habitats, and other water ecosystems
Supports building and fixing water supply systems, dams, and wastewater infrastructure
Cancels approval for some older water projects that were never built

118-hr-897.one_liner: Make an underwater cypress forest in the Gulf of Mexico a protected federal sanctuary
provisions: Makes an underwater cypress forest in the Gulf of Mexico off the Alabama coast a federally protected sanctuary.
Cutting, removing, or digging up any of the cypress trees in the sanctuary becomes illegal.
Using dredging equipment, drills, explosives, or laying cables on the seafloor in the sanctuary becomes illegal.
Fishing, diving, mooring, and other recreational or commercial water activities are still allowed in the sanctuary.
Building artificial reefs to improve fishing or diving in the area is still allowed.
Oil and gas projects that were approved before this bill passes can continue operating in the sanctuary.
The federal ocean agency (NOAA) must create a full management plan and set up an advisory council for the sanctuary.

118-hr-8774.one_liner: Fund the U.S. military for the year starting October 2024
provisions: Pays the salaries and benefits for active-duty troops across all military branches
Covers day-to-day costs of running the military, like fuel, repairs, and training exercises
Buys new weapons, vehicles, aircraft, and other equipment for the military
Funds research to develop new weapons, technology, and defense systems
Pays for health care for troops and their families through the military's health program
Funds military efforts to stop illegal drugs from entering the country
Funds retirement and disability payments for CIA workers

118-hr-8998.one_liner: Fund national parks, the EPA, tribal programs, and the arts for 2025
provisions: Gives money to the National Park Service, which runs more than 400 parks and historic sites across the country, to keep them staffed and open.
Funds the Environmental Protection Agency to keep running programs that set rules for air and water quality.
Gives money to the Bureau of Indian Affairs and Bureau of Indian Education, which run services and schools for Native American tribes.
Funds the Indian Health Service, which provides healthcare to about 2.6 million Native Americans and Alaska Natives.
Gives money to arts and culture organizations including the Smithsonian Institution, the Kennedy Center, the National Endowment for the Arts, and the National Endowment for the Humanities.
Includes a rule that lets the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians buy back land that was historically theirs.
Sets rules for how all of the money in this bill can and cannot be spent.

118-hres-1316.one_liner: Allow the House to vote on spending bills for Defense, State, and Homeland Security
provisions: Lets the full House vote on a spending bill for the Department of Defense for the year ending September 30, 2025
Lets the full House vote on a spending bill for the Department of State and foreign aid programs for the year ending September 30, 2025
Lets the full House vote on a spending bill for the Department of Homeland Security for the year ending September 30, 2025

118-hr-9456.one_liner: Require security reviews when people from China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea buy U.S. farmland
provisions: When a person from China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea tries to buy U.S. farmland, USDA must report that deal to a national security committee.
That committee, called CFIUS, decides if the deal is a security risk and whether to do a full review.
CFIUS can block or set conditions on a deal if it finds the purchase puts national security at risk.
The U.S. Secretary of Agriculture gets a seat on CFIUS when deals involve farmland, farm technology, or farm businesses.
This rule also covers farm storage, transportation, and food processing businesses, not just land.

118-hres-1341.one_liner: Schedule House votes on voter ID, school sex discrimination, and appliance energy rules
provisions: Lets the House vote on a bill that would require people to show proof of U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections.
Lets the House vote on a measure that would cancel a Department of Education rule on sex discrimination in schools and colleges that get federal money.
Lets the House vote on a spending bill that funds the U.S. Congress for the year ending September 2025.
Lets the House vote on a bill that would stop the Department of Energy from setting energy rules for dishwashers.
Lets the House vote on a bill that would stop the Department of Energy from setting energy rules for refrigerators and freezers.

118-hr-9076.one_liner: Keep funding for child welfare and foster care programs running through 2029
provisions: Keeps money flowing to child welfare programs through September 2029
Requires 3 out of every 100 dollars in child welfare funding to go directly to Native American tribes
Lets foster youth who are 18 or older choose to have caseworker visits done over video call instead of in person
Creates grants for states to test new ways to help foster children stay connected to a parent who is in prison
Requires the government to look at how much time state child welfare workers spend on paperwork and find ways to reduce it
Keeps funding running for a program that helps courts handle child welfare cases, including through video hearings
Requires a report on what services are available to families after a child is adopted or placed with a guardian

118-hr-9494.one_liner: Fund the government through March 2025 and require proof of citizenship to vote
provisions: The bill keeps the federal government funded at 2024 spending levels through March 28, 2025.
It stops a government shutdown that would have started on October 1, 2024.
It sends extra money to FEMA's disaster relief fund for people affected by natural disasters.
It sends extra money to the Navy's Virginia Class Submarine building program.
It keeps the National Flood Insurance Program running so homeowners can still buy flood insurance.
It extends farm livestock price reporting, federal timber sale rules, and the military's ability to fund certain building projects through March 2025.
Anyone registering to vote in a federal election must now show documents proving U.S. citizenship.

118-hres-1367.one_liner: Create a House task force to investigate the July 2024 Trump assassination attempt
provisions: Sets up a group of up to 11 House members to look into the July 13, 2024 shooting in Butler, Pennsylvania
Up to 5 of the 11 members are picked with input from the minority party leader
The task force can take sworn statements and issue legal orders to get documents and testimony
All relevant House committee records must be handed over within 7 days
The task force must release a final report by December 13, 2024
The report must include steps Congress could take to stop future security failures

118-hres-1370.one_liner: Set debate rules for two spending bills covering energy, water, and the environment
provisions: This rule allows the House to debate and vote on two separate spending bills.
The first bill covers money for energy and water programs for the year ending September 30, 2025.
The second bill covers money for the Department of the Interior and environment programs for the same year.
The rule sets limits on how long House members can speak during debate on each bill.
The rule controls which changes members are allowed to propose to each bill during debate.

118-hres-1371.one_liner: Put Congress on record condemning Biden Administration border policies
provisions: Congress formally states its disapproval of how the Biden Administration handled the southern border.
The resolution names Kamala Harris as the person in the Biden Administration responsible for border security.
This is a statement only — it does not change any laws, rules, or spending.

118-hres-1376.one_liner: Let the House debate a resolution about Biden's border record
provisions: This resolution sets the rules for bringing H. Res. 1371 to a vote on the House floor.
H. Res. 1371 condemns how the Biden administration handled the U.S. southern border.
This bill does not change any law, create any program, or spend any money.
It is a procedural step that controls how long the House can debate the resolution and whether changes to it are allowed.

118-hres-1344.one_liner: Declare the Attorney General in contempt of Congress for ignoring a subpoena
provisions: The House of Representatives voted to find Attorney General Merrick Garland in contempt of Congress.
Contempt of Congress means Garland did not comply with a legal order from the House to hand over documents.
The legal order — called a subpoena — was connected to a House investigation.
After a contempt vote, Congress can send the case to the Justice Department to decide whether to bring criminal charges.
The vote itself does not immediately remove or penalize Garland from his position.

118-s-1146.one_liner: Require federal help to states for finding and protecting missing foster kids
provisions: The Children's Bureau must give states and tribes information and tools to find children who go missing from foster care.
The bureau must review how states and tribes track missing foster children and identify what works best.
The bureau must help states screen children who were missing and returned to foster care for signs of sex trafficking.
Children already in foster care who are at risk of sex trafficking must also be assessed under this bill.

118-hres-901.one_liner: Express US support for democracy and human rights in Pakistan
provisions: The US government states it supports free and fair elections in Pakistan
The resolution calls on the President to work with Pakistan on democracy and human rights
It calls on Pakistan to protect democratic institutions and the rule of law

118-s-227.one_liner: Add two cities to the list of places where federal courts must hold sessions
provisions: Courts in the Pecos Division of the Western District of Texas must now hold sessions in Alpine, Texas.
Courts in the Western District of Washington must now hold sessions in Mount Vernon, Washington.
People in those areas can now go to a federal court closer to home instead of traveling to a more distant city.

118-s-2861.one_liner: Award Billie Jean King a Congressional Gold Medal
provisions: Gives Billie Jean King a Congressional Gold Medal for her work in advancing equal rights for women in sports and education.
The medal is one of the highest awards Congress can give to a civilian.

118-s-3706.one_liner: Let family members and guardians collect money owed to crime victims in court
provisions: When a crime victim is under 18, disabled, or has died, a parent, guardian, or family member can collect court-ordered payments from the convicted person on the victim's behalf.
The person stepping in for the victim can be repaid for money they lost from work, travel costs, and child care while helping with the investigation or going to court hearings.
They can also be repaid for costs of transporting the victim to get medical care, physical therapy, or other treatment.

118-s-3249.one_liner: Name a VA clinic in Kansas City, Kansas after Captain Elwin Shopteese
provisions: The VA outpatient clinic at 9201 Parallel Parkway in Kansas City, Kansas gets a new official name: the Captain Elwin Shopteese VA Clinic.
Captain Elwin Shopteese was a U.S. Army veteran from Kansas honored by Congress for his military service.
This name change applies only to this one clinic in Wyandotte County — no other VA buildings or locations are renamed.

118-hres-1430.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress debates six separate bills
provisions: This resolution sets the time limits and debate rules for six different bills being considered in the House
One of the six bills would create a program to track and respond to actions by China's government
One bill would require the Senate to vote to approve any global pandemic agreement before it becomes binding on the U.S.
One bill would cut federal money to colleges that have ties to Confucius Institutes, which are programs funded by the Chinese government
One bill would remove the $7,500 electric vehicle tax credit for cars with batteries that use materials from certain foreign countries, including China
One bill would add new rules on foreign governments buying farmland in the U.S.
One bill would keep the federal government funded through the end of 2025

118-hres-1455.one_liner: Set debate rules for seven bills on education, finance, trade, immigration, and environment
provisions: Sets the rules for how the House of Representatives will debate and vote on seven separate bills
One bill stops college accreditors from requiring schools to pass political tests to keep their accreditation
One bill changes what information public companies must share with investors and creates a new advisory committee
One bill keeps 'Made in West Bank or Gaza' labels on imported goods from those areas
One bill limits what retirement fund managers can consider when making investment choices
One bill cuts federal money to cities or states that give benefits to people who are in the country without legal status
People who have been convicted of or committed sex offenses or domestic violence can be denied entry to or removed from the U.S.
One resolution cancels an EPA rule that set pollution limits for cars and trucks made in 2027 and later

117-hr-2020.one_liner: Create a public website showing how federal disaster aid money is spent
provisions: The federal government must put disaster aid spending data in one place online where anyone can look it up.
The Small Business Administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and any other agency that gives out disaster aid must update this information every three months.
Each agency must show the total amount of money it gave out, how much of that money was actually spent, and what it was spent on.

117-hr-2377.one_liner: Let federal courts order people to give up their guns if a judge finds they pose a risk
provisions: A family member or police officer can ask a federal court to take away someone's guns if they think that person is dangerous to themselves or others.
A judge can issue an order that stops a person from buying, having, or receiving guns or bullets.
People who are under one of these court orders get added to the list of people who are not allowed to own guns under federal law.

117-hr-224.one_liner: Rename a Houston post office after Vanessa Guillén
provisions: Changes the official name of the post office at 5302 Galveston Road in Houston, Texas to the Vanessa Guillén Post Office Building
Vanessa Guillén was a U.S. Army soldier from Houston who was murdered at Fort Hood, Texas in 2020
Her death led to a federal law called the I Am Vanessa Guillén Act, which changed how the military handles reports of sexual harassment and assault

117-hr-209.one_liner: Rename a post office in Pontotoc, Mississippi after Lance Corporal Marc Lucas Tucker
provisions: Changes the official name of the post office at 305 Highway 15 North in Pontotoc, Mississippi to the 'Lance Corporal Marc Lucas Tucker Post Office Building'

117-hr-207.one_liner: Rename a post office in Amory, Mississippi after Command Sergeant Major Lawrence Kennedy
provisions: Renames the post office at 215 1st Avenue in Amory, Mississippi after Command Sergeant Major Lawrence E. 'Rabbit' Kennedy.
Command Sergeant Major is the highest rank an enlisted soldier can reach in the U.S. Army.
The building keeps the same address and all post office services stay the same.

117-hr-2773.one_liner: Fund state programs that protect wildlife and plants at risk of dying out
provisions: Gives money to states, territories, and Washington D.C. to protect animals and plants that are at risk of dying out
The Department of the Interior runs a grant program using part of this money
Grants go to new efforts to help endangered or threatened species, or to protect the places where those species live
States can also use the money for wildlife education and outdoor recreation projects

117-hr-2543.one_liner: Require the Federal Reserve to track and reduce racial gaps in jobs and wealth
provisions: Tells the Federal Reserve to do its work in a way that reduces gaps in jobs, income, wealth, and access to loans between racial and ethnic groups
Requires the Federal Reserve to release reports showing where gaps exist in employment between different racial and ethnic groups
Requires the Federal Reserve to share its plans for how it will work to close those gaps over time

117-hr-2724.one_liner: Assign peer support specialists to veterans filing military sexual trauma claims
provisions: The VA must assign a peer support specialist to each veteran who files a military sexual trauma claim.
Veterans can say no if they do not want a specialist assigned to them.
Each specialist must be trained as a victim advocate.
The specialist cannot have any role in deciding whether the veteran's claim is approved or denied.

117-hr-2499.one_liner: Give federal firefighters workers' compensation for job-related illnesses
provisions: Federal firefighters, paramedics, EMTs, and hazmat workers who get heart disease, lung disease, or certain cancers are automatically covered by workers' compensation — without having to prove the job caused the illness.
To qualify, the worker must have worked in fire protection for at least 5 years and be diagnosed within 10 years of starting the job.
Workers who catch a disease during a declared pandemic or a chronic infectious disease tied to job hazards are covered regardless of how long they have worked.
Workers' compensation covers both disability and death caused by these illnesses.
Covered workers include anyone whose main job is fire suppression — including firefighters, paramedics, EMTs, rescue workers, ambulance staff, and hazmat workers.

117-hr-2992.one_liner: Create training tools to help police respond to people with brain injuries or PTSD
provisions: The Bureau of Justice Assistance must create training tools to help police and other first responders work with people who have brain injuries or PTSD.
At least one police department named as a Law Enforcement Mental Health Learning Site must use these tools.
The tools must be added to an existing resource called the Police-Mental Health Collaboration Toolkit.
The CDC must study how often first responders get concussions and report back on what they find.

117-hr-3508.one_liner: Name a Honeoye Falls post office after Army Chief Warrant Officer Christian Koch
provisions: The post office at 39 West Main Street in Honeoye Falls, New York gets a new official name.
That name is the CW4 Christian J. Koch Memorial Post Office.
CW4 stands for Chief Warrant Officer 4, a senior Army rank.

117-hr-4693.one_liner: Direct USAID to run programs that prevent and treat malnutrition in other countries
provisions: USAID must work through a government-wide plan called the Global Nutrition Coordination Plan to guide how U.S. money for nutrition is spent.
USAID must pick which countries get help based on malnutrition data, and must update that list within five years.
USAID can create a group inside the agency called the Nutrition Leadership Council to keep all its nutrition work coordinated.
USAID can direct food and health help to the people most at risk of severe malnutrition.
USAID can work with UN agencies, private companies, and local groups to help partner countries build their own nutrition programs.
USAID must send Congress a plan and yearly reports on how these programs are running.
All these programs end seven years after the law is signed.

117-hr-4133.one_liner: Fund security and disaster programs in Caribbean countries
provisions: Sends money to Caribbean countries to help with public safety and fighting crime
Requires the State Department to make a plan for helping Caribbean countries prepare for and respond to disasters
The plan must include steps that can be measured to show progress
The State Department must submit a timeline and list of goals for carrying out the plan
Requires reports to track whether the money is being used and goals are being met

117-hr-3807.one_liner: Add $60 billion to a fund that gives money to restaurants hurt by COVID-19
provisions: Adds $60 billion to the Restaurant Revitalization Fund, a program that gives money directly to restaurants and other food and drink businesses
This fund was created to help these businesses recover from losses during the COVID-19 pandemic
Businesses can apply for grants — money they do not have to pay back — to cover costs like rent, payroll, and supplies

117-hr-3344.one_liner: Help Central and Eastern European countries secure their phone and internet networks
provisions: The State Department will help Central and Eastern European countries make their phone and internet networks more secure.
Projects that get U.S. support must use only safe equipment — Chinese equipment is not allowed.
If a country's network already uses Chinese equipment, it must replace that equipment to qualify.
The State Department will give diplomatic support and push international banks to invest in these projects.
U.S. agencies — including a government bank called the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation — will help fund studies and cover project costs.
Projects must meet international standards and be financially sustainable.
Projects must also help connect telecom networks across the Central and Eastern European region and block interference from foreign actors.

117-hr-5738.one_liner: Require VA medical centers to provide clean breastfeeding rooms for mothers
provisions: Every VA medical center must have a clean room where mothers can breastfeed or pump milk
The room cannot be a bathroom
The room must be easy to find

117-hr-5324.one_liner: Upgrade and expand NOAA's emergency weather radio network
provisions: Keeps NOAA Weather Radio working in areas with no or weak cell service
Makes sure broadcast towers and antennas get regular repairs and upkeep
Adds the ability to broadcast non-weather emergency alerts through the radio network
Puts real-time weather warnings online so more people can access them
Requires NOAA to study how many people can and cannot reach the weather radio network

117-hr-496.one_liner: Count Russia's actions in occupied Ukraine when rating its record on religious freedom
provisions: When the U.S. government decides whether to label Russia a country that violates religious freedom, it must now look at what is happening in the parts of Ukraine that Russia controls.
Russia can be put on a U.S. watchlist if it is found to be violating religious freedom — that label can lead to the U.S. pulling certain aid or taking other actions against Russia.

117-hr-5658.one_liner: Require DHS to report on who handles cyber attacks and how
provisions: The Department of Homeland Security must write a report explaining which parts of the agency are in charge of responding to cyber attacks.
DHS must work with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency when putting together the report.

117-hr-5129.one_liner: Extend and update a federal program that funds local antipoverty services
provisions: Keeps the Community Services Block Grant program running through 2031.
Opens up services to families earning up to twice the federal poverty level.
That is roughly $62,400 for a family of four in 2024, up from about $31,200.
Changes how the program is run and how results are measured.
Updates how money is divided among states, tribes, and territories.

117-hr-5754.one_liner: Create an online system for veterans to file and track complaints with VA patient advocates
provisions: The Veterans Health Administration must build an online system where veterans can file complaints with a patient advocate without going in person.
Veterans or someone acting on their behalf — like a family member or representative — can file and check the status of complaints through the system.
Right now, there is no standard electronic way to file or track these complaints; this bill requires one to be created.

117-hr-5900.one_liner: Rename a Los Angeles post office after Marine Corps Reserve Private Jacob Cruz
provisions: Renames the post office at 2016 East 1st Street in Los Angeles, California, to the Marine Corps Reserve PVT Jacob Cruz Post Office.
The name change is ceremonial and does not affect post office operations or services.
Jacob Cruz served in the United States Marine Corps Reserve and is being honored by this designation.

117-hr-5914.one_liner: Move a senior fraud protection grant program to a new agency and extend it to 2028
provisions: Keeps a grant program running that gives money to states to protect older Americans from financial fraud, through 2028.
Moves the program from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Creates a task force to watch over how the program runs.
Removes some of the rules that states had to meet before they could get grant money.

117-hr-5911.one_liner: Let people with old criminal records work at banks and credit unions without special permission
provisions: Right now, banks and credit unions must get special permission from the government before hiring someone convicted of certain crimes involving dishonesty or fraud.
This bill removes that requirement if 7 or more years have passed since the crime happened.
It also removes the requirement if 5 or more years have passed since the person was released from jail or prison.
If the crime was committed before the person turned 21 and it has been at least 30 months since sentencing, no special permission is needed.
If a person's criminal record was erased, sealed, or pardoned, they can be hired without special permission.

117-hr-5879.one_liner: Change the rules for when small businesses in low-income areas get a price advantage on government contracts
provisions: The HUBZone program lets small businesses in certain low-income areas compete for government contracts.
Right now, these businesses can get a price preference, meaning the government can pay up to 10% more to choose them over a larger competitor.
This bill changes the rules for when that price preference applies during the bidding process.

117-hr-6064.one_liner: Order a review of VA disability claim exams for veterans who experienced military sexual trauma
provisions: The VA must ask a national science group to review the medical exams used when veterans who were sexually assaulted file for disability pay.
The review covers exams for both mental and physical conditions tied to sexual assault during military service.
The science group must write a report on what it finds.
The VA must then write its own report on what steps it plans to take based on those findings.

117-hr-6052.one_liner: Require VA employees to take training on working with the Inspector General
provisions: All VA employees must complete training on how to report wrongdoing to the Inspector General.
The training also covers how to respond to requests from the Inspector General's office.
Employees learn what it means to cooperate with Inspector General investigations.
The Inspector General's office creates and manages this training.

117-hr-6087.one_liner: Let nurse practitioners and physician assistants treat injured federal workers
provisions: Right now, only doctors can treat injured federal government workers under the workers' compensation program. This bill lets nurse practitioners and physician assistants do that job too.
Nurse practitioners and physician assistants would be able to recommend treatment and prescribe medicine to injured federal workers.
They could also fill out paperwork certifying what the injury is and how long the worker might be unable to do their job.
They could take part in required medical exams alongside a doctor from the Department of Labor.

117-hr-6089.one_liner: Add armed drones to the weapons covered by U.S. Iran sanctions
provisions: U.S. law already puts penalties on people or companies that supply certain weapons to Iran — this bill adds armed drones to that list.
These penalties — called sanctions — can include travel bans, frozen bank accounts, and being blocked from doing business with American companies.
The law targets both individuals and organizations that give or sell armed drones to Iran.

117-hr-6270.one_liner: Create a grant program to plan and build landing pads for new small aircraft
provisions: The Department of Transportation can give planning money to local governments, airports, and transit agencies.
These groups would plan where to build vertiports — landing pads for small aircraft that take off straight up.
Plans must identify locations for vertiports and list available sources of money to pay for them.
If the FAA approves at least two new aircraft models, DOT can give money for construction.
Construction money can cover design costs, environmental studies, and other building expenses.
No grants can be given out after September 30, 2023.

117-hr-6386.one_liner: Rename a post office in Schaumburg, Illinois, to the Veterans of Iraq and Afghanistan Memorial Post Office Building
provisions: Changes the official name of the post office at 450 West Schaumburg Road in Schaumburg, Illinois, to the 'Veterans of Iraq and Afghanistan Memorial Post Office Building'
The post office keeps its address at 450 West Schaumburg Road and continues to operate the same way
No money is spent and no new programs are created by this name change
No further government action is needed once the bill passes

117-hr-6824.one_liner: Create an annual cybersecurity contest for U.S. government workers with cash prizes
provisions: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) runs a yearly competition open to U.S. government employees and teams.
Winners can receive cash prizes.
CISA can work with outside experts and organizations to help design and run the contest.
CISA can partner with nonprofits, private companies, or state and local agencies to manage the competition.
Money for the contest can come from Congress, other federal agencies, states, tribal governments, nonprofits, and private companies.

117-hr-6376.one_liner: Let more student veterans qualify for VA work-study pay
provisions: Right now, veterans must be enrolled at least three-quarter time to get paid through the VA work-study program.
This bill lowers that requirement to half-time, so more veterans can qualify.
Veterans can use the work-study program while they go to school, or are in a training or rehabilitation program.
The work-study program lets veterans earn money by doing jobs for the VA or on campus while they study.

117-hr-6531.one_liner: Track which communities get federal money and push more toward the poorest areas
provisions: The Census Bureau must publish a list of areas where poverty has stayed high for many years, and update it every year.
A federal office must create a plan to send more federal money to these high-poverty areas.
The same federal office must report to Congress every year on how much money went to these areas.
A government watchdog group must review the plan and report on whether more money is actually reaching the poorest communities.

117-hr-6604.one_liner: Help veterans get their GI Bill benefits back if their school closed
provisions: If a veteran's school closes or loses approval, the VA must let them sign a written statement saying they transferred fewer than 12 credits from that school
Once a veteran signs that statement, the VA must accept it as proof and restore their full GI Bill time — meaning they don't lose the months they spent at the closed school
The VA must send veterans a certificate showing they still have their full education benefit available to use
If a veteran actually transferred 12 or more credits, they do not get the benefit restored and the VA takes back the certificate
The VA must contact veterans who qualify for this process and tell them how to apply

117-hr-6873.one_liner: Create a DHS office to prevent bombing attacks in the US
provisions: Creates a new office inside the Department of Homeland Security focused on stopping bomb attacks
The office gives advice on explosive threats and helps different parts of DHS work together on the issue
Provides help to businesses and the public on how to protect important places and large events from bomb threats
Makes sure different agencies share information about research on stopping explosive attacks

117-hr-6825.one_liner: Update and extend the federal grant program that helps nonprofits pay for security
provisions: Keeps the program running and funded through 2028.
Requires FEMA to create a new office, run by a senior FEMA official, to manage the program.
The new office will reach out to nonprofits, answer questions, and help groups apply for grants.
FEMA must publish grant rules, and can stop states from closing their application windows before those rules come out.

117-hr-6871.one_liner: Change how the Department of Homeland Security buys goods and services
provisions: Gives the DHS Under Secretary for Management the job of overseeing all purchases and contracts for the department
Sets new rules for what the DHS money officer and technology officer must do when the department buys things
Creates a new office inside DHS called the Program Accountability and Risk Management Office to track spending and flag problems

117-hr-6891.one_liner: Block Russian government officials from major international finance meetings
provisions: Tells the Treasury Department and the Federal Reserve to keep Russian government officials out of major international finance meetings, as much as legally possible.
This covers meetings like the World Bank, International Monetary Fund, Group of 20, and Bank for International Settlements.
This rule lasts up to five years.
It ends earlier once the President tells Congress Russia has stopped its actions against Ukraine and 30 days have passed.

117-hr-6868.one_liner: Create a grant program to teach cybersecurity in K-12 schools
provisions: Lets a federal agency called CISA give money to schools, cities, colleges, and nonprofits to teach students about cybersecurity and how to stay safe online
Schools from kindergarten through 12th grade can apply for this money
States, local governments, colleges, and nonprofit groups can also apply for funding

117-hr-6899.one_liner: Block Russia and Belarus from exchanging their international reserve funds through the IMF
provisions: The U.S. Treasury cannot exchange or trade IMF reserve funds — called Special Drawing Rights — held by Russia or Belarus.
The U.S. must push other IMF member countries to also stop trading these reserve funds with Russia and Belarus.
U.S. representatives at the IMF must vote against giving Russia or Belarus any new reserve fund allocations.
These rules last for five years, or until Russia and Belarus stop acting against Ukraine's independence — whichever comes first.

117-hr-6943.one_liner: Expand disability and death benefits for public safety officers to cover PTSD
provisions: Public safety officers — like police, firefighters, and paramedics — can now get disability payments for PTSD or acute stress disorder.
The condition must come from a traumatic event on the job.
Family members of officers who developed PTSD on duty and later died can receive death benefits.
This expands the Public Safety Officers' Benefits Program, which already covers death, disability, and education benefits for officers hurt or killed on duty.

117-hr-700.one_liner: Rename a post office in Elwood, Illinois after Lawrence M. 'Larry' Walsh Sr.
provisions: Changes the official name of the post office at 303 East Mississippi Avenue in Elwood, Illinois to the "Lawrence M. 'Larry' Walsh Sr. Post Office".
The post office is located in Elwood, Illinois, a village in Will County.
The name honors Lawrence M. 'Larry' Walsh Sr., a local Illinois figure.
No changes are made to how the post office runs, its hours, or its services — this is a name-only change.
The U.S. Postal Service will update the official designation for this location.

117-hr-6961.one_liner: Change how the VA handles claims from veterans who experienced military sexual trauma
provisions: Requires every VA appeals board member to complete yearly training on military sexual trauma before they can decide those cases
Requires the VA to quickly identify when an appeal involves a military sexual trauma claim and whether the veteran asked for a hearing
Requires the VA to review the letters it sends to veterans when denying military sexual trauma claims and rewrite any language that could cause more harm
Requires outside medical providers who do exams for these claims to follow specific guidelines for working with trauma survivors

117-hr-6930.one_liner: Let the President seize assets from wealthy people who supported Putin
provisions: For two years after this bill passes, the President can take assets worth more than $5 million from people whose wealth is tied to supporting or corrupt dealings with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The President can only use this power if Russia is still fighting a war in Ukraine and has already placed sanctions on the person for corruption, human rights violations, or actions related to the conflict.
Money from selling seized assets can only go to rebuilding Ukraine after the war, helping Ukrainian refugees, buying weapons for Ukraine's military, or helping the Russian people with aid.

117-hr-7077.one_liner: Let the U.S. Fire Administration investigate major fires and release public reports
provisions: Lets the U.S. Fire Administration send investigators to major fires to find the cause and look at broader safety patterns.
Investigators can include safety specialists, fire engineers, codes experts, researchers, and fire training specialists.
All investigations must be done alongside the right local, state, and federal officials.
After each investigation, the agency must release a public report or contribute findings to another federal agency's report.
The agency can also send investigators to fires with unusual circumstances, even if the damage is less severe than a major fire.

117-hr-7153.one_liner: Require the VA to send Congress a plan for updating its benefits computer systems
provisions: The VA must send Congress a plan for updating the computer systems used to process veterans' benefits claims.
The plan must cover five years, starting in October 2025.
The Veterans Benefits Administration is the part of the VA that handles benefits claims — including disability pay and education support.
Congress receives this plan as a report only — the bill does not include any money to carry out the updates.

117-hr-7066.one_liner: Make US financial companies apply Russia and Belarus sanctions to all businesses they own
provisions: US financial companies must follow all financial sanctions on Russia and Belarus.
Any business they own or control must follow those same sanctions.
Companies must take all steps available to make sure their subsidiaries comply.

117-hr-7081.one_liner: Direct the U.S. to push for Ukraine to stop making debt payments
provisions: Tells the U.S. Treasury to contact major international lending groups and ask them to pause all loan payments Ukraine owes them
Tells the U.S. Treasury to work with other countries to get Ukraine's private and government lenders to also pause payments
Pushes for Ukraine to get lower-interest loans from international financial institutions during this period

117-hr-7211.one_liner: Change how FEMA handles disaster aid requests for small states and rural areas
provisions: Gives FEMA's Small State and Rural Advocate new duties to help states gather and present information when asking for disaster aid
Requires the Government Accountability Office to review how FEMA decides whether to approve a governor's request for major disaster aid
The review focuses on requests for individual assistance, which is aid that goes directly to people affected by a disaster

117-hr-7334.one_liner: Give the government 10 years to pursue COVID loan fraud cases
provisions: The government has 10 years from the date of the fraud to bring criminal charges against someone who cheated on a COVID disaster loan
The government also has 10 years to sue in civil court to recover money lost to COVID disaster loan fraud
Before this bill, the default time limit to bring most federal fraud cases was 5 years
This applies to loans made through the COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan program, which gave out over $390 billion to businesses during the pandemic

117-hr-7311.one_liner: Require the State Department to report to Congress a plan on countering Russia in Africa
provisions: The State Department must write a plan explaining what the U.S. is doing to limit Russia's influence in Africa and send it to Congress.
After the first report, the department must send Congress an update every year.
The law covers Russia's government, military, intelligence agencies, private military companies, and other groups working on Russia's behalf in Africa.

117-hr-7276.one_liner: Require the President to report to Congress on war crimes in Ukraine
provisions: Requires the President to send Congress a report on atrocities that have happened during Russia's invasion of Ukraine since February 24, 2022.
The report must describe what the U.S. government has done to collect and save evidence of war crimes.
The report must describe efforts to make Russian citizens, soldiers, and leaders aware that people are being identified for prosecution.
The report must explain how courts — in the U.S., other countries, or international — can get evidence from the U.S. government.

117-hr-7314.one_liner: Require regular reports on whether China is helping Russia fight in Ukraine
provisions: The State Department must regularly report to Congress on whether China's government, Communist Party, or companies are helping Russia in Ukraine.
The reports must say whether China is helping Russia avoid financial penalties or restrictions on buying certain goods and technology.
The reports must cover whether China is giving Russia technology to use in its military or spy programs.
The reports must also say whether China is helping Russia spread false stories or propaganda.

117-hr-7309.one_liner: Renew and expand job training, youth employment, and adult education programs
provisions: Keeps job training programs funded through 2028
Raises the share of business leaders required on state and local workforce boards from 20% to 30%
Creates paid job programs for young people that include job-skills training and mentoring
Expands Job Corps, a free job training program, to serve more people in U.S. territories and removes some age limits
Gives grants to groups of employers in the same industry to build more job training programs
Lets people with criminal records get job training help through new grants focused on reducing repeat offenses
Expands English literacy and job-skills classes to U.S. territories like the Northern Mariana Islands and American Samoa

117-hr-7335.one_liner: Require the VA to coordinate support resources for veterans filing military sexual trauma claims
provisions: Veterans filing a military sexual trauma claim can choose to receive support materials during the process.
Those materials include the Veterans Crisis Line number, mental health appointment info, and other MST help resources.
For veterans who sign up for the notification system, the VA alerts health staff before any exam, hearing, or related event.
The VA also alerts health staff before the veteran gets a final decision on their claim.
The VA must include these support materials with the final decision it sends to the veteran.

117-hr-7500.one_liner: Let the VA build and upgrade specific medical facilities for veterans in 2022
provisions: The VA gets approval to build or make major upgrades to specific medical facilities for veterans during 2022.
Each facility is named individually in the bill — only those specific locations are included, not VA buildings across the country.
The bill sets a dollar cap on each project so the VA cannot spend more than the listed amount on any one job.

117-hr-7375.one_liner: Let the VA send education payments electronically to colleges outside the US
provisions: The Department of Veterans Affairs must update its payment system to send GI Bill and other education money directly to foreign colleges by electronic transfer
Right now, some foreign schools cannot receive VA payments because they lack a US tax ID or a US bank account — this bill fixes that
Veterans attending approved programs at foreign schools would get their education money sent faster and more reliably

117-hr-7372.one_liner: Create a working group to study the war in Ukraine's impact on semiconductor supply chains
provisions: A group of federal agencies will work together to study how Russia's attack on Ukraine has affected semiconductor materials.
The group will report to Congress on shortages of materials like palladium, neon gas, and helium.
The group will study how the war has affected global supply chains and the world economy.
The group will give Congress steps it can take to protect the supply of these materials.
Each year, the group will report to Congress on world events that could disrupt semiconductor supply chains.

117-hr-7352.one_liner: Give prosecutors 10 years to charge fraud on COVID small business loans
provisions: Gives the government up to 10 years to charge someone with fraud on a Paycheck Protection Program loan
The PPP gave out over $800 billion in loans to businesses during COVID-19 to help keep workers paid
Before this bill, the window to bring fraud charges was shorter, which meant some cases could expire before investigators finished their work
Covers both criminal charges and civil cases where the government tries to get money back

117-hr-7667.one_liner: Renew FDA fees and add rules for drug trials and supply chains
provisions: Keeps the FDA's fee programs running through 2027 — these fees are paid by drug and device companies and fund FDA reviews
Requires drug makers to create plans to include more types of people in their medical trials
Requires the FDA to tell generic drug makers, if asked, whether their drug has the same ingredients in the same amounts as the brand-name version
Renews programs that support the development of drugs and devices for children
Sets new rules for checking drug factories and for studies companies must do after a drug is approved
Adds rules for using real-world patient data to help get drugs and devices approved

117-hr-7666.one_liner: Renew and expand federal funding for mental health and addiction programs through 2027
provisions: Keeps funding going through 2027 for mental health programs that serve children, communities, and people with addiction.
Removes the rule that required people to be addicted to opioids for at least one year before they could enter a treatment program.
Adds support for helping people find stable housing while they recover from addiction.
Funds programs to find and treat eating disorders and maternal depression.
Expands mental health services for Native American tribal communities.
Checks that employer-run insurance plans follow federal rules requiring equal coverage for mental and physical health.
Funds programs that add mental health care to regular doctor visits.

117-hr-7622.one_liner: Require small business development centers to offer apprenticeship and job training help
provisions: More than 900 Small Business Development Centers around the country give free or low-cost help to people starting or growing a small business.
This bill adds apprenticeships and work-based learning programs to the list of services every center must offer.
Work-based learning means programs where people learn job skills by doing real work — like apprenticeships, internships, or on-the-job training tied to a small business.

117-hr-7664.one_liner: Tell small business centers to help hire and support career and technical education graduates
provisions: Tells Small Business Development Centers and Women's Business Centers to help small businesses hire graduates from career and technical education programs.
Also tells both types of centers to help those graduates start their own small businesses.

117-hr-7606.one_liner: Create a federal office to investigate unfair practices in the meat and poultry industry
provisions: Creates a new office inside the Department of Agriculture to look into whether meat companies and poultry dealers are breaking competition rules.
Gives the office the power to use subpoenas — legal orders that force companies to hand over documents or answer questions.
The office can take companies to court or start formal government actions against them for breaking the rules.
The office works with the Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission when competition problems come up in food and farming.
The office also talks with the Department of Homeland Security about safety risks in the food supply chain.
The office must hire lawyers and other experts to do this work.

117-hr-7670.one_liner: Require the Small Business Administration to report on contracts given to women-owned small businesses
provisions: The Small Business Administration must report how many contracts were given to women-owned small businesses.
The report must also include the total dollar amount of those contracts.
The Women-Owned Small Business Federal Contracting program sets aside some government contracts for businesses that are at least 51% owned and run by women.

117-hr-7790.one_liner: Give the FDA $28 million to fix the baby formula shortage
provisions: Gives the FDA $28 million in emergency money to respond to the shortage of baby formula.
The money can also be used to prevent future shortages of baby formula and medical foods.
Some of the money goes toward stopping fake or fraudulent baby formula from entering the U.S. market.

117-hr-7688.one_liner: Ban fuel price gouging during declared energy emergencies
provisions: During a declared energy emergency, sellers cannot charge prices that are unreasonably high for gas or other fuels.
The price must also show the seller is taking advantage of the emergency to count as price gouging.
The President can declare an energy emergency and set which fuels and areas are covered, and for how long.
The Federal Trade Commission can take sellers to court and fine them for breaking this rule.
State attorneys general can also enforce this rule in their states.
Fines collected from violators go to a program that helps low-income households pay their heating and cooling bills.

117-hr-7777.one_liner: Create free cybersecurity training for workers who protect industrial systems
provisions: Sets up a free training program inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) for workers who protect industrial systems from hackers
The training covers systems that run factories, power plants, water treatment, and other industrial operations
Workers in the cybersecurity field can take the training at no cost

117-hr-7694.one_liner: Require federal agencies to favor contractors who use small businesses as subcontractors
provisions: When the government picks a company to do a job, it must look at how much of that work the company plans to give to small businesses.
Companies bidding on government contracts must submit a plan showing how much work small businesses will get.
Federal agencies must use that small business plan as one factor when deciding who wins the contract.

117-hr-903.one_liner: Give TSA airport security workers the same job rights as other federal employees
provisions: TSA workers currently operate under a separate set of rules that gives them fewer job protections than most other federal workers. This bill moves them onto the same system used by the rest of the federal government within 180 days.
Workers keep their current pay rates, vacation time, and other rights during the switch.
The TSA must work with the workers' union during the transition.
Bans TSA workers from putting TikTok on government phones.
Requires TSA to hire more veterans, including those with disabilities.
Requires TSA to give workers clear guidance on how to protect themselves from COVID-19.
TSA must talk with groups connected to the Federal Air Marshal Service about issues facing air marshals, including mental health and suicide rates.

117-hr-7910.one_liner: Add new gun rules covering sales to people under 21, ghost guns, and large magazines
provisions: Stops the sale of certain semi-automatic rifles and shotguns to anyone under 21 years old
Creates new federal crimes for selling or moving guns illegally across state lines
Requires guns built at home without serial numbers to be registered and tracked like store-bought guns
Sets rules for how gun owners must store firearms in their homes
Puts bump stocks — devices that make a gun fire faster — under the same rules as other regulated weapons
Bans the import, sale, making, and ownership of magazines that hold large amounts of ammunition

117-hr-847.one_liner: Direct the National Science Foundation to support research on technology that protects digital privacy
provisions: The National Science Foundation is directed to support research on technology that protects digital privacy, chosen through a merit review and competition.
Existing grants for computer security research can now also cover privacy technology and keeping data confidential.
A federal program must send Congress a report on how far privacy technology research has come and what voluntary guides or resources exist.

117-hr-91.one_liner: Name a post office in Easley, South Carolina after Private First Class Barrett Lyle Austin
provisions: This bill gives an official name to the post office at 810 South Pendleton Street in Easley, South Carolina.
The building will be called the "Private First Class Barrett Lyle Austin Post Office Building."
Private First Class is the third enlisted rank in the U.S. Army — one step above the basic rank of Private.

117-hr-7791.one_liner: Give the USDA power to fix baby formula shortages for low-income families
provisions: Lets the USDA step in during emergencies to help families in WIC, a federal food program for low-income mothers and babies.
Requires companies with WIC formula contracts to have a plan for keeping families supplied if their product is recalled.
Requires the USDA to set up a written agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services within 30 days.
The agreement covers how the two agencies share information during formula shortages or recalls.
Lets the USDA temporarily waive WIC rules during emergencies — for example, lifting the monthly limit on how much formula a family can get.
Requires the USDA and state agencies to notify each other when formula supply problems happen.

117-hres-1023.one_liner: Set rules for how the House handles the January 6th Committee report
provisions: Sets the steps the House follows to debate and vote on the January 6th Committee's report
Controls how much time members can speak and what changes can be made during the debate
Applies only to this one report from the committee that investigated the January 6th attack

117-hr-92.one_liner: Name a post office in Pickens, South Carolina after Specialist Four Charles Johnson
provisions: A post office at 110 Johnson Street in Pickens, South Carolina will be officially named the 'Specialist Four Charles Johnson Post Office'.
The name honors Charles Johnson, who held the military rank of Specialist Four.
This is a naming-only action — no money is spent and no rules change.

117-hr-923.one_liner: Impose sanctions on people who commit human rights abuses in Russian-occupied parts of Georgia
provisions: The President must block the U.S. entry and freeze the U.S. assets of people found responsible for human rights abuses in two regions of Georgia that Russia occupies: Abkhazia and South Ossetia.
Every 180 days, the President must send Congress a list of those people.
The State Department must report to Congress on what military help the U.S. gives Georgia and how well Georgia can defend itself.
The State Department must report on cybersecurity work the U.S. and Georgia do together.
The State Department must report on a plan to help Georgia fight false information spread by Russia.

117-hres-1033.one_liner: Set the rules for debating a bill to add money to the restaurant relief fund
provisions: This rule sets the terms for how the House will debate and vote on H.R. 3807.
H.R. 3807 would add money to the Restaurant Revitalization Fund, which was created in 2021 to help restaurants that lost money during COVID-19.
The fund was originally given $28.6 billion, but more restaurants applied than there was money available, leaving many without aid.

117-hr-935.one_liner: Let certain business sale brokers skip federal registration rules
provisions: Brokers who help sell privately owned businesses do not have to register with federal securities regulators if the company they are selling earns below a set dollar amount
This applies only to brokers helping transfer ownership of private companies — not public ones
Brokers who lend money as part of the sale do not get this pass
Brokers involved with shell companies — businesses that exist on paper but have no real operations — do not qualify
Brokers who have had their license suspended or taken away also do not qualify

117-hres-1037.one_liner: Find two former White House officials in contempt of Congress for ignoring subpoenas
provisions: Peter Navarro and Daniel Scavino refused to respond to subpoenas from the committee investigating January 6th
The House votes to hold both men in contempt of Congress
The Speaker of the House sends the contempt findings to federal prosecutors in Washington D.C.
Federal prosecutors can then decide whether to bring criminal charges against Navarro and Scavino

117-hres-1097.one_liner: Set the rules for debating four separate bills in Congress
provisions: This bill sets the time limits and debate rules for bringing four other bills to a vote in the House.
One of those bills would give TSA airport security workers the same job protections as other federal workers.
Another would make it easier for federal firefighters to get benefits if they get sick with certain diseases.
A third would renew a program that gives money to local groups helping people in poverty.
The fourth would send emergency money to Ukraine during the 2022 conflict.

117-hres-1124.one_liner: Set the rules for debating three separate bills in the House
provisions: This bill sets the time limits and voting rules for how the House of Representatives would debate three other bills.
The first bill would create offices inside the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Justice, and the FBI to track and respond to domestic terrorism.
The second bill would set rules against charging too much for gas and other fuels sold to everyday consumers.
The third bill would send emergency money to fix a shortage of baby formula in the United States before September 30, 2022.

117-hres-1119.one_liner: Set the rules for debating three separate bills in Congress
provisions: Decides how long Congress can debate a bill that would send more money to low-income areas
Decides how long Congress can debate a bill that would renew job training programs around the country
Decides how long Congress can debate a bill that would rename a federal courthouse in Tallahassee, Florida after Judge Joseph Woodrow Hatchett

117-hres-1065.one_liner: Set House debate rules for a bill to lend weapons to Ukraine
provisions: This bill sets the rules for how the House will debate and vote on a separate bill called S. 3522.
S. 3522 would let the President sign agreements to lend or lease military equipment to Ukraine.
The military equipment would be used to protect Ukrainian civilians during the Russian invasion.
Ukraine would be expected to pay back or return the equipment after the conflict ends.
This rule does not create any programs, funding, or new laws — it only controls how Congress debates the Ukraine bill.

117-hres-1125.one_liner: Call on leaders to speak out against antisemitism in the US and worldwide
provisions: Calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and community leaders to publicly condemn antisemitism
Calls for more action to fight antisemitism in the United States, in other countries, and on the internet

117-hres-1153.one_liner: Set the rules for Congress to debate two gun safety bills
provisions: Allows Congress to vote on a bill that would let courts take guns from people a judge finds dangerous.
Allows Congress to vote on a bill that would raise the gun-buying age from 18 to 21 for some firearms.
Allows Congress to vote on a bill that would make it a crime to buy a gun for someone else.
Allows Congress to vote on a bill that would require safe storage of guns at home.
Allows Congress to vote on a bill that would make guns without serial numbers illegal.

117-hres-833.one_liner: State U.S. support for Moldova's independence and call on Russia to pull out its troops
provisions: States that the U.S. backs Moldova's right to run its own government and make its own alliances
Supports the U.S.-Moldova talks as a way to build a stronger relationship between the two countries
Calls on Russia to remove its military forces and weapons from Moldova
Tells Russia to stop backing groups inside Moldova that want to break away from the country
Supports finding a peaceful solution to the conflict in the Transnistria region, a strip of land that broke away from Moldova in the 1990s and still has Russian troops in it

117-hres-1191.one_liner: Allow the House to debate three health-related bills
provisions: Opens floor debate on a bill that would let Americans voluntarily share their sexual orientation and gender identity in some federal surveys
Opens floor debate on a bill that would create a new federal health research agency called ARPA-H
Opens floor debate on a bill that would keep funding going for mental health and drug treatment programs
This bill sets the rules for how long each debate lasts and what changes can be proposed — it does not pass the bills itself

117-hres-1170.one_liner: Set debate rules for three bills about the Federal Reserve, wildlife, and farming
provisions: This bill sets the rules for how the House of Representatives will debate three separate bills.
One bill would require the Federal Reserve to collect and report data broken down by race, gender, and other groups.
That same bill would also change the official goals that guide how the Federal Reserve runs.
A second bill would send more money to states to manage animals and plants that are at risk in their area.
A third bill would create a new office inside the Department of Agriculture to look into whether large companies in farming and food are following competition rules.

117-s-2514.one_liner: Rename a Utah veterans center after Col. Gail S. Halvorsen
provisions: Changes the official name of the VA veterans center in Orem, Utah to the Col. Gail S. Halvorsen 'Candy Bomber' Veterans Center

Col. Halvorsen was a U.S. Air Force pilot who dropped candy by parachute for children in Berlin during the 1948–1949 Berlin Airlift, when the Soviet Union blocked food and supplies from reaching the city
The renaming is a formal act by Congress and applies to the VA-operated facility in Orem, Utah

117-s-2520.one_liner: Expand federal help to state and local governments on cybersecurity
provisions: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) will give more help to state, local, tribal, and territorial governments to protect against cyberattacks.
DHS will provide grants and training to help governments understand cyber threats and how to respond when an attack happens.
A DHS center will team up with a group called the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center to run practice drills and teach cybersecurity skills.
DHS will promote cybersecurity education for government workers and the public.
DHS will start a test program that puts sensors on government networks to find and block harmful internet traffic.

117-s-1872.one_liner: Award a Congressional Gold Medal to World War II Army Rangers
provisions: Gives a single Congressional Gold Medal to the U.S. Army Rangers who served in World War II.
The medal is a formal thank-you from Congress for their service during the war.

117-s-1760.one_liner: Name a new VA clinic in Oahu, Hawaii after Daniel Kahikina Akaka
provisions: Gives an official name to a new VA clinic being built in Oahu, Hawaii
The clinic will be called the Daniel Kahikina Akaka VA Clinic

117-s-2102.one_liner: Expand VA mammogram coverage to veterans who served in listed combat zones abroad
provisions: Female veterans who served in Iraq between August 2, 1990 and February 28, 1991, or again from March 19, 2003 onward, can get VA mammograms.
Veterans who served in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar, or other parts of the Southwest Asia region from August 2, 1990 onward can get VA mammograms.
Veterans who served in Afghanistan, Djibouti, Syria, Jordan, Egypt, Lebanon, or Yemen from September 11, 2001 onward can get VA mammograms.
Coverage for all listed locations continues until burn pits — open-air trash fires used by the military — are no longer in use there.
The VA can add more locations and time periods based on its Airborne Hazards and Open Burn Pit Registry.

117-s-2687.one_liner: Give the VA Inspector General power to require witnesses to testify
provisions: The VA's watchdog office can now legally require people to show up and answer questions during investigations.
This subpoena power cannot be used to force witnesses to testify in criminal cases.
Before sending a subpoena, the VA watchdog must notify the Department of Justice and the person being called.
If the Department of Justice says the subpoena would get in the way of an ongoing investigation, the VA watchdog must cancel it.

117-s-2533.one_liner: Expand breast cancer screening and treatment options for veterans through the VA
provisions: The VA must create a plan to improve breast imaging services for veterans.
The VA must run a three-year program to offer mammograms by video for veterans who live far from a VA facility.
The VA must upgrade all mammogram machines at VA facilities to use 3D imaging technology.

The VA must partner with at least one National Cancer Institute cancer center in each regional network, and ensure veterans in rural areas can get cancer care through telehealth if no partner center is nearby.
The VA must update its guidelines to offer more genetic testing and counseling to veterans diagnosed with breast cancer.
The VA must check that a mammogram site can physically accommodate veterans with spinal cord injuries before sending them to a non-VA provider.
