The VA must work with the Department of Defense on shared breast cancer research and care programs and report on those collaborations.

117-s-3527.one_liner: Let the VA move an official facility name to another nearby property
provisions: The VA can move the official name of a building or facility to a different VA property in the same city or local area.
This only applies when Congress originally gave that name to the first property through a law.
The new property must be at a different address or location from the original named property.
The VA cannot use this to rename a facility to something new — only to move an existing congressional name to a new location.

117-s-3522.one_liner: Let the U.S. lend weapons and military equipment to Ukraine faster
provisions: Lets the U.S. government lend or lease military equipment to Ukraine without the usual rules that slow the process down
Removes the normal five-year limit on how long the U.S. can lend military equipment to Ukraine
Removes the rule requiring Ukraine to pay the U.S. back for the cost of leasing the equipment
Takes away Congress's ability to block these equipment transfers while the law is active
Stays in effect until the Russia-Ukraine conflict — which started with Russia taking Crimea in 2014 — ends and Russian troops pull back to where they were before March 1, 2021
Requires the President to set up a fast-track system to get the equipment to Ukraine quickly

117-s-3580.one_liner: Stop ocean carriers from refusing cargo and using unfair shipping methods
provisions: Changes the rules that govern ocean shipping to support the growth of U.S. exports.
Stops ocean carriers, marine terminal operators, and ocean transportation intermediaries from turning away cargo when space is available on their ships.
Stops those same carriers and operators from using unfair methods in ocean shipping.

117-s-4089.one_liner: Protect veterans' retraining benefits if their school closes or loses approval
provisions: If a veteran's school closed or lost approval, the VA cannot count that time against their training benefits.
This applies when the veteran could not finish because of the closure or disapproval.
The protected time equals the full amount of training time the veteran was enrolled.
Schools that close or lose approval cannot receive any more payments from this program.
Any payments a closed or disapproved school already received become money owed back to the government.

117-s-4160.one_liner: Lets Supreme Court Police protect the families of justices and court officers
provisions: Before this bill, Supreme Court Police could only protect the justices and court officers themselves — not their families.
This bill lets the Marshal of the Supreme Court decide when to protect the immediate family members of any Supreme Court justice or court officer.
The Marshal and the Supreme Court Police can now act to protect those family members if the Marshal decides protection is needed.

117-s-516.one_liner: Create a federal working group to plan for new small aircraft that carry people and cargo
provisions: The Department of Transportation must create a group of agencies to work together on a new type of air travel called Advanced Air Mobility (AAM).
AAM includes small aircraft, like air taxis, that can take off and land in cities, rural areas, and everywhere in between.
The working group will plan for safety rules, buildings and landing pads, protection from hackers, and how much federal money to spend on this.
The group will coordinate how these new aircraft fit into the airspace already used by planes and helicopters.

117-s-497.one_liner: Create a committee to help run grants for fishing communities
provisions: Creates a new committee under the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to help manage a grant program for fishing communities.
Divides the committee into six regional groups so different parts of the country are represented.
Committee members come from different parts of the fishing industry, chosen by region.
The committee finds out what fishing communities need, writes up grant proposals, reviews applications, and sends them to NOAA for final approval.

117-s-3823.one_liner: Raise the debt limits for people and small businesses filing for bankruptcy
provisions: Keeps the higher debt limit for small businesses filing for bankruptcy — the limit was temporarily raised to $7.5 million and this bill makes that permanent
Adjusts that $7.5 million limit over time so it keeps up with inflation
Lets a small business that is connected to a publicly traded company still use this type of bankruptcy
If a small business owner stops running their company during bankruptcy, a court-appointed trustee can take over running it
Raises the debt limit for individuals filing under Chapter 13 bankruptcy, which is a repayment plan for wage earners
Combines the two separate debt limits for individuals — one for secured debt (like a mortgage) and one for unsecured debt (like credit cards) — into one single limit

118-hjres-136.one_liner: Cancel EPA pollution rules for cars and trucks made in 2027 and later
provisions: Cancels a rule the EPA published on April 18, 2024 about pollution from cars, trucks, and SUVs.
The cancelled rule set limits on greenhouse gas emissions for vehicles made starting in 2027.
The cancelled rule included rules about how long batteries in electric and hybrid cars must last.
The cancelled rule changed how fuel economy is measured for these vehicles.

118-hr-1449.one_liner: Require more frequent lease sales and faster permits for geothermal energy on federal land
provisions: The federal government must now hold lease sales for geothermal energy land at least once a year.
Before this bill, sales were required only once every two years.
If a sale is canceled or delayed, a replacement sale must happen within the same year.
When someone applies for a permit to drill for geothermal energy, the government has 30 days to say whether the application is complete.
After telling the applicant the application is complete, the government has 30 days to make a final decision on the permit.

118-hr-3012.one_liner: Keep funding programs that support human rights and free information in North Korea
provisions: Funds grants to groups working on human rights and free press inside North Korea through 2028
Pays for radio and other broadcasts that send uncensored news into North Korea
Gives money to groups helping North Koreans who have left the country without government permission

117-s-66.one_liner: Order a federal assessment and plan to address algae blooms in South Florida waters
provisions: A group of federal agencies must study algae blooms and low-oxygen water conditions in South Florida.
The group must submit a plan for reducing and controlling those conditions in the region.
The bill covers algae events that make water toxic or starve fish of oxygen, setting the scope for the federal review.

117-s-812.one_liner: Require annual reports on U.S. efforts to get Taiwan into World Health Organization meetings
provisions: The State Department must include more detail in its yearly reports about Taiwan's efforts to join World Health Organization meetings as an observer.
China has blocked Taiwan from joining these meetings, which is why the U.S. tracks its own efforts to help.
After any meeting where Taiwan was not allowed in, the report must describe what changed or improved in the U.S. plan to get Taiwan a seat.
The report covers the World Health Assembly, which is the main decision-making meeting of the World Health Organization.

118-hr-3208.one_liner: Create a cybersecurity job training program for DHS employees
provisions: Sets up a training program inside the DHS cybersecurity agency known as CISA.
DHS workers who are not already in cybersecurity jobs can join the program to learn cybersecurity skills.
The program follows a national standard called the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education Framework.
Each year, CISA must send Congress a report on the program.
The report shows how many people joined, what jobs they moved into, and other key details.

118-hr-390.one_liner: Expand the Hudson River Valley Heritage Area to cover two more counties in New York
provisions: Adds the rest of Saratoga County and all of Washington County in New York to the Hudson River Valley Heritage Area
This area covers land along the Hudson River that has historic and cultural significance
A local organization manages this area with support and some funding from the federal government
The expansion gives these two counties access to the same recognition and resources the rest of the heritage area already has

118-hr-5342.one_liner: Change how Social Security calculates benefits for people who also get a government pension
provisions: Some government workers — like certain teachers, firefighters, and police — pay into a pension instead of Social Security. A current rule called the WEP cuts their Social Security check when they retire.
This bill changes the math used to calculate those cuts, basing the reduction on what share of a person's career earnings went into Social Security.
People who retire between 2025 and 2067 get whichever calculation gives them the higher monthly payment.
People retiring after 2067 will only use the new formula.
Some people already affected by the current rule get an extra one-time or ongoing payment.
The Social Security Administration must add non-covered earnings to the yearly statements it sends workers.

118-hr-3334.one_liner: Ban Chinese Communist Party leaders and their families from entering the U.S.
provisions: The top ruling body of the Chinese Communist Party, called the Central Committee, has about 376 members — this bill bans all of them from getting visas to enter the United States.
Adult family members of those Central Committee members are also banned from getting U.S. visas.
Any money or property those people have in the United States gets frozen — they cannot spend it or move it.
The President can pause these sanctions for up to 30 days at a time by notifying Congress that China has changed course on four actions.

To pause the sanctions, the President must confirm that China has stopped carrying out genocide against Uyghur Muslims, threatening Taiwan, weakening Hong Kong's self-rule, and stealing American business ideas and inventions.
Any presidential pause must be posted publicly on a U.S. government website.

118-hr-4790.one_liner: Limit what information public companies must share with investors
provisions: Companies only have to share information with investors if the company itself decides that information affects buying or voting decisions about its stock.
The SEC must post on its website a list of every disclosure companies are currently required to make that does not affect investment decisions, along with a reason for each one.
The SEC must send that list to Congress every five years.
A company cannot be sued for not sharing information that does not affect investment decisions.
Creates a new group inside the SEC, made up of public company officials and advisors, to give the SEC advice on its rules and company policies.
The SEC must study and report on how European Union sustainability rules affect U.S. companies, consumers, and investors.

118-hr-5658.one_liner: Require tracking barcodes on all mail-in ballots
provisions: Mail-in ballots must have a U.S. Postal Service barcode so voters and officials can track each ballot.
Ballot envelopes must meet postal design rules so machines can process them.
Each ballot must show the official election mail logo.

118-hr-5349.one_liner: Fund a high school curriculum about communism and totalitarianism
provisions: The Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation would create a curriculum for high school students about communism and totalitarianism.
The Foundation would also create oral history resources for students to learn from people who lived under these governments.
The curriculum would explain how these systems differ from U.S. democracy.

118-hr-7073.one_liner: Fund research and testing of new materials and technology for pipelines
provisions: The Department of Energy must run a 5-year program that gives money to test new pipeline technology at different stages of development.
The Department of Energy, the Department of Transportation, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology must work together on research into new materials for pipelines.
The Department of Energy must create a National Pipeline Modernization Center to work with companies on testing and selling new pipeline products.
The National Institute of Standards and Technology must run a research program focused on keeping pipelines safe, secure, and working well.

118-hr-6513.one_liner: Let Congress send official observers to watch how federal elections are run
provisions: House committee chairs can name their employees to watch federal elections as official observers.
States must let these observers into any area where ballots are cast, counted, scanned, or certified.
Observers can watch but cannot touch ballots or election equipment.
Observers cannot campaign for any candidate or take any action that could reveal how a voter voted.
Observers cannot stop a voter from casting a ballot or an election worker from doing their job.
If an observer breaks the rules, election officials can remove them and must notify the House committee in writing.

118-hr-5717.one_liner: Cut federal money to cities refusing to share immigration data or honor federal detention holds
provisions: Cities and states lose federal money if they have rules stopping officials from sharing immigration status.
The money at risk is only the part they planned to spend on people living in the country without legal permission.
They also lose money if they ignore a federal request to hold an immigrant in jail.
They also lose money if they don't tell federal immigration officials before letting an immigrant out of jail.
Crime victims and witnesses are not covered — cities can keep rules that protect them from immigration checks.
This rule starts in the first full budget year after the law is passed.

118-hr-8057.one_liner: Rename a Westminster, California post office after Little Saigon Vietnam War Veterans
provisions: Renames the post office at 9317 Bolsa Avenue in Westminster, California as the 'Little Saigon Vietnam War Veterans Memorial Post Office'
This is a ceremonial name change — no money is spent and no new programs are created
The name honors Vietnamese-American veterans who served in the Vietnam War
Once Congress passes this, only Congress can change the official name of this post office

118-hr-7409.one_liner: Remove federal permit requirements for geothermal drilling on state and private land, not tribal lands
provisions: Geothermal companies drilling on state or private land no longer need a federal drilling permit.
This applies when the U.S. government owns less than 50% of the underground geothermal rights and the company holds a state permit.
These rules do not apply on tribal lands.
These projects no longer need to go through the federal environmental review process.
These projects no longer need a federal check on how they may affect endangered species.
These projects do not need federal historic preservation review unless the state has no state law covering historic properties.

118-hr-8205.one_liner: Apply federal insurance rules to cash bail and bail bond companies
provisions: Cash bail and bail bond companies would have to follow the same federal rules that insurance companies follow.
Right now, bail bond companies are not covered by those federal insurance laws — this bill would change that.
This applies to both criminal bail bonds and immigration bail bonds.

118-hr-7673.one_liner: Limit the Department of Energy's power to set rules on washing machines
provisions: The Department of Energy can only set energy rules for washing machines if the rules are technically possible to meet.
The rules cannot end up costing consumers more money overall.
The rules must save a meaningful amount of energy — not just a small amount.

118-hr-7198.one_liner: Require federal agencies to study how proposed rules affect small businesses before finalizing them
provisions: When a federal agency proposes a new rule, it must include indirect costs the rule could place on small businesses, not just direct costs.
If an agency says a rule will not significantly affect small businesses, it must tell the Office of Advocacy within 10 days.
Small businesses can file a petition asking the Office of Advocacy to review that decision.
If the Office of Advocacy reviews the petition and finds the rule does affect many small businesses, the agency must do a full cost study.
This cost study must be completed before the rule takes effect.
If the agency does not take part in that review, the rule will not apply to small businesses.
For rules that could significantly affect many small businesses, agencies must publish their policy guides and allow public comments.

118-hr-8446.one_liner: Require the government's mineral list to match the energy department's materials list
provisions: The U.S. Geological Survey keeps a list of minerals important to the country's security and economy.
The Department of Energy keeps a separate list of materials important for energy.
Right now, these two lists do not have to match.
This bill requires the USGS to add any material from the Energy Department's list to its own list.
When the Energy Department adds a new material to its list, the USGS has 45 days to add it to the USGS list.

118-hr-8219.one_liner: Study whether Lahaina, Hawaii should become a National Heritage Area
provisions: Tells the National Park Service to look into whether Lahaina, Maui should be named a National Heritage Area
The study would check if Lahaina meets the standards for that status under a federal law called the National Heritage Areas Act
No money is spent or land changed until the study is done and Congress acts on its findings

118-hr-8368.one_liner: Create a coordinator to help Afghan allies, U.S. citizens, and green card holders leave Afghanistan
provisions: The State Department must hire an official called the Coordinator for Afghan Relocation Efforts to run these programs.
The coordinator moves and resettles Afghan allies who meet the requirements to come to the U.S.
The coordinator helps U.S. citizens and green card holders who ask for help leaving Afghanistan.
The coordinator makes sure all parts of the federal government work together on these efforts.
The coordinator can hire temporary workers and sign service contracts, and can extend and keep active contracts that were already in place.
This program lasts for three years after the law passes.

118-hr-8790.one_liner: Set new rules for managing federal forests to reduce wildfire risk
provisions: Groups high-risk federal forest areas into zones called 'firesheds' and tracks them on a public website with maps and data
Creates a new joint center between the U.S. Forest Service and U.S. Geological Survey to track and predict wildfires
Cuts the environmental review steps required before starting certain forest management projects
Skips environmental review entirely for some forest activities
Creates small teams inside agencies to speed up approvals for forest projects
Limits how much courts can do when people sue over forest management decisions in these fire-risk zones
Funds projects to restore forests, reduce fire risk near neighborhoods, and test new technologies to fight wildfires

118-hr-8371.one_liner: Expand healthcare, housing, and benefits for veterans and their families
provisions: Lets veterans see doctors outside the VA system and protects the agreements those doctors make with veterans
Raises the spending limit on home care options so more veterans can get care at home instead of a nursing home
Gives more support to family members who are the main caregivers for veterans with serious injuries or illness
Removes the deadline on college scholarship money for surviving spouses of service members killed in the line of duty
Lets Native American veterans refinance their home loans through a VA program they previously could not use for that purpose
Pays burial and funeral costs for veterans who die in hospice care at home, if they came to hospice directly from a VA hospital or nursing home
Temporarily raises the daily payment rate the VA gives to shelters and housing programs that serve homeless veterans
Starts a program to update the VA's electronic health record system

118-hr-9598.one_liner: Keep the federal drug control office and its programs running through 2031
provisions: Keeps the Office of National Drug Control Policy running with its current powers through 2031.
Continues funding for the High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas program, which gives money and resources to local law enforcement in areas with high drug activity.
Continues the Drug-Free Communities program, which gives grants to local groups working to reduce drug use among young people.
Continues the Drug Court Training program, which helps courts that send people with drug offenses to treatment instead of jail.
Continues the National Community Anti-Drug Coalition Institute, which trains and supports local groups fighting drug use.

118-hr-9106.one_liner: Require equal Secret Service protection staffing for presidents, vice presidents, and major candidates
provisions: The Secret Service must use the same rules to decide how many agents protect the President, Vice President, and major candidates for those offices.
Right now, the number of agents assigned can differ between those groups — this bill removes that difference.
The Department of Homeland Security decides who counts as a major candidate after talking with a committee of congressional leaders.

118-hr-9495.one_liner: Delay tax deadlines for hostage Americans and remove tax breaks for terrorism-supporting groups
provisions: Americans held hostage or wrongfully detained in another country get more time to file their taxes.
Their spouses also get the same extra time to file.
If a detained American already paid tax fines during the time they were held, the government refunds that money.
Groups that give money or other support to terrorist organizations lose their tax-free status.

118-hr-8932.one_liner: Require the student financial aid application to open by October 1 each year
provisions: The FAFSA — the form students fill out to apply for federal college money — must open every year by October 1.
Right now, the law says the FAFSA must open by January 1, with October 1 as a goal but not a hard deadline.
This bill makes October 1 a firm deadline that the Department of Education must meet every year.
Opening the FAFSA earlier gives students and families more time to compare college costs before application deadlines.

118-hr-8958.one_liner: Keep NASA funded and running through 2025 while adding new space and science rules
provisions: NASA keeps its funding for all of its programs through September 2025.
NASA continues working toward landing people on the Moon and eventually sending people to Mars, with help from private space companies.
Private companies can fly their own missions to the International Space Station.
When the International Space Station is eventually retired, NASA must partner with a private company to safely bring it out of orbit and dispose of it.
NASA must test how well satellites can detect greenhouse gases from space.
NASA must share Earth science data — like weather and land information — with farmers and the agriculture industry.
NASA must keep researching drones and high-speed experimental aircraft.

118-hr-9600.one_liner: Name a post office in Plains, Georgia after Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter
provisions: The post office at 119 Main Street in Plains, Georgia will be officially called the "Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter Post Office."
This bill only changes the name of the building — it does not change postal services, hours, or anything else at that location.
Jimmy Carter was the 39th President of the United States, serving from 1977 to 1981. He was born and raised in Plains, Georgia.
Rosalynn Carter served as First Lady from 1977 to 1981. She died in November 2023, and Jimmy Carter died in December 2024.
Plains, Georgia is a small town of about 700 people where both Jimmy and Rosalynn Carter were born and spent most of their lives.

118-hr-9668.one_liner: Create a DHS team to study and counter security threats from China's government
provisions: Sets up a team inside the Department of Homeland Security to look at security threats from China's government
The team studies terrorist threats, cybersecurity threats, border and port security threats, and transportation security threats
The team must find gaps in how the U.S. is responding to these threats and report its findings to Congress every year
The Department of Homeland Security must also research and build new tools to detect and respond to these threats
A government watchdog office reviews how well the program is working and reports back to Congress
The team and its work end seven years after it is set up

118-hres-1449.one_liner: Condemn the rise of antisemitism and call on countries to fight it
provisions: States that antisemitism has grown around the world
Calls on countries and international groups to take steps to fight antisemitism
Supports a set of global guidelines launched in July 2024 that countries can use to track and address antisemitism

118-hres-1469.one_liner: Condemn Biden, Harris, and 13 others for their roles in the Afghanistan withdrawal
provisions: The House formally condemns President Biden and Vice President Harris for decisions made during the 2021 withdrawal from Afghanistan
The resolution also condemns 13 other named officials for their roles in planning and carrying out the withdrawal
No new laws or rules are created — this is a formal statement of disapproval by the House

118-hr-9716.one_liner: Require the government's budget office to publish more frequent spending forecasts
provisions: The Congressional Budget Office must publish at least two budget forecasts each year, instead of just one
At least one of those forecasts must include the economic data used to build it
The President must send detailed budget numbers to Congress by February 1 each year, instead of bundling that data into the full budget request later in the year

118-hres-1568.one_liner: Set House debate rules for bills on FAFSA, geothermal drilling, and critical minerals
provisions: This bill sets the terms for the House to debate and vote on three separate bills.
One bill would move the FAFSA college financial aid application window to an earlier date each year, so students get aid decisions sooner.
One bill would remove the requirement for a federal drilling permit for some geothermal energy projects on federal land.
That same bill would remove the requirement for an environmental review for those geothermal projects.
One bill would add a category called 'critical materials' to the government's official list of essential minerals.

118-hres-1486.one_liner: Set floor debate rules for five measures on China, crime, forests, Afghanistan, and witness rules
provisions: This resolution sets the rules for how the House debates and votes on five separate measures.
One measure puts financial penalties on members of China's ruling Communist Party.
One bill lets local governments use federal crime grant money to build public safety reporting systems.
One bill speeds up government review of forest projects on national forests, federal land, and tribal land.
One measure calls for an investigation into Biden-Harris administration officials over decisions made during the U.S. withdrawal from Afghanistan.
One change updates House rules to let witnesses appear by video during official proceedings.

118-hres-1576.one_liner: Set House debate rules for two bills on geothermal leasing and taxes
provisions: Sets the debate rules for the House to consider these two bills together under one process.
The first bill makes the government hold geothermal energy lease sales more often.
The first bill requires a new lease sale to be scheduled if one is canceled.
The second bill lets Americans who are held hostage or wrongfully detained abroad skip tax deadlines without penalty.
The second bill pays back any late tax fees those detained Americans already paid.
The second bill lets the government remove the tax-free status of groups found to support terrorism.

118-hres-1608.one_liner: Release the House Ethics Committee's report on Matt Gaetz to the public
provisions: The House Ethics Committee looked into allegations against Matt Gaetz, who was a member of Congress from Florida until late 2024.
The committee finished its report but never released it to the public.
This bill tells the Ethics Committee to make that report available for anyone to read.
The report covers the committee's findings from its investigation into Gaetz.

118-hres-1602.one_liner: Schedule House floor votes on two bills about civic education and small business rules
provisions: Sets up a House floor vote on a bill that would create a civic education program about certain political ideologies
Sets up a House floor vote on a bill that would require the federal government to share more information when new rules affect small businesses
This is a procedural step — it does not pass either bill, it just allows the House to debate and vote on them

118-s-3613.one_liner: Require federal building security committees to respond to security recommendations
provisions: When the Federal Protective Service sends a security recommendation to a building's security committee, that committee has 90 days to say yes or no.
If the committee says no, it must explain to the Department of Homeland Security why it is willing to accept the risk.
DHS must create a system to track all recommendations and responses.
DHS must also take steps to make sure committees follow through on responding.
DHS must report to Congress 270 days after this bill passes, and every year after that, on how committees are responding to recommendations.

118-hres-915.one_liner: Ask Ukraine to resume letting Americans adopt Ukrainian children
provisions: Ukraine stopped allowing non-Ukrainians to adopt children on March 13, 2022.
This resolution asks Ukraine to first look at cases where American families already finished the adoption process and got approved before that date.
It also asks Ukraine to let American families who had a Ukrainian child stay with them through a hosting program start the full adoption process.
It asks Ukraine to let those same families apply to take in Ukrainian children who are in legal limbo about whether they can be adopted.

118-hres-1609.one_liner: Release House Ethics Committee records on Matt Gaetz's alleged misconduct
provisions: The House Ethics Committee must keep all records from its review of Matt Gaetz, who served as a U.S. Representative from Florida.
The Committee must make those records available to the public.
The records cover the time Gaetz served as a Member of the House of Representatives.

118-hres-1612.one_liner: Set the debate rules for three bills on energy standards, judges, and wildlife
provisions: Lets the House debate and vote on a bill that stops the Energy Department from setting efficiency rules for clothes washers unless those rules are cost-effective and technically possible
Lets the House debate and vote on a bill that adds more judges to federal district courts and makes some temporary judge positions permanent
Lets the House debate and vote on a bill that renews government programs that protect wildlife habitats and fund conservation work
Does not change any law on its own — it only controls how and when the House can debate these three bills

118-s-2228.one_liner: Speed up environmental reviews for microchip factory projects that get federal funding
provisions: Some microchip factory projects that get federal money no longer need an environmental review before they can be built.
The Department of Commerce takes the lead on environmental reviews for chip projects that still require one.
Each chip factory project gets one combined review document instead of separate ones from multiple agencies.
States can choose to run the environmental review for chip factory projects themselves instead of the federal government doing it.
People who want to challenge a chip project in court over environmental review have a set deadline to file their lawsuit.

119-hr-6422.one_liner: Renew funding for five federal water programs protecting lakes, coastlines, and waterways through 2031
provisions: Keeps five federal water protection programs running through 2031, including programs for the Great Lakes, Long Island Sound, Columbia River, and coastal beaches.
Adds the Mississippi Sound to a list of nationally important water areas that can receive federal support.
Lets states and local governments use federal beach grants to track down where water pollution is coming from.
Makes federal agencies able to apply for grants under the San Francisco Estuary Partnership program.
Stops Clean Water Act grant money from going to groups based in or connected to countries the U.S. considers a security risk.
Has a government watchdog office review how well the EPA's regional water programs are working.

118-s-3764.one_liner: Keep a federal commission running that tracks threats to religious freedom around the world
provisions: The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom gets funding and legal backing to keep running through the year starting October 2025.
The commission tracks countries and situations where people cannot practice their religion freely.
It reviews how the U.S. government responds to these situations and recommends changes to policy.

119-hr-5103.one_liner: Set up a federal commission and cleaning program for Washington D.C.
provisions: Creates a federal commission made up of officials from U.S. Attorneys' Offices in Washington D.C., Maryland, and Virginia, plus other federal agencies.
The commission gives recommendations on enforcing federal immigration laws inside Washington D.C.
The commission works to bring in federal resources to lower crime in D.C. and helps recruit and keep more officers in the D.C. Metropolitan Police Department.
The Department of the Interior runs a program to clean and take care of monuments, parks, and roads in D.C. that many people visit.
The program also repairs or puts back federal monuments and similar properties that have been damaged or removed.
All parts of this bill end on January 2, 2029.

118-s-709.one_liner: Require federal agencies to check and report their progress on goals each year
provisions: Each federal agency must review its progress on every goal it has set at least once a year.
Agencies must find and list problems that could stop them from reaching their goals.
For goals most at risk of being missed, agencies must come up with a plan to get back on track.
Each agency must appoint a Deputy Performance Improvement Officer to help run these reviews.
The government's top priority goals must be updated during the first year of each new presidential term.
Each top priority goal must include a plan to complete it within one four-year presidential term.
Each top priority goal must point to the specific parts of the federal budget that pay for it.

118-s-3791.one_liner: Extend and update wildlife and conservation programs through 2030
provisions: Keeps several wildlife and conservation programs running through the year starting October 2029, including programs for wetlands, fish habitat, and the Chesapeake Bay
Extends a program that tracks and manages Chronic Wasting Disease, a sickness that spreads among deer and elk
Lets one government group per state get a permit to protect farm animals from black vulture attacks
Funds the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to finish a national survey of fish habitats and build a database to track the results
Keeps a rule in place through 2030 that stops the EPA from adding rules about lead in sport fishing gear

119-hres-1128.one_liner: Express House support for keeping the Department of Homeland Security funded
provisions: The House says it supports giving the Department of Homeland Security enough money to keep running
The House says Americans face more risk every day that DHS runs out of money and has to pause its work
The House thanks DHS employees for their work protecting the country

119-hres-1131.one_liner: Set the rules for debating four bills in the House
provisions: Sets the time and rules for how the House will debate a bill to fund the Department of Homeland Security for the year ending September 30, 2026
Sets the rules for debating a statement of support for the Department of Homeland Security
Sets the rules for debating a bill to create a program to clean up and improve Washington D.C.
Sets the rules for debating a bill about which ships can use U.S. waterways and ports

119-hres-1142.one_liner: Set the rules for how Congress handles Senate changes to a government spending bill
provisions: This is a procedural step that decides what happens to changes the Senate made to a spending bill called H.R. 7147.
H.R. 7147 funds many parts of the federal government through September 30, 2026.
This resolution tells the House how to respond — whether to accept, reject, or negotiate the Senate's changes.
No new spending or policy changes are made by this resolution itself.

119-hr-8029.one_liner: Fund the Department of Homeland Security and end its partial shutdown
provisions: The Department of Homeland Security ran out of money on February 14, 2026, and this bill gives it funding to keep running for the rest of the year.
Agencies that get funded include Border Patrol, ICE, TSA, the Coast Guard, and the Secret Service.
FEMA and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency also get money to keep operating.
Federal workers who missed paychecks during the shutdown get their back pay.
Costs the government took on during the shutdown to protect people and property are approved as valid.

119-hr-7084.one_liner: Block ships from US ports if they called at a port taken from American owners
provisions: The President can block ships from US ports if those ships stopped at an American-owned port that was seized by another government.
The rule only applies to ports seized by countries in the Western Hemisphere that have a trade deal with the US.
The block can be lifted when the country returns the property, pays the US owner, or both sides reach an agreement.
Ships in an emergency can still enter US ports even if they are otherwise blocked.
A ship can also enter if the American who owned the seized port gave it permission to use the facility.

117-hconres-45.one_liner: Call on Serbia to prosecute those responsible for killing three American brothers
provisions: Three American brothers — Ylli, Agron, and Mehmet Bytyqi — were killed in Serbia in July 1999.
Congress states that the people responsible for those killings should be prosecuted.
Congress states that the U.S. should put enough money and staff toward watching and supporting Serbia's investigation.
This resolution does not create a law or require any action — it states Congress's position.

117-hconres-59.one_liner: Condemn the 2021 military takeover in Sudan and call for return to civilian rule
provisions: States that Congress does not support the October 25, 2021 military takeover of Sudan's government.
Calls on Sudan's military leaders to free all government officials and civilians they arrested during the takeover.
Calls on Sudan's military to restore the civilian-led government and constitution that was in place before the coup.
Calls on Sudan's military to end the state of emergency and turn communications back on.
Calls on other countries to join the U.S. in placing targeted sanctions on Sudan's military leaders.
Calls on international groups to suspend Sudan from regional organizations until civilian rule is restored.

117-hr-1456.one_liner: Extend Peace Corps funding and expand benefits and protections for volunteers
provisions: Keeps the Peace Corps funded through September 2025
Raises the payment volunteers get when their service ends
Lets returned volunteers apply for federal jobs without going through the standard hiring process
Gives returned volunteers three months of health coverage at no cost after service ends, with an option to pay for three more months at their own cost
Requires the Peace Corps to provide mental health care to volunteers during and after service, and to supply period products
Lets volunteers who had to leave early through no fault of their own re-enroll faster
Expands protections for volunteers who report problems or wrongdoing, and raises the pay rate used to calculate workers compensation claims

117-hr-1066.one_liner: Set the federal government's share of wildfire aid at 75% or more
provisions: The federal government must pay at least 75% of the cost of wildfire emergency grants, called Fire Management Assistance Grants.
FEMA must create new rules that set clear levels of fire damage that would allow the federal share to go above 75%.
The rules must use a measurement specific to fire damage — not general disaster damage — to decide when to increase federal funding.

117-hr-1808.one_liner: Make it a federal crime to buy, sell, make, or own certain semi-automatic guns and large magazines
provisions: Makes it a crime to buy, sell, make, or own certain semi-automatic guns and magazines that hold large numbers of bullets.
Bolt-action, pump-action, lever-action, and slide-action guns are not covered by this rule, nor are antiques or guns that no longer work.
Active police, certain government workers, and retired police officers can still own these guns and magazines.
People who already own these guns can keep them but must store them safely, and a background check is required before selling or giving one to someone else.
People who already own large magazines can keep them but cannot sell or give them to anyone else.
New large magazines must have a serial number, and new guns and magazines covered by this rule must display the year they were made.
Cities and states can use federal grant money from the Byrne Justice Assistance program to pay people who turn in these guns or magazines voluntarily.

117-hr-2250.one_liner: Set new rules for how the VA manages its technology projects and spending
provisions: The VA cannot spend money on any new major tech project unless it first submits a report covering the project's cost, timeline, and goals.
That report becomes the baseline — the VA must track and report any changes against it throughout the life of the project.
Each project must be run by a team that includes a certified project manager, a technical lead, a functional lead, and a contracting officer.
The VA's top tech official must take direct control over the technology staff and contractors at the VA's Financial Services Center.
The VA must review all of its tech investments to decide which ones could move to cloud computing.

117-hr-263.one_liner: Limit who can own or touch big cats like lions and tigers
provisions: Makes it illegal for most private owners to get new big cats, including lions, tigers, leopards, cheetahs, jaguars, and cougars.
People who already own big cats can keep them but cannot breed them or get more.
Stops members of the public from touching or petting big cats at zoos, circuses, or other exhibits.
Only licensed facilities like accredited zoos can keep big cats under the new rules.

117-hr-2521.one_liner: Start a VA pilot program to provide doula support to pregnant veterans
provisions: The VA will run a 5-year test program to offer doula services to pregnant veterans already enrolled in VA health care.
Doulas are trained support people who help women before, during, and after childbirth.
The program will track how doula support affects birth outcomes and mental health for pregnant veterans.
Services will be provided through outside organizations that work with the VA.

117-hr-203.one_liner: Name a Houston post office building after Benny C. Martinez
provisions: The post office at 4020 Broadway Street in Houston, Texas will officially be called the 'Benny C. Martinez Post Office Building'.
The name applies to the building only — mail delivery, services, and daily operations at that location stay the same.
The bill honors Benny C. Martinez by giving his name to this Houston post office as a form of public recognition.
No federal money is spent and no laws or rules change as a result of this bill.

117-hr-1934.one_liner: Create a government team to boost U.S. influence in global 5G technology rule-making
provisions: Creates a group of federal agencies working together to shape international rules for 5G wireless technology
The group works to get U.S. allies and private companies more involved in setting those rules
Reports to Congress on plans for working with other countries to share safety information about 5G
Reports to Congress on what China is doing in international 5G rule-setting groups

117-hr-3588.one_liner: Fund grants to colleges and nonprofits for math modeling research in K-12 schools
provisions: The National Science Foundation must create a program to give grants to colleges and nonprofits for research on math and statistics teaching in public K-12 schools.
The grants will support teaching areas like data science and how to use math to solve real-world problems.
The National Science Foundation must try to set up a study with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine on how math and statistics modeling is taught in schools.
The study will produce a report on what is working and what is not in math modeling education.

117-hr-3372.one_liner: Fund community centers and hotlines to help people leaving prison
provisions: Lets the Department of Justice give money to community nonprofits to open reentry centers for people coming out of prison
Lets the Department of Justice give money to states, tribes, and local governments to run phone hotlines that connect people leaving prison to services in their community

117-hr-3482.one_liner: Create a national center to support aviation education and job training
provisions: Creates a new group called the National Center for the Advancement of Aviation to connect schools, businesses, and government agencies in the aviation field.
The center will help develop school lessons and training programs for aviation and aerospace jobs.
It will help military veterans move into civilian aviation or aerospace careers through outreach and apprenticeships.
It will collect and store public data on aviation safety, jobs, and research in one place.
It will host events and conferences where people from different parts of the aviation world can share ideas.
It can give grants — money with no payback required — to schools and training programs that teach aviation, including high schools and trade schools.

117-hr-2988.one_liner: Strengthen protections for federal workers who report government problems to Congress
provisions: Federal workers are protected from job punishment if they report problems to Congress.
The President, members of Congress, military members, and other federal workers cannot block an employee's right to report to Congress.
Workers cannot reveal a whistleblower's name to people outside the government.
Workers who face job punishment can ask a government board to fix it.
If the board does not decide within 180 days, workers can take the case to court.
Workers can now report problems to a supervisor in their chain of command as a protected action.
Job suspensions of 1 to 13 days not caused by budget gaps, and suspensions of 14 to 29 days, can now be appealed.

117-hr-302.one_liner: Stop agencies from moving federal workers into a less-protected job category
provisions: This bill stops federal agencies from moving jobs out of the standard federal hiring system into separate, less-protected categories.
It makes it illegal to create any new job categories beyond the ones already in federal hiring rules as of September 30, 2020.
A 2020 executive order had created a new category called Schedule F, covering federal workers whose jobs involve setting or advising on government policy.
Workers placed in Schedule F lose the job protections that most federal employees have.
Reports at the time estimated around 50,000 federal workers could have been moved into Schedule F under the 2020 order.

117-hr-3630.one_liner: Add Medicare coverage for compression garments that treat lymphedema
provisions: Medicare would start covering compression sleeves, stockings, and wraps prescribed to treat lymphedema.
Lymphedema is a condition where fluid builds up and causes swelling, usually in the arms or legs.
Items must be prescribed by a health care provider, such as a doctor, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.
Coverage includes both standard sizes and custom-fitted garments made to fit a specific patient.
Other devices that help prevent or treat lymphedema could also be covered if found to work.

117-hr-3771.one_liner: Direct CDC to give states grants for heart disease awareness in high-risk communities
provisions: Requires the CDC to give money to states to run heart disease awareness programs.
States can use the money to create educational materials and research collections about heart disease.
The program focuses on South Asian people in the U.S., who face heart disease more often than many other groups.
Other groups that face heart disease more often than average are also covered by the program.
Research and awareness efforts include how type 2 diabetes connects to heart disease in these communities.

117-hr-4040.one_liner: Make COVID-era telehealth rules permanent for Medicare patients
provisions: Medicare patients can get telehealth visits from anywhere, not just rural areas or approved locations.
Community health centers and rural clinics can be the location where a doctor connects with a patient over video or phone.
Any type of Medicare-approved medical provider can offer telehealth visits, not just certain specialists.
Patients can have audio-only phone appointments for general care and mental health services, without needing a camera or video connection.

117-hr-4118.one_liner: Create federal grants and new offices to reduce violence in communities with high homicide rates
provisions: Gives money to local programs that work to stop violence in areas where homicides happen most
Creates a new office inside the Department of Health and Human Services to run these programs
Sets up a group of advisors to help guide how violence reduction programs are run
Creates a national center to train local groups, share research, and track data on violence
Gives job training money to connect young people ages 16 to 24 to jobs in areas hit hard by gun violence

117-hr-3843.one_liner: Change the fees companies pay to the government before completing a merger
provisions: Companies that want to merge must pay a fee to the government before the deal is approved — this bill changes how much that fee is
The fees are based on the size of the deal, with bigger mergers paying more
Each year, the fees go up automatically to keep pace with rising prices

117-hr-4404.one_liner: Add a section of the Kissimmee River in Florida to the national protected rivers list
provisions: A restored section of the Kissimmee River in Florida gets added to the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System, a federal program that protects certain rivers from development.
Rivers in this system cannot have federally funded dams, diversions, or other projects built on them without special approval.
The U.S. government manages the land along the river to keep it in its natural state.

117-hr-4176.one_liner: Require federal surveys to collect data on sexual orientation and gender identity
provisions: Federal agencies that run surveys must check their existing surveys to see which ones do not ask about sexual orientation or gender identity.
Agencies must review how they ask questions about sexual orientation and gender identity and figure out what changes are needed.
Any federal agency that publishes reports using survey data must include sexual orientation and gender identity information in those reports.

117-hr-4785.one_liner: Create a U.S. government position focused on human rights in China's Xinjiang region
provisions: Creates a Special Coordinator for Uyghur Issues job at the State Department to focus on human rights in China's Xinjiang region.
Lets the State Department give money to people who speak at public events about the rights of Uyghurs and other minority groups in Xinjiang.
Requires the State Department to make Uyghur language classes available to U.S. diplomats.
Requires the State Department to place at least one Uyghur-speaking diplomat at U.S. offices in China.

117-hr-5118.one_liner: Finish buying land to complete the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail by 2028
provisions: The Forest Service must finish buying all land needed for the Continental Divide Trail by November 10, 2028.
The Forest Service and the Bureau of Land Management must form a joint team to work on completing the trail.
Within 3 years of passing, the Forest Service must send Congress a plan showing which parts of the trail are still missing.
The plan must include the cost to finish building and protecting each part of the trail.
The government can only buy land from sellers who agree to sell — it cannot force anyone to give up their land.
Both the Forest Service and the Continental Divide Trail Coalition must send Congress yearly updates until the trail is done.

117-hr-521.one_liner: Let injured federal first responders keep their retirement benefits if they move to a different government job
provisions: Federal law enforcement officers, border patrol officers, and firefighters pay more into retirement than other government workers and must retire by age 57.
When one of these workers gets hurt on the job and moves to a different government position to recover, this bill lets them stay in their original retirement plan.
Under current rules, moving to a different government job after an injury can knock them out of the retirement plan they paid into.
If one of these workers leaves government service before they can collect retirement, this bill lets them get back the extra retirement money they paid in.

117-hr-5274.one_liner: Give Customs and Border Protection workers tools and training to avoid fentanyl exposure
provisions: Containment devices are sealed containers or bags used to handle seized drugs safely, without direct skin contact.
Customs and Border Protection must give these sealed devices to all of its officers, agents, and other workers.
CBP must hold training at least once a year on how to use these devices correctly.
The training covers how to avoid accidental contact with fentanyl and other deadly drugs — contact that can happen even without touching the drugs directly.

117-hr-5407.one_liner: Ask colleges to make plans for student mental health and suicide prevention
provisions: Tells the Department of Education to push colleges to create mental health plans for their students
Colleges that follow through would have a written plan for preventing suicide on campus

117-hr-5271.one_liner: Name a Nashville post office after Tennessee state senator Thelma Harper
provisions: The post office at 2245 Rosa L Parks Boulevard in Nashville, Tennessee will be officially named the 'Thelma Harper Post Office Building.'
Thelma Harper served in the Tennessee State Senate from 1990 to 2014, representing parts of Nashville, and was the first Black woman elected to that office.
This is a ceremonial action only — it does not change how the post office runs or spend any government money.

117-hr-5441.one_liner: Tighten rules against painful training methods used on show horses
provisions: Makes it harder to use painful methods on horses' legs to change how they walk or run in shows
Creates a new system for checking horses for signs of pain or injury at shows, sales, and auctions
Raises the fines and punishments for people caught using these painful training methods

117-hr-5315.one_liner: Give grants to governments and colleges to use drones for inspecting roads, power lines, and water systems
provisions: The Department of Transportation gives money to state, local, and tribal governments to buy drones for inspecting roads, power lines, and water systems.
Governments that get the money must use drones made in the United States by companies not owned or controlled by China.
The Department of Transportation also gives money to colleges to train students for jobs that use drones.
The grants cover inspections, repairs, and construction of roads and other public infrastructure.

117-hr-5455.one_liner: Let more people sentenced for crack cocaine ask for shorter prison terms
provisions: Before 2010, courts gave much longer prison sentences for crack cocaine than for powder cocaine.
A 2010 law changed those sentencing rules to treat crack and powder cocaine more equally.
A 2018 law let some people sentenced under the old rules ask a court for a shorter sentence.
In 2021, the Supreme Court ruled that low-level offenders could not use the 2018 law to get a shorter sentence.
This bill lets low-level crack cocaine offenders use the 2018 law to ask for shorter sentences too.

117-hr-5768.one_liner: Fund police and prosecutors to use new technology to solve violent crimes
provisions: The Department of Justice sets up a program to give money to police and prosecutors.
The money goes toward using new technology to help close open violent crime cases.
State, tribal, and local law enforcement agencies can apply for the money, including groups of them working together.
Prosecutors can also apply, alone or with police departments.

117-hr-5585.one_liner: Create a new federal agency to fund high-risk health and medical research
provisions: Creates a new agency inside the Department of Health and Human Services to fund health and medicine research that other agencies won't take on
The agency gets its own separate budget, not shared with the rest of HHS
A director chosen by the President runs the agency and can speak directly to Congress without getting approval from other government officials first
The agency can give out money through grants, contracts, and prize competitions to support research projects
Staff called program managers pick which projects get funded, set goals, and decide whether to keep or stop each project
The agency must work with the FDA and Medicare and Medicaid to speed up the path from new cures to patient coverage
Every year, the agency reports on what it's doing, and the National Academies of Sciences checks whether it's working

117-hr-5774.one_liner: Give FEMA power to build housing for disaster survivors in U.S. territories
provisions: After a major disaster is declared, the President can tell FEMA to pay for things people still need that no other program covers.
FEMA can give money directly to people or families to help them get a place to live.
FEMA can build permanent or semi-permanent homes in U.S. territories like Puerto Rico or the U.S. Virgin Islands.
The President can approve home construction in other locations if it costs less than other housing options.

117-hr-5659.one_liner: Name a post office in Oxnard, California after John R. Hatcher III
provisions: Renames the U.S. Post Office at 1961 North C Street in Oxnard, California to the 'John R. Hatcher III Post Office Building'
No money is spent and no mail service, hours, or staffing rules change as a result of this bill
The post office keeps running exactly as it does today — only the building's official name changes
Congress passes bills like this to give federal buildings official names, often to honor people from a local community
The new name takes effect when the President signs the bill into law

117-hr-6538.one_liner: Create a national alert system to warn the public during active shooter events
provisions: Assigns one person at the Department of Justice to run a national active shooter alert network
That person works with states and tribal governments to build plans for sending out active shooter alerts
Federal, state, local, and tribal agencies are encouraged to set up steps for how to respond when an active shooter is reported
The Government Accountability Office must study how states and local governments respond to active shooters and issue a report on their findings

117-hr-6552.one_liner: Keep funding programs that fight human trafficking in the US and abroad
provisions: Keeps money flowing through 2026 for State Department and Justice Department programs that fight human trafficking in other countries.
Keeps running the Angel Watch Center, a program that warns other countries when a convicted sex offender is about to travel there.
Lets the Department of Health and Human Services run a program to help trafficking survivors get back on their feet and support themselves.

States that get federal money for foster care must stay in contact with police and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children when a child in their care goes missing and may be a trafficking victim.
Requires the Angel Watch Center to get lists from other countries of people who are required to register as sex offenders.
Requires federal workers to book overnight stays at hotels that have policies in place to fight human trafficking.

117-hr-6878.one_liner: Set health and safety rules for pregnant women held in federal prisons
provisions: Federal prisons must provide health care and services to pregnant women and women who recently gave birth
Prisons cannot put pregnant women or new mothers in solitary confinement or use physical restraints on them
A pregnant woman whose baby is due within the last year of her sentence can be released early to home or a halfway house
The government will track how many pregnant women are in federal, state, and local jails and prisons, and what health care they receive
A government watchdog office will study what health services and protections pregnant women get in state and local jails and prisons
States, local governments, tribes, and nonprofits can apply for grants to pay for pregnancy care and women's health services inside jails and prisons

117-hr-6448.one_liner: Give grants to local and tribal police departments with under 200 officers
provisions: Police departments and tribal governments with fewer than 200 officers can apply for a federal grant.
Grant money can be used to buy body cameras for officers.
Departments can use the money to train officers on how to calm down tense situations before they escalate.
Funds can also go toward recruiting new officers and keeping the ones they have.

117-hr-6493.one_liner: Extend and expand college drug and alcohol prevention programs through 2028
provisions: Keeps federal funding for drug and alcohol prevention programs at colleges running through the year starting October 2027.
Expands the program to cover a wider range of substance misuse, not just illegal drugs and alcohol.
Colleges that receive this funding run programs to help students avoid or recover from substance problems.

117-hr-7174.one_liner: Keep funding a Secret Service school that trains police on cybercrime
provisions: Keeps the National Computer Forensics Institute running through 2032
The institute trains police officers and others to investigate cyber crimes and electronic crimes
Adds training on how to prevent cyber crimes, not just investigate them after they happen
Requires the institute to find new ways to investigate cyber crimes
Requires the institute to send a yearly report on what it has done

117-hr-6929.one_liner: Restore full pension payments for Delphi Corporation workers whose benefits were cut in 2009
provisions: Workers who had pensions through Delphi Corporation, which went bankrupt in 2009, had their monthly payments cut. This bill restores those payments to the full amount.
The federal pension agency (PBGC) must recalculate each worker's monthly pension payment.
The PBGC must also go back and recalculate all past payments already made.
Workers get a one-time lump-sum check to make up for any money they were underpaid in past months.
The government sets up a fund and puts money into it to cover these payments.
The bill sets rules for how the lump-sum payments are taxed.

117-hr-6965.one_liner: Create a 10-year federal plan to bring more international tourists to the United States
provisions: The Department of Commerce must write a 10-year plan for U.S. travel and tourism, with yearly goals for how many international visitors come to the U.S. and how much money those visitors spend here.
The bill creates a new government position — Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Travel and Tourism — to lead that plan.
That official must set yearly visitor goals, work to speed up visa approvals for people who want to visit the U.S., and promote U.S. travel and tourism to people in other countries.
The new official must also write and carry out a plan to help the U.S. travel and tourism industry recover from the COVID-19 pandemic.
A group called the United States Travel and Tourism Advisory Board gets a formal legal role helping the new official carry out the COVID-19 recovery plan.

117-hr-7180.one_liner: Fund research on how COVID-19 affects the brain and thinking
provisions: The National Science Foundation will give out grants to researchers studying how COVID-19 affects thinking and memory, both short-term and long-term.
The research includes how COVID-19 affects children and teenagers.
Within 45 days of passing, the National Science Foundation must work with the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to produce a report on how COVID-19 disrupts brain function.

117-hr-7025.one_liner: Stop U.S. wildlife money from going to foreign military units that abuse human rights
provisions: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service must check that the foreign groups it sends money to are not paying or supporting military or police units accused of serious human rights abuses.
Before giving out grants, the agency must run background checks on the groups that will receive the money.
Groups getting money must share financial records and follow a safety plan to make sure funds don't reach abusive units.
The agency must post a public list of military and police units that are banned from getting this money.
The agency must work with the State Department to screen groups before sending funds.
The ban can be lifted if the foreign government is taking real steps to punish the people responsible and stop future abuses.
Grants must go through regular audits to confirm the money is being used correctly.

117-hr-7321.one_liner: Set new safety inspection and worker rules for foreign aircraft repair shops
provisions: Requires every foreign aircraft repair shop to get at least one surprise inspection per year from the FAA
Requires airlines to send the FAA a report every month about any work done on their planes
Sets minimum job requirements that mechanics and other workers must meet before working on U.S. planes at foreign repair shops
Stops the FAA from approving any new foreign repair shops if certain safety rules are not put in place within one year

117-hr-7693.one_liner: Keep the National Park Foundation running through 2030
provisions: Lets the National Park Foundation keep operating and receiving money through the year ending September 2030
The National Park Foundation raises private money to support national parks across the United States

117-hr-7283.one_liner: Let states use mine cleanup funds to treat acidic water from old coal mines
provisions: States can use up to 30% of their federal mine cleanup money to treat acidic water flowing out of abandoned coal mines.
The money comes from grants already set up under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.
Acid mine drainage is water that turns toxic after mixing with rocks and minerals exposed in old coal mines.

117-hr-7337.one_liner: Require the National Archives to submit a plan for clearing veteran record request backlogs
provisions: The National Personnel Records Center holds service records for veterans, but requests have piled up in a backlog.
The head of the National Archives must send Congress a plan to clear that backlog.
The plan must include deadlines for when the backlog will be reduced.
The plan must describe steps to upgrade computer systems to stop backlogs from building up again.
The plan must also include steps to improve service for people waiting on their requests.

117-hr-7289.one_liner: Order studies on PFAS chemicals in the environment and human body
provisions: Tells the EPA to work with a national science group to study how people are exposed to PFAS chemicals and how dangerous they are.
Tells the EPA to work with that same science group to study how PFAS spreads in the environment and how to clean it up.
Tells the White House science office to write a plan for how the federal government will research PFAS based on what the studies find.
PFAS are man-made chemicals found in nonstick pans, waterproof clothing, and other products that may cause health problems.

117-hr-7900.one_liner: Fund the U.S. military and set troop and equipment levels for 2023
provisions: Pays the salaries and training costs for U.S. military troops for the year starting October 2022.
Sets aside money for research and testing of new military technology and weapons systems.
Pays for aircraft — such as planes and helicopters — for the U.S. military.
Pays for missiles and ammunition to stock U.S. military supplies.
Sets the maximum number of troops allowed to serve in each branch of the military during 2023.

117-hr-7780.one_liner: Add mental health workers in schools and change employer health plan rules
provisions: Creates grants to put more mental health counselors and therapists in public schools
Colleges must follow new rules for supporting students with disabilities
Stops employers from requiring workers to use private arbitration instead of courts when disputing health benefit decisions
Stops employers from including clauses in health plans that let the employer make the final call on all benefit disputes

117-hr-7734.one_liner: Require Treasury to share bank financial crime reports with Congress within 30 days
provisions: The Treasury Department must give Congress any Bank Secrecy Act report within 30 days of being asked for it.
Banks must hand over these reports to a congressional committee if Congress issues a subpoena.
Bank Secrecy Act reports track suspicious money activity, like possible money laundering, that banks are required to flag.

117-hr-8296.one_liner: Stop governments from restricting access to abortion services or who provides them
provisions: Stops state and federal governments from passing laws that limit access to abortion services.
Lets providers prescribe drugs used for abortion — such as medication abortion pills — and offer abortion services through telemedicine, without added government restrictions.
Stops governments from requiring providers to delay care when the provider decides a delay puts the patient's health at risk.

Stops governments from requiring providers to do medical procedures patients do not need, share medical information that is not accurate, or meet certification or licensing requirements that do not apply to other providers who perform similar procedures.
Patients do not have to make extra in-person visits or explain their reasons before getting an abortion.
Abortion cannot be banned before a fetus can survive outside the womb; after that point, it must still be allowed if the provider decides the pregnancy risks the patient's life or health.
The Department of Justice, individual patients, and healthcare providers can all sue to enforce this law, and states can be taken to court for violations.

117-hr-8294.one_liner: Fund federal transportation and housing agencies for the year starting October 2022
provisions: Gives money to the Department of Transportation to run programs covering roads, highways, airlines, railroads, and public transit for the year starting October 2022.
Gives money to the Department of Housing and Urban Development for public housing, home loan programs, and efforts to reduce homelessness.
Funds the office that enforces fair housing rules, which bar landlords and sellers from turning away people based on race, religion, or other protected traits.
Funds a program that finds and removes lead paint hazards in homes, which can harm young children.
Funds safety offices at the Federal Aviation Administration and Federal Railroad Administration, which inspect planes and trains.
Funds Amtrak's inspector general, who checks whether Amtrak spends its money correctly.
Sets rules on how all the money in this bill can and cannot be spent.

117-hr-8373.one_liner: Protect the legal right to access and provide contraception
provisions: Makes it illegal for any law or government action to block or single out people from getting contraception
Protects doctors and other health care workers who provide contraception from being penalized
Covers birth control devices, medications, sterilization procedures, and fertility-awareness methods
Lets the Department of Justice, patients, or health care providers sue in court if this law is broken
States cannot claim they are immune from being sued under this law

117-hr-8351.one_liner: Remove import taxes on baby formula through the end of 2022
provisions: Removes all import taxes and fees on baby formula from the date this passes through December 31, 2022.
During that time, baby formula coming into the country will not face any extra charges, quotas, or limits at the border.
Companies bringing in baby formula must list the correct tariff code on their customs paperwork.

117-hr-8297.one_liner: Block states from punishing people who get or help with abortions in other states
provisions: States cannot use their laws to stop someone from going to another state to get an abortion.
States cannot punish doctors or clinics in other states for providing abortion care to patients who traveled there.
States cannot punish people who help doctors or clinics provide abortion care to patients from other states.
States cannot punish people or groups who help someone travel to another state for abortion care.
States cannot block abortion pills from being shipped across state lines.
The U.S. Justice Department can go to court to stop anyone using state law to block this.
People who are blocked from getting this care can also take whoever blocked them to court.

117-hr-8446.one_liner: Keep funding a U.S. program that fights hunger in other countries through 2028
provisions: Continues U.S. government funding for a global food and nutrition program through 2028.
Adds a new rule requiring the program to look for ways to make farming more efficient and sustainable.
Continues funding for a separate program that helps people in other countries buy food in local markets through 2028.

117-hr-8326.one_liner: Set new rules for what questions the Census Bureau can add to the census
provisions: The head of the Census Bureau can only be fired if there is a specific proven reason — not just because the President wants to.
The Census Bureau cannot add a new question or topic to the census unless it first notifies Congress.
Every two years, the Census Bureau must send Congress a progress report on how it is planning for the next national population count.
Before adding a question that did not appear on the last two censuses, the Census Bureau must show that it researched and tested that question.
A federal watchdog office checks whether new census questions were properly researched and tested, then sends a report to Congress with its findings.

117-hr-8466.one_liner: Require federal agencies to post workplace safety plans during public health emergencies
provisions: Each federal agency must post a safety plan on its website.
The plan applies during a nationwide public health emergency for an infectious disease.
The plan must describe what protective equipment workers get and how testing works for people who come into the office.
It must also cover cleaning schedules and how many people can be in the building.
Workers who have to travel off-site for their job must also be covered by the plan.
New employees and contractors must receive the plan within 30 days of being hired or starting a contract.
Each agency's internal watchdog office must report on whether the agency published and followed its plan.

117-hr-8542.one_liner: Create grants to send mental health workers to emergencies instead of police
provisions: Creates a program that trains and sends mental health workers to respond to emergencies instead of police.
States, tribes, and local governments can apply for grants to start these programs.
A federal health agency called SAMHSA runs the program.
SAMHSA can take back grant money if a program leads to more people being jailed or sent to institutions.
The federal government checks whether the program is working.

117-hr-884.one_liner: Require a federal plan for disease outbreaks in air travel
provisions: Tells the Department of Transportation to write a plan for how airports and airlines should handle disease outbreaks
The plan must require that airline workers who deal with the public have the right protective gear during a disease outbreak
Airlines and airline workers must be consulted when the plan is written
A government watchdog group called the Government Accountability Office must review the plan and report on whether it is working

117-hr-8463.one_liner: Expand which countries can apply for U.S. development aid
provisions: Right now, only countries ranked among the 75 poorest in the world can apply for aid from the Millennium Challenge Corporation.
This bill raises that limit so countries ranked up to 125th poorest can apply.
The World Bank's yearly income rankings decide which countries qualify.

117-hr-8454.one_liner: Set up a new DEA sign-up process for medical marijuana and CBD research
provisions: Creates a separate sign-up process through the Drug Enforcement Administration so doctors and researchers can get permission to study marijuana
Lets registered colleges, doctors, and drug makers handle marijuana and CBD for medical research
Lets companies get DEA permission to produce drugs that contain marijuana or CBD once those drugs are approved for sale
Requires the DEA to check whether there is enough marijuana available so research is never stopped by a shortage
Brings back open access for marijuana research by blocking the Department of Health and Human Services from restoring an old review process that slowed approvals
Lets doctors talk openly with patients about what marijuana and CBD might do to them
Requires a government report on whether marijuana could treat conditions like epilepsy, what it does to teenage brains, and how it affects driving

117-hr-8888.one_liner: Create a new VA office to help veterans get food assistance
provisions: Creates a new office inside the Department of Veterans Affairs focused on food assistance for veterans
The office gives veterans information about which food assistance programs they can apply for
The office creates rules to find veterans who do not have enough food and connect them with help
